==> ./tools/place_check.py <==
"""Live placement check for one layout of the capture plans (docs/capture_plan_v2.json, docs/capture_plan_v3.json),
then the capture.

Reads the boxes and the robots from OptiTrack twice a second and prints, for every target of the layout,
how far the nearest box (and, in the random family, the nearest robot) is and in which direction to move
it. Boxes are matched to targets by the smallest total distance, so any box can go on any target. A box of
the set (rigid bodies 11-17) that is inside the arena but not part of the layout is flagged: take it out.

When everything is within --tolerance, Enter starts the capture: the launch_all command of the layout (the
OptiTrack connection of this script is closed first). Ctrl+C quits without capturing.

    python -m tools.place_check --layout R01
    python -m tools.place_check --layout R01 --no-launch      # only the check
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from itertools import permutations

ALL_BOX_IDS = [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17]
ROBOT_IDS = {"P0": 8, "P1": 7, "P3": 10, "P5": 6}
ARENA = (-2.690, 2.135, -2.672, 1.519)


def match(targets, found):
    """Assignment of found points to targets with the smallest total distance:
    list of (target index, found index or None, distance or None)."""
    idx = list(range(len(found)))
    best = None
    k = min(len(targets), len(found))
    for perm in permutations(idx, k):
        cost = sum(math.hypot(targets[i][0] - found[j][0], targets[i][1] - found[j][1]) for i, j in enumerate(perm))
        if best is None or cost < best[0]:
            best = (cost, perm)
    out = []
    for i in range(len(targets)):
        if best and i < len(best[1]):
            j = best[1][i]
            out.append((i, j, math.hypot(targets[i][0] - found[j][0], targets[i][1] - found[j][1])))
        else:
            out.append((i, None, None))
    return out


def direction(dx, dy):
    """Move hint in Motive axes, cm."""
    return f"move x {100 * dx:+5.0f} cm, y {100 * dy:+5.0f} cm"


def key_pressed():
    if os.name == "nt":
        import msvcrt
        if msvcrt.kbhit():
            return msvcrt.getwch() in ("\r", "\n")
        return False
    import select
    r, _, _ = select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], 0)
    if r:
        sys.stdin.readline()
        return True
    return False


def report(L, hub, tol):
    """Lines to print and whether every target is within tol."""
    lines, ok_all = [], True
    targets = [b[:2] for b in L["boxes"]]
    ids = list(L["box_ids"])
    found, found_ids = [], []
    for rb in ids:
        q = hub.get_pose(rb)
        if q is not None:
            found.append(q[:2])
            found_ids.append(rb)
    lines.append(f"{L['id']}: {L['n_boxes']} boxes, {L['arrangement']}, robots {L['robots']}   (tolerance "
                 f"{100 * tol:.0f} cm)")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("BOXES")
    missing = [rb for rb in ids if rb not in found_ids]
    if missing:
        lines.append(f"  not tracked: rigid bodies {missing} (in view of OptiTrack?)")
        ok_all = False
    for i, j, d in match(targets, found):
        t = targets[i]
        if j is None:
            lines.append(f"  box {i + 1}: no box for it")
            ok_all = False
            continue
        good = d <= tol
        ok_all &= good
        f = found[j]
        lines.append(f"  box {i + 1} (rb {found_ids[j]}): {100 * d:5.1f} cm  "
                     + ("OK" if good else direction(t[0] - f[0], t[1] - f[1])))
    for rb in ALL_BOX_IDS:
        if rb in ids:
            continue
        q = hub.get_pose(rb)
        if q is not None and ARENA[0] <= q[0] <= ARENA[1] and ARENA[2] <= q[1] <= ARENA[3]:
            lines.append(f"  rb {rb} is in the arena but not in this layout: take it out")
            ok_all = False
    lines.append("")
    if L["radius_m"] is None:
        lines.append("ROBOTS (round 0, place by hand, facing the boxes)")
        rt = [r[:2] for r in L["robot_targets"]]
        rf, rnames = [], []
        for name, rb in ROBOT_IDS.items():
            q = hub.get_pose(rb)
            if q is not None:
                rf.append(q[:2])
                rnames.append(name)
        for i, j, d in match(rt, rf):
            if j is None:
                lines.append(f"  R{i + 1}: no robot tracked for it")
                ok_all = False
                continue
            good = d <= 2 * tol
            ok_all &= good
            lines.append(f"  R{i + 1} ({rnames[j]}): {100 * d:5.1f} cm  "
                         + ("OK" if good else direction(rt[i][0] - rf[j][0], rt[i][1] - rf[j][1])))
    else:
        lines.append(f"ROBOTS: anywhere near the circle of {L['radius_m']:g} m (they drive to the stations)")
    return lines, ok_all


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--layout", required=True, help="layout id of the plan, e.g. R01")
    ap.add_argument("--plan", default=None,
                    help="plan JSON (default: the first of docs/capture_plan_v2.json, docs/capture_plan_v3.json "
                         "that has the layout)")
    ap.add_argument("--tolerance", type=float, default=0.05, help="m, boxes (robots: twice this)")
    ap.add_argument("--optitrack-server", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--optitrack-local", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--no-launch", action="store_true", help="only the check, never start the capture")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    plan = {}
    for path in ([a.plan] if a.plan else ["docs/capture_plan_v2.json", "docs/capture_plan_v3.json"]):
        if os.path.exists(path):
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                plan = {L["id"]: L for L in json.load(f)}
            if a.layout in plan:
                break
    if a.layout not in plan:
        raise SystemExit(f"{a.layout} is not in {a.plan or 'docs/capture_plan_v2.json or docs/capture_plan_v3.json'}")
    L = plan[a.layout]
    from vf.localization.mocap_pose import MocapHub
    hub = MocapHub(sorted(set(ALL_BOX_IDS) | set(ROBOT_IDS.values())), a.optitrack_server, a.optitrack_local)
    start = False
    try:
        while True:
            lines, ok = report(L, hub, a.tolerance)
            os.system("cls" if os.name == "nt" else "clear")
            print("\n".join(lines))
            print()
            if a.no_launch:
                print("Ctrl+C to quit")
            elif ok:
                print("ALL PLACED. Enter: start the capture   |   Ctrl+C: quit")
            else:
                print("Enter: start the capture anyway   |   Ctrl+C: quit")
            if not a.no_launch and key_pressed():
                start = True
                break
            time.sleep(0.5)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nquit, nothing captured")
    finally:
        hub.close()
    if start:
        cmd = shlex.split(L["command"])
        cmd[0] = sys.executable
        print("\n" + " ".join(cmd) + "\n", flush=True)
        time.sleep(1.0)                                 # let the NatNet port go before launch_all opens it
        sys.exit(subprocess.call(cmd))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/calibrate_camera.py <==
"""RoboMaster EP camera calibration (standard OpenCV checkerboard).

Replaces the APPROXIMATE camera matrix of aruco_detector.py
(approximate_camera(), from the declared FOV, never verified) with a real
one, measured on YOUR camera: the distance and angle coming out of ArUco
depend on this calibration as much as on the marker size -- without it,
the numbers that end up in the logs (and then in the professor's fault
model) remain an approximation, not a measurement.

How to use
-----------
1. Print a standard OpenCV checkerboard (default 9x6 inner corners,
   squares of known side -- default 25mm below; MEASURE your printout,
   printers often scale slightly).
2. Hold it still/flat, move the camera (or the checkerboard) in front of
   the other in ~15-20 different poses (varied angles, distances, tilts:
   more variation = better calibration), pressing SPACE when you see it
   detected (coloured outlines) to capture that pose. 'q' to finish and
   compute.
3. python -m tools.calibrate_camera --source robot --robot-id P0 --out config/checkerboard_calib_P0.json
4. Pass that file to static_trial.py with
   --camera-calib config/checkerboard_calib_P0.json when using
   --detector aruco.

Using a local webcam instead of the robot camera
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Useful to try the script/procedure before being in front of the real robot
(the calibration geometry does not depend on which camera it is, only the
final NUMBERS are specific to the camera used):

    python -m tools.calibrate_camera --source webcam --out camera_calib_test.json

Without a printer: checkerboard shown on a screen
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
It works, but detection is objectively harder than with a printout:
non-uniform backlight, moire between the screen pixels and the sensor
pixels, reflections on the glass -- hence the "looks fine but it doesn't
find it" that happens even when the checkerboard is clearly visible to the
eye. detect_checkerboard() below already uses cv2.findChessboardCornersSB
(much more robust than the classic one precisely in these conditions) with
an automatic fallback, but if detection is still inconsistent it helps to
use: screen at MAXIMUM brightness and high contrast, no light creating
reflections on the glass (turn off direct lights behind the camera), a
checkerboard large/close enough to fill a good part of the frame (corners
that are small in pixels are the first to fail).
"""

import argparse
import json

import cv2
import numpy as np


def detect_checkerboard(gray, checkerboard):
    """Checkerboard corners in the greyscale image, or (False, None). Tries
    findChessboardCornersSB FIRST (OpenCV >= 4.0, "sector-based" algorithm
    much more robust than the classic one against uneven lighting, slight
    blur and reflections -- exactly the conditions of a checkerboard
    photographed from a SCREEN instead of printed: non-uniform backlight,
    moire between screen pixels and sensor pixels, possible reflections on
    the glass. It already returns sub-pixel accurate corners, with no need
    for cornerSubPix afterwards. If SB is not available (old OpenCV) or
    finds nothing, it falls back to the classic findChessboardCorners BUT
    with the adaptive flags (CALIB_CB_ADAPTIVE_THRESH +
    CALIB_CB_NORMALIZE_IMAGE, not enabled by default with `None`), which
    still help a bit with the screen case even though they remain weaker
    than SB."""
    if hasattr(cv2, "findChessboardCornersSB"):
        found, corners = cv2.findChessboardCornersSB(
            gray, checkerboard,
            flags=cv2.CALIB_CB_EXHAUSTIVE + cv2.CALIB_CB_ACCURACY)
        if found:
            return True, corners, True  # final True = already sub-pixel
    found, corners = cv2.findChessboardCorners(
        gray, checkerboard,
        cv2.CALIB_CB_ADAPTIVE_THRESH + cv2.CALIB_CB_NORMALIZE_IMAGE)
    return found, corners, False


def capture_poses(read_frame, checkerboard=(9, 6), square_size_m=0.025,
                  min_poses=15):
    criteria = (cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_EPS + cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_MAX_ITER, 30, 0.001)
    obj_pt = np.zeros((checkerboard[0] * checkerboard[1], 3), np.float32)
    obj_pt[:, :2] = np.mgrid[0:checkerboard[0], 0:checkerboard[1]].T.reshape(-1, 2)
    obj_pt *= square_size_m

    object_points, image_points = [], []
    image_size = None
    n_captured = 0

    print(f"SPACE to capture a good pose (coloured outlines "
          f"visible), 'q' to finish and compute "
          f"(recommended minimum: {min_poses} poses)")
    while True:
        img = read_frame()
        if img is None:
            continue
        image_size = (img.shape[1], img.shape[0])
        gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        found, corners, already_subpixel = detect_checkerboard(gray, checkerboard)

        display = img.copy()
        if found:
            if not already_subpixel:
                corners = cv2.cornerSubPix(
                    gray, corners, (11, 11), (-1, -1), criteria)
            cv2.drawChessboardCorners(display, checkerboard, corners, found)
        cv2.putText(display, f"captured: {n_captured}", (10, 30),
                    cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1, (0, 255, 0), 2)
        cv2.imshow("calibration (SPACE=capture, q=finish)", display)

        key = cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF
        if key == ord(" ") and found:
            object_points.append(obj_pt)
            image_points.append(corners)
            n_captured += 1
            print(f"  captured pose {n_captured}")
        elif key == ord("q"):
            break

    cv2.destroyAllWindows()
    if n_captured < min_poses:
        print(f"WARNING: only {n_captured} poses (< {min_poses} "
              f"recommended) -- the calibration may not be very "
              f"accurate. You can still proceed, or run again to "
              f"add more.")
    return object_points, image_points, image_size


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--source", choices=["robot", "webcam"], default="robot")
    p.add_argument("--webcam-index", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--robot-id", default=None,
                   help="robot name in config.ROBOTS (only with "
                        "--source robot; if omitted you are asked for it)")
    p.add_argument("--checkerboard", default="9x6",
                   help="inner corners horizontal x vertical, e.g. 9x6")
    p.add_argument("--square-size-m", type=float, default=0.025,
                   help="side of one checkerboard square in metres "
                        "-- MEASURE your printout, do not trust the "
                        "default")
    p.add_argument("--out", default="camera_calib.json")
    args = p.parse_args()

    checkerboard = tuple(int(v) for v in args.checkerboard.lower().split("x"))

    if args.source == "webcam":
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(args.webcam_index)

        def read_frame():
            ok, frame = cap.read()
            return frame if ok else None

        close = cap.release
    else:
        # Imported here, not at the top of the file: this script is also
        # used just to calibrate from a webcam without having robomaster_sdk
        # installed.
        from robomaster_sdk import Robot
        from robomaster_sdk.camera import Camera as SdkCamera

        robot_id = args.robot_id or input("robot name (config.ROBOTS): ").strip()
        robot_cm = Robot(robot_id)
        robot = robot_cm.__enter__()
        camera = SdkCamera(robot.camera).start(resolution="720")

        def read_frame():
            img, _age = camera.read()
            return img

        def close():
            camera.stop()
            robot_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)

    try:
        object_points, image_points, image_size = capture_poses(
            read_frame, checkerboard, args.square_size_m)
    finally:
        close()

    if len(object_points) < 4:
        print("Too few poses captured (< 4, the mathematical minimum "
              "for calibrateCamera): calibration aborted, no file "
              "written.")
        return

    rms_error, camera_matrix, dist_coeffs, _rvecs, _tvecs = cv2.calibrateCamera(
        object_points, image_points, image_size, None, None)

    print(f"\nRMS reprojection error: {rms_error:.4f} px "
          f"(below 0.5 is good, above 1.0 repeat with more poses/more "
          f"angle variation)")

    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
        json.dump({
            "camera_matrix": camera_matrix.tolist(),
            "dist_coeffs": dist_coeffs.tolist(),
            "rms_error_px": rms_error,
            "image_size": image_size,
            "n_poses": len(object_points),
        }, f, indent=2)
    print(f"saved to {args.out} -- pass it to static_trial.py with "
          f"--camera-calib {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/calibrate_optitrack.py <==
"""Calibrates the frame correction (rotation + translation) between the raw
pose of an OptiTrack robot and the true GLOBAL reference frame.

Why it is needed
-------------
The raw pose of an OptiTrack rigid body (x, y, yaw) may not be registered
in the same "true" frame used to define where the objects really are in the
room -- this happens when the rigid body was created/zeroed in Motive
without an explicit alignment to the room axes. [NOTE September 2026: the
bearing math was NOT correct -- global_position used yaw + bearing instead
of yaw - bearing, now fixed; corrections fitted before that fix must be
redone.] Neither the camera calibration (checkerboard) nor the plausibility
of the single robot's pose (all already verified) touch this problem: a
rigid body can report a pose that is perfectly self-consistent and still be
rotated/translated with respect to the true frame. The effect: every object
detected by that robot (object_position.global_position(), which uses the
robot's x,y,yaw directly) inherits a CONSTANT rotation+translation error for
that robot, which shows up as disagreement between the positions computed
by different robots for the same physical object -- confirmed in
conversation by comparing the positions with an independent ground-truth
reference (see below): up to 1.8m of error for a single robot on a single
object.

How the ground-truth reference is measured
------------------------------------------
You need an OptiTrack rigid body ATTACHED to an object (e.g. the box),
whose TRUE position (x,y) you read directly from OptiTrack --
mocap_pose.MocapPose(object_rb_id, server, local).get_pose() -- WITHOUT
going through the camera/bearing/distance of any robot. For N different
positions of the object: note (a) its true position from this, (b) the
position that ONE robot computes for the same object (xy= shown by
static_trial.py --live). With AT LEAST 2 (true, computed) pairs the
rotation+translation is solved exactly; with 3+ a least-squares fit is done
(more points = more robust to the noise of single measurements, and it lets
you check the residual). The calibration is PER ROBOT: P0 and P1 must be
calibrated separately (different frames = different corrections), see
--points/--out to do one pass at a time.

The fit is a 2D rigid alignment (Procrustes/Kabsch without scale): it finds
the rotation theta and translation (dx,dy) that minimize
sum |R(theta)*computed_i + (dx,dy) - true_i|^2, with the closed form for
the 2D case:
    theta = atan2(sum(Sx'*Ty' - Sy'*Tx'), sum(Sx'*Tx' + Sy'*Ty'))
where S' = computed - centroid(computed), T' = true - centroid(true),
followed by the translation that aligns the two centroids after the
rotation.

Usage
---
    python -m tools.calibrate_optitrack --points points_P1.json --out correction_P1.json

points_P1.json:
    {"points": [{"true": [0.022, -0.066], "computed": [-0.33, -0.11]},
                {"true": [-0.409, 0.852], "computed": [-0.16, 1.00]},
                {"true": [0.752, -0.537], "computed": [-0.93, -0.82]}]}

correction_P1.json (the output) is then passed to static_trial.py with
--frame-correction-file correction_P1.json (see FrameCorrectedPose in
vf/localization/localization.py for how it is applied)."""

import argparse
import json
import math


def fit_rigid_transform(points):
    """points: list of dicts {"true": [x,y], "computed": [x,y]}.
    Returns (rotation_rad, dx, dy, residuals) where residuals is the list
    of point-by-point distances between corrected-computed and true, after
    applying the transformation found (lower = better fit; a high residual
    on all points means the error is not explained by a single constant
    rotation+translation)."""
    if len(points) < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "at least 2 (true, computed) pairs are needed to solve "
            "rotation+translation; with 3+ the fit is least-squares "
            "and more robust to the noise of single measurements")

    true_pts = [tuple(p["true"]) for p in points]
    computed_pts = [tuple(p["computed"]) for p in points]
    n = len(points)

    cx_v = sum(v[0] for v in true_pts) / n
    cy_v = sum(v[1] for v in true_pts) / n
    cx_c = sum(c[0] for c in computed_pts) / n
    cy_c = sum(c[1] for c in computed_pts) / n

    sum_cross = 0.0
    sum_dot = 0.0
    for (vx, vy), (cx, cy) in zip(true_pts, computed_pts):
        sx, sy = cx - cx_c, cy - cy_c
        tx, ty = vx - cx_v, vy - cy_v
        sum_cross += sx * ty - sy * tx
        sum_dot += sx * tx + sy * ty

    theta = math.atan2(sum_cross, sum_dot)
    cos_t, sin_t = math.cos(theta), math.sin(theta)

    # required: true_centroid = R(theta)*computed_centroid + (dx,dy)
    rcx = cos_t * cx_c - sin_t * cy_c
    rcy = sin_t * cx_c + cos_t * cy_c
    dx = cx_v - rcx
    dy = cy_v - rcy

    residuals = []
    for (vx, vy), (cx, cy) in zip(true_pts, computed_pts):
        px = cos_t * cx - sin_t * cy + dx
        py = sin_t * cx + cos_t * cy + dy
        residuals.append(math.hypot(px - vx, py - vy))

    return theta, dx, dy, residuals


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Calibrates rotation+translation between the pose of ONE "
                    "OptiTrack robot and the true frame, from pairs "
                    "(true position, position computed by the robot) "
                    "for the same independently tracked object.")
    p.add_argument("--points", required=True,
                   help="JSON file with {\"points\": [{\"true\": [x,y], "
                        "\"computed\": [x,y]}, ...]} -- see the "
                        "module docstring")
    p.add_argument("--out", default=None,
                   help="if given, writes the result here "
                        "(rotation_rad, dx_m, dy_m) as JSON, ready "
                        "for --frame-correction-file of static_trial.py")
    args = p.parse_args()

    with open(args.points) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    points = data["points"]

    theta, dx, dy, residuals = fit_rigid_transform(points)

    print(f"rotation: {math.degrees(theta):+.2f} degrees "
          f"({theta:+.4f} rad)")
    print(f"translation: dx={dx:+.3f}m dy={dy:+.3f}m")
    print(f"\npoint-by-point residuals after the correction ({len(points)} "
          f"points):")
    for i, r in enumerate(residuals):
        print(f"  point {i + 1}: {r:.3f}m")
    print(f"mean residual: {sum(residuals) / len(residuals):.3f}m  "
          f"max: {max(residuals):.3f}m")
    if max(residuals) > 0.3:
        print("\nmax residual above 0.3m: rotation+translation alone "
              "does not explain all the disagreement -- a common error "
              "remains to be checked separately (e.g. configured vs real "
              "marker size, offset between the ground-truth tracker and "
              "the physical point measured on the object).")

    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"rotation_rad": theta, "dx_m": dx, "dy_m": dy},
                      f, indent=2)
        print(f"\nwrote {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/capture_plan_v3.py <==
"""Capture plan of the third block of real scenes (R81 onwards): layouts chosen by their difficulty level.

The scenes of the real campaigns are split into three levels by their geometry only (tools/scene_levels.py):
  easy    every pair of boxes at least 25 cm apart, every box in clear view of at least two robots,
          no obstacles or white objects
  medium  as easy, but at least one box in clear view of a single robot
  hard    two boxes less than 25 cm apart, a box in clear view of no robot, obstacles or white objects
(a box is in clear view of a robot if it is within 40 deg of the optical axis and 3 m, and the line of sight
to it does not cross another box).

The second campaign has few medium scenes and few scenes of blocks D (white objects) and E (light). This plan
adds layouts of exactly those kinds. Every candidate layout is drawn at random (seed fixed), its robot positions
of the 4 rounds are predicted (circle: the stations of launch_all --radius turning by 22.5 deg per round;
random: the positions placed by hand turning about the boxes), and the level of every round is computed with
the boxes moved by +-4 cm and the robots by +-8 cm, as placement and driving errors. A medium layout is kept
only if at least 3 of its 4 rounds are medium in at least 60% of these draws, whichever way the formation
turns; in practice these are dense blocks of 6-7 boxes, close but not touching.

    python -m tools.capture_plan_v3                    # docs/capture_plan_v3.json, docs/capture_guide_v3.pdf,
                                                       # docs/capture_commands_v3.txt
    python -m tools.place_check --plan docs/capture_plan_v3.json --layout R81
"""

import argparse
import json
import math

import numpy as np

from tools.capture_plan import (BOX_IDS, CENTRE, KEEP_OUT_M, MIN_GAP_M, RADIUS, ROBOTS, STEP_DEG, SWEEP_DEG,
                                inside, random_robots, stations, white_objects, write_pdf)
from tools.scene_levels import scene_level

N_ROUNDS = int(round(SWEEP_DEG / STEP_DEG)) + 1
LENS_M = 0.15                       # camera ahead of the robot's rigid body


def cameras(robots, centre, turn_deg):
    """Camera poses (x, y, yaw) of the robots placed at `robots` [x, y, heading_deg] after the formation
    turned by turn_deg about `centre`, every robot facing `centre`."""
    out = []
    c = np.asarray(centre, float)
    t = math.radians(turn_deg)
    R = np.array([[math.cos(t), -math.sin(t)], [math.sin(t), math.cos(t)]])
    for x, y, _ in robots:
        p = c + R @ (np.array([x, y]) - c)
        yaw = math.atan2(c[1] - p[1], c[0] - p[0])
        out.append((p[0] + LENS_M * math.cos(yaw), p[1] + LENS_M * math.sin(yaw), yaw))
    return out


def round_levels(boxes, robots, centre, rng, draws=40, box_err=0.04, robot_err=0.08):
    """For each round and turning direction: the share of draws (boxes and robots moved by uniform errors)
    in which the round is easy / medium / hard. Returns {direction: [dict(level -> share) per round]}."""
    out = {}
    for sign in (+1, -1):
        rounds = []
        for k in range(N_ROUNDS):
            count = dict(easy=0, medium=0, hard=0)
            for _ in range(draws):
                b = np.asarray(boxes, float) + rng.uniform(-box_err, box_err, (len(boxes), 2))
                r = [(x + rng.uniform(-robot_err, robot_err), y + rng.uniform(-robot_err, robot_err), h)
                     for x, y, h in robots]
                count[scene_level(b, cameras(r, centre, sign * k * STEP_DEG))[0]] += 1
            rounds.append({lv: n / draws for lv, n in count.items()})
        out[sign] = rounds
    return out


def candidate_boxes(n, kind, rng):
    """n box centres (relative to the formation centre) of one arrangement kind, at least 30 cm apart."""
    gap = 0.30
    if kind == "line":                          # a line pointing between two robots: the rear boxes hide
        a = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
        pitch = rng.uniform(0.30, 0.38)
        t = (np.arange(n) - (n - 1) / 2) * pitch
        pts = np.stack([t * math.cos(a), t * math.sin(a)], 1) + rng.normal(0, 0.03, (n, 2))
    elif kind == "block":                       # a compact group, not touching
        pitch = rng.uniform(0.32, 0.38)
        lat = np.array([(i * pitch + j * pitch / 2, j * pitch * math.sqrt(3) / 2)
                        for i in range(-3, 4) for j in range(-3, 4)])
        order = np.argsort(np.hypot(*(lat - rng.normal(0, pitch / 3, 2)).T))
        pts = lat[order[:n]]
        pts = pts - pts.mean(0) + rng.normal(0, 0.02, (n, 2))
    else:                                       # a group plus a box behind it
        a = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
        u = np.array([math.cos(a), math.sin(a)])
        v = np.array([-u[1], u[0]])
        m = n - 1
        t = (np.arange(m) - (m - 1) / 2) * rng.uniform(0.32, 0.38)
        pts = np.vstack([np.outer(t, v), [u * rng.uniform(0.32, 0.40)]]) + rng.normal(0, 0.02, (n, 2))
        pts -= pts.mean(0)
    d = np.hypot(*(pts[:, None] - pts[None]).transpose(2, 0, 1))
    d[np.diag_indices(n)] = 9
    if d.min() < max(gap, MIN_GAP_M) or np.max(np.hypot(*pts.T)) > 0.55:
        return None
    return pts


def dense_block(n, rng, lo=0.30, hi=0.34):
    """n boxes on a jittered triangular lattice of pitch lo-hi (centres 30-34 cm apart: close, not touching)."""
    pitch = rng.uniform(lo, hi)
    lat = np.array([(i * pitch + j * pitch / 2, j * pitch * math.sqrt(3) / 2) for i in range(-3, 4) for j in range(-3, 4)])
    order = np.argsort(np.hypot(*(lat - rng.normal(0, pitch / 3, 2)).T))
    pts = lat[order[:n]]
    return pts - pts.mean(0) + rng.normal(0, 0.015, (n, 2))


def plan_medium(rng, n_layouts, start_id, draws=20, tries=3000):
    """Medium layouts: dense blocks of 6-7 boxes (centres 30-34 cm apart), robots on a circle of 1.0 or 1.3 m
    or at random. Kept if at least 3 of the 4 rounds are medium in at least 60% of the draws, whichever way
    the formation turns (a box hidden by the others from all robots but one)."""
    specs = [(7, "cerchio 1.0"), (7, "casuale"), (7, "cerchio 1.3"), (6, "casuale"), (6, "cerchio 1.0")]
    out, t = [], 0
    while len(out) < n_layouts and t < tries:
        n, robots_kind = specs[t % len(specs)]
        t += 1
        pts = dense_block(n, rng)
        boxes = pts + np.asarray(CENTRE)
        if RADIUS[robots_kind]:
            robots, centre = stations(RADIUS[robots_kind]), CENTRE
        else:
            robots = random_robots(boxes, rng, dmin=0.9)
            if robots is None:
                continue
            centre = tuple(boxes.mean(0))
        lv = round_levels(boxes, robots, centre, rng, draws=draws)
        good = min(sum(r["medium"] >= 0.6 for r in lv[sign]) for sign in lv)
        if good < 3:
            continue
        share = float(np.mean([r["medium"] for sign in lv for r in lv[sign]]))
        out.append(dict(boxes=boxes, robots=robots, robots_kind=robots_kind, n=n, kind="block", medium_share=share,
                        rounds=good))
        print(f"  medium layout {len(out)}: {n} boxes, {robots_kind}, {good}/4 rounds medium, after {t} tries",
              flush=True)
    return out


def layout_dict(lid, block, n, arrangement, robots_kind, boxes, robots, note, objects, rng, level):
    from tools.capture_plan import command
    row = dict(id=lid, robots=robots_kind, extra=note)
    cmd = command(row, n)
    return dict(id=lid, day=6, block=block, split="test", n_boxes=n, arrangement=arrangement, robots=robots_kind,
                radius_m=RADIUS[robots_kind], note=note, centre=list(CENTRE), level=level,
                boxes=[[round(float(x), 3), round(float(y), 3), round(float(rng.uniform(0, 120)), 0)] for x, y in boxes],
                box_ids=BOX_IDS[:n], robot_targets=robots, objects=objects, command=cmd)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--json", default="docs/capture_plan_v3.json")
    ap.add_argument("--pdf", default="docs/capture_guide_v3.pdf")
    ap.add_argument("--commands", default="docs/capture_commands_v3.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--medium", type=int, default=14)
    ap.add_argument("--white", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--light", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--first-id", type=int, default=81)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=2027)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(a.seed)
    layouts, k = [], a.first_id
    names = dict(block="dense block, not touching")
    for m in plan_medium(rng, a.medium, k):
        layouts.append(layout_dict(f"R{k}", "M medium", m["n"], names[m["kind"]], m["robots_kind"], m["boxes"],
                                   m["robots"], f"medium in {m['rounds']}/4 rounds ({100 * m['medium_share']:.0f}% of the draws)",
                                   [], rng, "medium"))
        k += 1
    # white objects (block D) and light (block E): 3-5 sparse boxes, circle or random robots
    for block, count in (("D white objects", a.white), ("E light", a.light)):
        made = 0
        while made < count:
            n = (3, 4, 5)[made % 3]
            robots_kind = ("cerchio 1.3", "casuale")[made % 2]
            pts = []
            for _ in range(4000):
                r, ang = 0.5 * math.sqrt(rng.random()), rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
                p = np.array([r * math.cos(ang), r * math.sin(ang)])
                if all(np.hypot(*(p - q)) >= 0.40 for q in pts):
                    pts.append(p)
                if len(pts) == n:
                    break
            if len(pts) < n:
                continue
            pts = np.array(pts)
            boxes = pts + np.asarray(CENTRE)
            robots = stations(1.3) if RADIUS[robots_kind] else random_robots(boxes, rng, dmin=0.9)
            if robots is None:
                continue
            if block.startswith("D"):
                objs = white_objects(2 if made % 2 else 1, pts, rng, 0.6)
                note = f"{len(objs)} white object(s) that are not boxes (paper bin, white bag, white cup...)"
            else:
                objs = []
                note = ("curtains open" if made % 2 == 0 else "half of the lights off")
            centre = CENTRE if RADIUS[robots_kind] else tuple(boxes.mean(0))
            lv = round_levels(boxes, robots, centre, rng, draws=20)
            lvl = "hard" if block.startswith("D") else max(("easy", "medium", "hard"),
                                                             key=lambda L: sum(r[L] for r in lv[1]))
            layouts.append(layout_dict(f"R{k}", block, n, "sparse", robots_kind, boxes, robots, note, objs, rng, lvl))
            k += 1
            made += 1
    with open(a.json, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(layouts, f, indent=1)
    write_pdf(layouts, a.pdf)
    with open(a.commands, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("CAPTURE COMMANDS - third block of real scenes (R%d-R%d)\n" % (a.first_id, k - 1))
        f.write("Run from the project folder on the lab PC, venv active. Capture in this order (medium first).\n")
        f.write("Medium layouts: dense blocks whose boxes must NOT touch (centres 28-34 cm apart): place them\n"
                "within 3 cm (--tolerance 0.03). White objects of block D are not tracked: place them by eye\n"
                "from the guide. Block E: change the light before starting the layout and keep it for all 4 rounds.\n"
                "End of the day: git add data/survey_v2 config/ground_truth_positions.json, commit, push.\n\n")
        for L in layouts:
            f.write(f"{L['id']}  {L['block']}  {L['n_boxes']} boxes, {L['arrangement']}, robots {L['robots']}"
                    f"  [{L['note']}]\n")
            tol = " --tolerance 0.03" if L["level"] == "medium" else ""
            f.write(f"    python -m tools.place_check --plan {a.json} --layout {L['id']}{tol}\n")
            f.write(f"    (it runs: {L['command']})\n\n")
    print(f"{len(layouts)} layouts -> {a.json}, {a.pdf}, {a.commands}")
    for L in layouts:
        print(f"  {L['id']} {L['block']:<16} {L['n_boxes']} boxes {L['arrangement']:<22} {L['robots']:<12} "
              f"{L['level']:<7} {L['note']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/select_runs.py <==
"""Copies one run per layout of a capture campaign into a clean folder, so that every pipeline (classical
methods, GNN, image network) reads the same scenes and none of the aborted or repeated attempts.

The run kept for a layout is the one of pipeline.build_scans.best_runs: among the runs with the most
stored frames, the one whose folder name ends in F (marked as the good capture), otherwise the latest.

    python -m tools.select_runs --src data/survey_v2/ --dst data/survey_v2_best/
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import shutil

from pipeline.build_scans import best_runs


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--src", default="data/survey_v2/")
    ap.add_argument("--dst", default="data/survey_v2_best/")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    runs = sorted(d for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(a.src, "*")) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "raw")))
    keep = best_runs(runs)
    os.makedirs(a.dst, exist_ok=True)
    for d in keep:
        name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d))
        target = os.path.join(a.dst, name)
        if not os.path.isdir(target):
            shutil.copytree(d, target)
    print(f"{len(keep)} layouts from {len(runs)} runs -> {a.dst}")
    print(" ".join(os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d)) for d in keep))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/scene_levels.py <==
"""Difficulty level of every real scene, from its geometry only (OptiTrack positions of boxes and cameras),
independently of any method, and the correct scenes of every method per level.

A box is in CLEAR VIEW of a robot if it is within 40 deg of the optical axis and 3 m of the camera, and the line
of sight to its centre does not pass within 0.8 circumradius of another box closer to the camera.
  easy    every pair of boxes at least 25 cm apart, every box in clear view of at least two robots,
          no obstacles or white objects
  medium  as easy, but at least one box in clear view of a single robot
  hard    two boxes less than 25 cm apart, a box in clear view of no robot, obstacles (block C) or white
          objects (block D)

    python -m tools.scene_levels                       # results/scene_levels.csv and results/levels_summary.csv
"""

import argparse
import collections
import csv
import glob
import json
import math
import os

import numpy as np

BOX_SIDE_M = 0.235
APOTHEM_M = BOX_SIDE_M / (2 * math.sqrt(3))
CIRCUMRADIUS_M = BOX_SIDE_M / math.sqrt(3)
HALF_FOV = math.radians(40)
MAX_RANGE_M = 3.0
TOUCH_M = 0.25
LENS_FIX_M = 0.03                   # recorded camera pose (12 cm ahead of the body) -> lens (15 cm)


def clear_views(boxes, cams):
    """Per box: the number of cameras (x, y, yaw) that have it in clear view."""
    B = np.asarray(boxes, float)
    views = []
    for k in range(len(B)):
        v = 0
        for x, y, yaw in cams:
            d = math.hypot(B[k][0] - x, B[k][1] - y)
            if d < 1e-6 or d > MAX_RANGE_M:
                continue
            u = (B[k] - [x, y]) / d
            if abs((math.atan2(u[1], u[0]) - yaw + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi) > HALF_FOV:
                continue
            hidden = False
            for j in range(len(B)):
                if j == k:
                    continue
                t = float(np.dot(B[j] - [x, y], u))
                across = abs(u[0] * (B[j][1] - y) - u[1] * (B[j][0] - x))
                if 0 < t < d - APOTHEM_M and across < 0.8 * CIRCUMRADIUS_M:
                    hidden = True
                    break
            v += not hidden
        views.append(v)
    return views


def scene_level(boxes, cams, block=""):
    """(level, closest centre distance [m], fewest clear views of a box)."""
    B = np.asarray(boxes, float)
    n = len(B)
    gap = min([float(np.hypot(*(B[i] - B[j]))) for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)] or [9.0])
    mv = min(clear_views(B, cams))
    if gap < TOUCH_M or mv == 0 or (block and block[0] in "CD"):
        return "hard", gap, mv
    return ("medium" if mv == 1 else "easy"), gap, mv


def run_scenes(run_dir, gt_key=None):
    """Boxes and, per round, the camera poses of reading 0 (no yaw offset) of one run."""
    with open(os.path.join(run_dir, "ground_truth.json")) as f:
        gt = json.load(f)
    v = gt.get(gt_key) if gt_key else None
    v = v or list(gt.values())[0]
    boxes = [(b["x"], b["y"]) for b in v if b["class_name"] == "box"]
    cams = collections.defaultdict(dict)
    for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(run_dir, "raw", "P*.jsonl")):
        with open(p) as f:
            for line in f:
                r = json.loads(line)
                if r.get("reading", 0) != 0 or r["trial_id"].split("/")[-1] not in ("+0", "0"):
                    continue
                x, y, yaw = r["camera_pose"]
                cams[int(r["round"])][r["robot_id"]] = (x + LENS_FIX_M * math.cos(yaw),
                                                        y + LENS_FIX_M * math.sin(yaw), yaw)
    return boxes, cams


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--first", default="data/survey_rounds/*", help="runs of the first campaign")
    ap.add_argument("--second", default="data/survey_v2/*", help="runs of the second campaign")
    ap.add_argument("--runs-list", default="results/gnn_mixed_large/detection_full_ring_h3/test_scenes_real_v2.csv",
                    help="CSV with a 'run' column: the run kept for each layout of the second campaign")
    ap.add_argument("--plans", nargs="+", default=["docs/capture_plan_v2.csv", "docs/capture_plan_v3.json"])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/scene_levels.csv")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    block = {}
    for p in a.plans:
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            continue
        if p.endswith(".csv"):
            with open(p, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                block.update({r["id"]: r["block"] for r in csv.DictReader(f)})
        else:
            with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                block.update({L["id"]: L["block"] for L in json.load(f)})
    rows = []
    for d in sorted(glob.glob(a.first)):
        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "raw")):
            continue
        L = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d)).split("_")[0]
        boxes, cams = run_scenes(d)
        for rnd, c in sorted(cams.items()):
            lv, gap, mv = scene_level(boxes, list(c.values()))
            rows.append(dict(campaign="first", layout=L, round=rnd, block="", n_boxes=len(boxes), gap_m=round(gap, 3),
                             min_clear_views=mv, level=lv))
    keep = None
    if a.runs_list and os.path.exists(a.runs_list):
        with open(a.runs_list, newline="") as f:
            keep = {r["run"] for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
    dirs = {os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d)): d for d in glob.glob(a.second) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "raw"))}
    from pipeline.build_scans import best_runs
    chosen = []
    for L in sorted({n.split("_")[0] for n in dirs}):
        cand = {n: d for n, d in dirs.items() if n.split("_")[0] == L}
        # the run used by the other evaluations; a folder renamed with a final F may have lost a digit
        hit = [d for n, d in cand.items() if keep and any(r.startswith(n.rstrip("F")) for r in keep)]
        chosen += hit[:1] if hit else best_runs(list(cand.values()))
    for d in sorted(chosen):
        name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d))
        L = name.split("_")[0]
        boxes, cams = run_scenes(d, name.rstrip("F"))
        for rnd, c in sorted(cams.items()):
            lv, gap, mv = scene_level(boxes, list(c.values()), block.get(L, ""))
            rows.append(dict(campaign="second", layout=L, round=rnd, block=block.get(L, ""), n_boxes=len(boxes),
                             gap_m=round(gap, 3), min_clear_views=mv, level=lv))
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(a.out), exist_ok=True)
    with open(a.out, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    c = collections.Counter((r["campaign"], r["level"]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{len(rows)} scenes -> {a.out}")
    for k in sorted(c):
        print(f"  {k[0]:<7} {k[1]:<7} {c[k]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/read_yaw.py <==
"""Continuously prints x, y, yaw (degrees) of ONE OptiTrack rigid body --
used for the alignment check: place the two robots physically PARALLEL
(same heading, use a ruler or a wall as reference), run this on one robot
at a time with its --rb-id, and compare the printed yaw. If for an
identical physical alignment the two robots give a different yaw, that
difference is the rigid body calibration offset to correct before
trusting any distance/position computed by the acquisition scripts (see
object_position.global_position, which adds bearing + this yaw).

Usage
---
    python -m tools.read_yaw --rb-id 8
    python -m tools.read_yaw --rb-id 7 --server 127.0.0.1 --local 127.0.0.1

'q' + enter to quit, or Ctrl+C. Only one robot/rigid body at a time is
intentional: it is a check, there is no need to read them together.
"""

import argparse
import math
import threading
import time
from vf.localization.mocap_pose import MocapPose


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--rb-id", type=int, required=True,
                   help="rigid body id in Motive for THIS robot")
    p.add_argument("--server", default="127.0.0.1")
    p.add_argument("--local", default="127.0.0.1")
    p.add_argument("--hz", type=float, default=2.0,
                   help="how many readings per second to print (default 2)")
    args = p.parse_args()
    source = MocapPose(args.rb_id, args.server, args.local)
    source.wait_ready()

    stop = threading.Event()

    def wait_for_exit():
        try:
            input()
        except EOFError:
            pass
        stop.set()

    print("'q' + enter (or Ctrl+C) to quit. Printing x, y, yaw until "
          "you stop.\n")
    threading.Thread(target=wait_for_exit, daemon=True).start()

    try:
        while not stop.is_set():
            pose = source.get_pose()
            if pose is None:
                print("\rno pose available (tracking lost?)"
                      "                    ", end="", flush=True)
            else:
                x, y, yaw_rad = pose
                yaw_deg = math.degrees(yaw_rad)
                print(f"\rrb_id={args.rb_id}  x={x:+.3f}  y={y:+.3f}  "
                      f"yaw={yaw_deg:+7.2f} degrees ({yaw_rad:+.4f} rad)"
                      f"          ", end="", flush=True)
            time.sleep(1.0 / args.hz)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        print()
        source.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/fig_levels_examples.py <==
"""Figure of the reports: one real scene per difficulty level (tools/scene_levels.py), seen from above.

Each box is coloured by the number of robots that have it in clear view (green: two or more, orange: one, red:
none); the dashed lines are the clear views. In a hard scene the cause is marked: the two boxes that almost
touch (red ring).

    python -m tools.fig_levels_examples --scene R03:1:easy --scene R81:0:medium --scene R08:0:hard \\
        --out results/figures/fig_levels_examples.png
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import math
import os

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Ellipse, Polygon

from pipeline.build_scans import best_runs
from tools.draw_robot import draw_robot
from tools.fig_scene_rounds import LEVEL_COLOUR, VIEW_COLOUR, seen_by
from tools.scene_levels import CIRCUMRADIUS_M, TOUCH_M, run_scenes, scene_level

WHY = {"easy": "every box seen clearly by 2+ robots,\nboxes at least 25 cm apart",
       "medium": "boxes seen clearly by a single robot\n(orange)",
       "hard": "{cause}"}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--scene", action="append", required=True, metavar="LAYOUT:ROUND:LEVEL")
    ap.add_argument("--runs", default="data/survey_v2/*")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/figures/fig_levels_examples.png")
    ap.add_argument("--half", type=float, default=1.65, help="half side of each panel [m]")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    runs = sorted(d for d in glob.glob(a.runs) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "raw")))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(a.scene), figsize=(4.4 * len(a.scene), 5.6))
    for ax, spec in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), a.scene):
        layout, rnd, expected = spec.split(":")
        run = best_runs([d for d in runs if os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d)).split("_")[0] == layout])[0]
        name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(run))
        boxes, cams = run_scenes(run, name.rstrip("F"))
        with open(os.path.join(run, "ground_truth.json")) as f:
            gt = json.load(f)
        entries = gt.get(name.rstrip("F")) or next(iter(gt.values()))
        yaws = [b.get("yaw") or 0.0 for b in entries if b["class_name"] == "box"]
        cs = [cams[int(rnd)][q] for q in sorted(cams[int(rnd)])]
        level, gap, mv = scene_level(boxes, cs)
        if level != expected:
            print(f"{spec}: level is {level}, not {expected}")
        views = seen_by(boxes, cs)
        B = np.asarray(boxes, float)
        allxy = np.vstack([B, np.asarray(cs)[:, :2]])
        centre = (allxy.min(0) + allxy.max(0)) / 2
        for k, (bx, by) in enumerate(boxes):
            for n in views[k]:
                ax.plot([cs[n][0], bx], [cs[n][1], by], color="#2a78d6", lw=0.7, ls=(0, (3, 2)), alpha=0.6)
        for k, (bx, by) in enumerate(boxes):
            pts = [(bx + CIRCUMRADIUS_M * math.cos(yaws[k] + i * 2 * math.pi / 3),
                    by + CIRCUMRADIUS_M * math.sin(yaws[k] + i * 2 * math.pi / 3)) for i in range(3)]
            ax.add_patch(Polygon(pts, closed=True, fc=VIEW_COLOUR[min(len(views[k]), 2)], ec="#222", lw=0.9,
                                 zorder=4))
        cause = ""
        if level == "hard":
            if gap < TOUCH_M:
                i, j = min(((i, j) for i in range(len(B)) for j in range(i + 1, len(B))),
                           key=lambda p: np.hypot(*(B[p[0]] - B[p[1]])))
                mid = (B[i] + B[j]) / 2
                ang = math.degrees(math.atan2(*(B[j] - B[i])[::-1]))
                ax.add_patch(Ellipse(mid, gap + 0.42, 0.40, angle=ang, fill=False, ec="#c0392b", lw=2, ls="--",
                                     zorder=6))
                cause = f"two boxes {100 * gap:.0f} cm apart,\nalmost touching (red ring)"
            elif mv == 0:
                cause = "a box (red) seen clearly\nby no robot"
        for x, y, yaw in cs:
            draw_robot(ax, x, y, yaw)
        half = max(a.half, float(np.max(np.abs(allxy - centre))) + 0.35)
        ax.set_xlim(centre[0] - half, centre[0] + half)
        ax.set_ylim(centre[1] - half, centre[1] + half)
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.set_xticks([])
        ax.set_yticks([])
        for s in ax.spines.values():
            s.set_color("#ccc")
        ax.set_title(level.capitalize(), loc="left", pad=46, fontsize=15, fontweight="bold",
                     color=LEVEL_COLOUR[level])
        ax.text(0.0, 1.02, WHY[level].format(cause=cause), transform=ax.transAxes, va="bottom", fontsize=11,
                color="#333")
        print(f"{spec}: {name}, level {level}, closest boxes {100 * gap:.0f} cm, fewest clear views {mv}")
    handles = [plt.Line2D([], [], marker="^", ls="", ms=10, mfc=VIEW_COLOUR[v], mec="#222", label=t)
               for v, t in ((2, "box in clear view of 2+ robots"), (1, "of 1 robot only"), (0, "of no robot"))]
    handles.append(plt.Line2D([], [], marker="s", ls="", ms=9, mfc="#d6e4f7", mec="#2a78d6", label="robot"))
    handles.append(plt.Line2D([], [], color="#2a78d6", lw=0.8, ls=(0, (3, 2)), label="clear view"))
    fig.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower center", ncol=5, frameon=False, fontsize=10)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 0.97))
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(a.out) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig(a.out, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight", pad_inches=0.15)
    print(f"written {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/fig_image_report.py <==
"""Figures of the image-network report: what the pretrained segmentation extracts from the real frames of one
scene, what the network receives, and the map of box centres it returns, on masks alone and on masks + markers.

For every --scene LAYOUT:ROUND (the run kept for that layout in --runs, first reading of the stop):
  <out>/<layout>_r<round>_frames.png   top: the four frames, brightened for display, with the rectangles found by
                                       Grounding DINO (red), the SAM mask (green) and the detected ArUco markers
                                       (yellow); bottom: the 256 x 144 input of each robot (mask white, markers red)
  <out>/<layout>_r<round>_maps.png     the floor map of box-centre probability of the network on masks alone and
                                       of the network on masks + markers, with the true boxes (OptiTrack), the
                                       boxes found and the four robots (their maps, boxes and robots are kept in
                                       <layout>_r<round>_maps.npz)
Runs in the environment of the demo (torch, transformers, a GPU helps):

    python -m tools.fig_image_report --scene R81:0 --scene R96:0 --out results/figures/image_report/
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import math
import os
import pickle
import shutil

import cv2
import numpy as np

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Polygon

from bevnet import geometry as geo
from bevnet import real
from pipeline.build_scans import best_runs
from tools.draw_robot import draw_robot

SCALE = 0.2


def brighten(img, gain=2.2):
    """The laboratory frames are dark: a gamma lift for display only (the network never sees the frame)."""
    lut = np.clip(255 * (np.arange(256) / 255) ** (1 / gain), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return cv2.LUT(img, lut)


def frame_overlay(img, mask, rects, dets):
    """The frame brightened, the mask tinted green with its outline, DINO rectangles red, markers yellow."""
    view = brighten(img)
    tint = view.copy()
    tint[mask > 127] = (80, 200, 80)
    view = cv2.addWeighted(view, 0.65, tint, 0.35, 0)
    cnts, _ = cv2.findContours((mask > 127).astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    cv2.drawContours(view, cnts, -1, (60, 230, 60), 3)
    for x0, y0, x1, y1 in rects:
        cv2.rectangle(view, (int(x0), int(y0)), (int(x1), int(y1)), (40, 40, 235), 3)
    for d in dets:
        if d.get("bbox"):
            bx, by, bw, bh = [int(round(v)) for v in d["bbox"]]
            cv2.rectangle(view, (bx, by), (bx + bw, by + bh), (0, 220, 255), 4)
    return cv2.cvtColor(view, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)


def network_input(mask, dets, W, H):
    """What the network receives: the mask at 256 x 144 (white) and the marker rectangles (red)."""
    w, h = int(round(1280 * SCALE)), int(round(720 * SCALE))
    small = (cv2.resize(mask, (w, h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA) > 127).astype(np.uint8) * 255
    mk = np.zeros_like(small)
    for d in dets:
        if d.get("bbox"):
            bx, by, bw, bh = d["bbox"]
            cv2.rectangle(mk, (int(round(bx * w / W)), int(round(by * h / H))),
                          (int(round((bx + bw) * w / W)), int(round((by + bh) * h / H))), 255, -1)
    rgb = np.dstack([small, small, small]).astype(np.uint8)
    rgb[mk > 0] = (230, 50, 50)
    return rgb


def predict(net, threshold, scene, folder, device, markers):
    """(probability map, estimates (K, 2) in the frame of the scene) of one scene."""
    from bevnet.data import BevDataset
    from bevnet.train import loader, predict_iter
    shutil.rmtree(folder, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(folder)
    with open(os.path.join(folder, "shard_0000.pkl"), "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump([scene], f, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
    with open(os.path.join(folder, "meta.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(dict(set=os.path.basename(folder), scenario="real", scenes=1, camera="real", K=scene["K"][0],
                       D=scene["D"][0], size=[256, 144], scale=SCALE, marker_channel=markers), f)
    heat, off, *_ = next(predict_iter(net, loader(BevDataset([folder]), 1, False, 0), device))
    return heat, geo.decode(heat, off, threshold)


def match(est, boxes, cutoff=0.15):
    pairs = sorted((math.hypot(e[0] - b[0], e[1] - b[1]), i, j) for i, e in enumerate(est) for j, b in enumerate(boxes))
    e_ok, b_ok = [False] * len(est), [False] * len(boxes)
    for d, i, j in pairs:
        if d <= cutoff and not e_ok[i] and not b_ok[j]:
            e_ok[i] = b_ok[j] = True
    return e_ok, b_ok


def verdict(est, boxes):
    e_ok, b_ok = match(est, boxes)
    if len(est) < len(boxes):
        return f"{len(est)} found, {len(boxes) - len(est)} missing"
    if len(est) > len(boxes):
        return f"{len(est)} found, {len(est) - len(boxes)} too many"
    return "all correct" if all(b_ok) else "right count, one misplaced"


def draw_map(ax, heat, est, boxes, yaws, cams, title, half):
    G = heat.shape[0]
    ext = [-geo.GRID_HALF_M, geo.GRID_HALF_M, -geo.GRID_HALF_M, geo.GRID_HALF_M]
    ax.imshow(heat, origin="lower", extent=ext, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1, interpolation="bilinear")
    r = real.BOX_SIDE_M / math.sqrt(3)
    e_ok, b_ok = match(est, boxes)
    for (bx, by), yaw, ok in zip(boxes, yaws, b_ok):
        pts = [(bx + r * math.cos(yaw + k * 2 * math.pi / 3), by + r * math.sin(yaw + k * 2 * math.pi / 3))
               for k in range(3)]
        ax.add_patch(Polygon(pts, closed=True, fill=False, ec="#111" if ok else "#c0392b", lw=1.8,
                             ls="-" if ok else "--"))
    for (x, y), ok in zip(est, e_ok):
        if ok:
            ax.plot(x, y, "o", ms=9, mfc="#1e8449", mec="white", mew=1.5)
        else:
            ax.plot(x, y, "X", ms=11, mfc="#c0392b", mec="white", mew=1.2)
    for x, y, yaw in cams:
        draw_robot(ax, x, y, yaw)
    ax.set_xlim(-half, half)
    ax.set_ylim(-half, half)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=13)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--scene", action="append", required=True, metavar="LAYOUT:ROUND")
    ap.add_argument("--runs", default="data/survey_v2/*")
    ap.add_argument("--image", default="results/bev_mask_wp/masks_wp")
    ap.add_argument("--image-markers", default="results/bev_mask_mk/masks_mk")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/figures/image_report/")
    ap.add_argument("--device", default="auto")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    import torch
    from bevnet.model import BevNet
    from bevnet.segment import BoxSegmenter
    device = torch.device(("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu") if a.device == "auto" else a.device)
    nets = {}
    for key, folder in (("masks", a.image), ("markers", a.image_markers)):
        with open(os.path.join(folder, "variant.json")) as f:
            v = json.load(f)
        net = BevNet(v["channels"], v["message"], len(geo.HEIGHTS_M), v.get("encoder", "small"),
                     pretrained=False).to(device)
        net.load_state_dict(torch.load(os.path.join(folder, "model.pt"), map_location=device))
        net.eval()
        nets[key] = (net, float(v["threshold"]))
    seg = BoxSegmenter(device=a.device)
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    work = os.path.join(a.out, "work")
    runs_all = sorted(d for d in glob.glob(a.runs) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "raw")))
    for spec in a.scene:
        layout, rnd = spec.split(":")
        rnd = int(rnd)
        cand = [d for d in runs_all if os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(d)).split("_")[0] == layout]
        run_dir = best_runs(cand)[0]
        runs = [(run_dir, *real.load_run(run_dir))]
        _d, lay_id, boxes, frames, cams = runs[0]
        cal = real.calibration(runs, real.PITCH_DEG, "same-run")
        recs = frames[(rnd, 0, 0)]
        with open(os.path.join(run_dir, "ground_truth.json")) as f:
            gt = json.load(f)
        gt_key = lay_id if lay_id in gt else os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(run_dir))   # as real.load_run
        yaws = [b.get("yaw") or 0.0 for b in gt[gt_key]]
        cache = os.path.join(work, "cache")
        tops, bottoms = [], []
        for q in sorted(recs):                                        # segment once, cached for build_scene
            img = cv2.imread(os.path.join(run_dir, recs[q]["image"].replace("\\", "/")))
            mask, rects, labels = seg(img)
            key = os.path.join(cache, os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(run_dir)),
                               os.path.basename(recs[q]["image"].replace("\\", "/"))[:-4] + ".png")
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(key), exist_ok=True)
            cv2.imwrite(key, mask)
            cv2.imwrite(key[:-4] + "_ids.png", labels)
            dets = recs[q].get("detections", [])
            tops.append((q, frame_overlay(img, mask, rects, dets)))
            bottoms.append(network_input(mask, dets, img.shape[1], img.shape[0]))
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, len(tops), figsize=(4.2 * len(tops), 4.9),
                                 gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1, 1], hspace=0.12, wspace=0.04))
        for k, ((q, top), bottom) in enumerate(zip(tops, bottoms)):
            axes[0, k].imshow(top)
            axes[0, k].set_title(f"robot {q}", fontsize=12)
            axes[1, k].imshow(bottom)
            for ax in (axes[0, k], axes[1, k]):
                ax.set_xticks([])
                ax.set_yticks([])
        axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("camera frame", fontsize=12)
        axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("network input", fontsize=12)
        name = f"{layout}_r{rnd}"
        fig.savefig(os.path.join(a.out, f"{name}_frames.png"), dpi=170, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)
        results = {}
        for key, markers in (("masks", False), ("markers", True)):
            scene = real.build_scene(run_dir, lay_id, boxes, recs, cams, SCALE, 92, real.PITCH_DEG, cal, seg,
                                     cache, None, False, False, markers, False)
            net, thr = nets[key]
            heat, est = predict(net, thr, scene, os.path.join(work, key), device, markers)
            results[key] = (heat, est, scene)
        scene = results["masks"][2]
        centre = np.array(scene["centre"])
        bx = np.asarray(boxes, float) - centre
        cams_rel = [(p[0], p[1], p[2]) for p in np.asarray(scene["poses"], float)]
        half = max(1.2, float(np.max(np.abs(np.vstack([bx, np.asarray(cams_rel)[:, :2]])))) + 0.55)
        np.savez_compressed(os.path.join(a.out, f"{name}_maps.npz"), boxes=bx, yaws=np.asarray(yaws),
                            cams=np.asarray(cams_rel), half=half,
                            **{f"{k}_{f}": v for k in results for f, v in (("heat", results[k][0]),
                                                                            ("est", np.asarray(results[k][1])))})
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5.6))
        for ax, key, label in ((axes[0], "masks", "masks only"), (axes[1], "markers", "masks + markers")):
            heat, est, _s = results[key]
            draw_map(ax, heat, est, bx, yaws, cams_rel, f"{label}: {verdict(est, bx)}", half)
        fig.tight_layout()
        fig.savefig(os.path.join(a.out, f"{name}_maps.png"), dpi=170, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)
        print(f"{name} ({os.path.basename(run_dir)}): " + ", ".join(
            f"{k}: {verdict(v[1], bx)}" for k, v in results.items()), flush=True)
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
    print(f"figures in {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./tools/capture_plan.py <==
"""Capture plan of the second real data set: 80 layouts (R01-R80), each with the box positions, the box
orientations, the robot positions (random family), the obstacles and the launch command, drawn one per page.

The layouts follow docs/capture_plan_v2.csv (blocks, days, test/dev split). Every layout is drawn here once
with a fixed seed, so the plan is reproducible:
  docs/capture_plan_v2.json   the layouts (Motive coordinates, metres; yaw in degrees)
  docs/capture_guide_v2.pdf   one page per layout, in capture order, plus a cover page

The boxes are placed around the arena centre CENTRE (the middle of the OptiTrack bounding box), so that
every robot position, on the circle or at random, stays --margin inside the arena. tools/place_check.py
reads the same JSON and shows live, from OptiTrack, how far each box and robot is from its target.

    python -m tools.capture_plan                      # writes both files
    python -m tools.capture_plan --pdf-only           # redraw the PDF from the JSON
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import os

import numpy as np

ARENA = (-2.690, 2.135, -2.672, 1.519)              # x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max (config/optitrack_regions.json)
CORNERS = [(1.918, 1.452), (2.135, -2.672), (-2.690, -2.628), (-2.213, 1.519)]
CENTRE = (round((ARENA[0] + ARENA[1]) / 2, 2), round((ARENA[2] + ARENA[3]) / 2, 2))
MARGIN_M = 0.5                                      # survey --margin
KEEP_OUT_M = 0.45                                   # survey --keep-out-m (robot to box)
BOX_SIDE_M = 0.235
BOX_R_M = BOX_SIDE_M / math.sqrt(3)                 # centre to corner of the triangle
MIN_GAP_M = 2 * BOX_R_M + 0.02                      # centre distance at which two boxes cannot touch
STEP_DEG, SWEEP_DEG = 22.5, 67.5
ROBOTS = [("P0", 8, None), ("P1", 7, None), ("P3", 10, "config/checkerboard_calib_P1.json"),
          ("P5", 6, "config/checkerboard_calib_P1.json")]
BOX_IDS = [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17]
RADIUS = {"cerchio 1.0": 1.0, "cerchio 1.3": 1.3, "cerchio 1.5": 1.5, "casuale": None}


def box_limit(robots):
    """Largest distance of a box centre from CENTRE that keeps the robots clear of it."""
    r = RADIUS[robots]
    return (r if r else 1.2) - KEEP_OUT_M - BOX_R_M


def spaced(pts, p, gap):
    return all(math.hypot(p[0] - q[0], p[1] - q[1]) >= gap for q in pts)


def cluster(n, rng, pitch=0.32, centre=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """n boxes packed on a jittered triangular lattice (pitch = centre distance), around centre."""
    lat = [(i * pitch + j * pitch / 2, j * pitch * math.sqrt(3) / 2) for i in range(-4, 5) for j in range(-4, 5)]
    lat = np.array(lat)
    seed = rng.normal(0, pitch / 3, 2)
    order = np.argsort(np.hypot(*(lat - seed).T))
    pts = lat[order[:n]]
    pts = pts - pts.mean(0)
    a = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
    R = np.array([[math.cos(a), -math.sin(a)], [math.sin(a), math.cos(a)]])
    pts = pts @ R.T + rng.uniform(-0.015, 0.015, pts.shape)
    return pts + np.asarray(centre)


def arrangement(kind, n, rng, limit):
    """Box centres relative to CENTRE, or None if this draw does not fit."""
    if n == 1:
        return np.array([[rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05), rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05)]])
    if kind == "fitta":
        pts = cluster(n, rng, pitch=rng.uniform(0.30, 0.34))
    elif kind == "sparsa":
        pts = []
        for _ in range(4000):
            r, a = limit * math.sqrt(rng.random()), rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
            p = (r * math.cos(a), r * math.sin(a))
            if spaced(pts, p, 0.50 if limit >= 0.6 else 0.38):     # small circle: less room
                pts.append(p)
            if len(pts) == n:
                break
        if len(pts) < n:
            return None
        pts = np.array(pts) - np.mean(pts, 0) * 0.5
    elif kind == "fila/arco":
        pitch = 0.36
        if (n - 1) * pitch / 2 <= limit:                # straight line
            a = rng.uniform(0, math.pi)
            t = (np.arange(n) - (n - 1) / 2) * pitch
            pts = np.stack([t * math.cos(a), t * math.sin(a)], 1)
        else:                                           # arc of radius rho through the centre region
            rho = min(0.55 if n < 7 else 0.47, 0.9 * limit)
            dth = pitch / rho
            th0 = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
            th = th0 + (np.arange(n) - (n - 1) / 2) * dth
            pts = np.stack([rho * np.cos(th), rho * np.sin(th)], 1)
            pts -= pts.mean(0)
        pts += rng.uniform(-0.02, 0.02, pts.shape)
    else:                                               # two groups
        a = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
        u = np.array([math.cos(a), math.sin(a)])
        n1 = (n + 1) // 2
        sep = (0.42 if n >= 5 else 0.36) if limit >= 0.6 else 0.33
        pts = np.vstack([cluster(n1, rng, 0.32, -sep * u), cluster(n - n1, rng, 0.32, sep * u)])
    if np.max(np.hypot(*pts.T)) > limit:
        return None
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i):
            if math.hypot(*(pts[i] - pts[j])) < MIN_GAP_M:
                return None
    return pts


def inside(p, extra=0.0):
    return (ARENA[0] + MARGIN_M + extra <= p[0] <= ARENA[1] - MARGIN_M - extra and
            ARENA[2] + MARGIN_M + extra <= p[1] <= ARENA[3] - MARGIN_M - extra)


def random_robots(boxes, rng, tries=20000, dmin=0.9):
    """4 robot positions at dmin-1.8 m from the box centre, at least 40 deg apart, clear of the boxes, and
    inside the arena also after the formation has turned by SWEEP_DEG (counter-clockwise) around it."""
    c = boxes.mean(0)
    for _ in range(tries):
        ang = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi, 4))
        gaps = np.diff(np.concatenate([ang, [ang[0] + 2 * math.pi]]))
        if gaps.min() < math.radians(40):
            continue
        dist = rng.uniform(dmin, 1.8, 4)
        ok = True
        for a, d in zip(ang, dist):
            for turn in np.radians(np.arange(0, SWEEP_DEG + 1e-6, STEP_DEG)):
                p = c + d * np.array([math.cos(a + turn), math.sin(a + turn)])
                if not inside(p, 0.05) or np.min(np.hypot(*(boxes - p).T)) < KEEP_OUT_M + 0.12:
                    ok = False
                    break
            if not ok:
                break
        if ok:
            out = []
            for a, d in zip(ang, dist):
                p = c + d * np.array([math.cos(a), math.sin(a)])
                out.append([round(float(p[0]), 3), round(float(p[1]), 3),
                            round(math.degrees(math.atan2(c[1] - p[1], c[0] - p[0])), 1)])
            return out
    return None


def stations(radius):
    """Round 0 positions on the circle (launch_all --radius, --first-angle-deg 0), facing CENTRE."""
    out = []
    for i in range(4):
        a = math.radians(90.0 * i)
        p = (CENTRE[0] + radius * math.cos(a), CENTRE[1] + radius * math.sin(a))
        out.append([round(p[0], 3), round(p[1], 3), round(math.degrees(a) + 180.0, 1)])
    return out


def obstacles(n, boxes, rng, robots_round0, kind="obstacle"):
    """n objects (about 30 cm) between the boxes and the robots of round 0: on the line from CENTRE to a
    robot, 0.75-0.82 m from CENTRE, clear of the boxes."""
    out = []
    for k in range(200):
        if len(out) == n:
            break
        r = robots_round0[int(rng.integers(len(robots_round0)))]
        u = np.array(r[:2]) - np.asarray(CENTRE)
        u = u / np.linalg.norm(u)
        p = np.asarray(CENTRE) + u * rng.uniform(0.75, 0.82) + rng.normal(0, 0.03, 2)
        rel = boxes - (p - np.asarray(CENTRE))
        if np.min(np.hypot(*rel.T)) < 0.30 or not spaced([o[:2] for o in out], p, 0.6):
            continue
        out.append([round(float(p[0]), 3), round(float(p[1]), 3), kind])
    return out


def white_objects(n, boxes, rng, limit):
    """n white objects that are not boxes, among the boxes (away from them by 30 cm)."""
    out = []
    for _ in range(2000):
        if len(out) == n:
            break
        r, a = limit * math.sqrt(rng.random()), rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
        p = np.array([r * math.cos(a), r * math.sin(a)])
        if np.min(np.hypot(*(boxes - p).T)) < 0.32 or not spaced([np.array(o[:2]) - CENTRE for o in out], p, 0.35):
            continue
        q = p + np.asarray(CENTRE)
        out.append([round(float(q[0]), 3), round(float(q[1]), 3), "white object"])
    return out


def command(row, n_boxes):
    parts = ["python -m acquisition.launch_all"]
    for rid, rb, cal in ROBOTS:
        parts.append(f"--robot {rid}:{rb}" + (f":{cal}" if cal else ""))
    parts.append(f"--layout-id {row['id']}")
    parts += [f"--box {b}:box" for b in BOX_IDS[:n_boxes]]
    parts += ["--ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json", "--regions config/optitrack_regions.json",
              "--out data/survey_v2/", "--aruco-marker-size 0.077", "--range-fit 1.064 -0.080",
              "--camera-offset-forward-m 0.12", "--instance-threshold-m 0.2",
              f"--step-deg {STEP_DEG:g} --sweep-deg {SWEEP_DEG:g}",
              f"--circle-center {CENTRE[0]:g} {CENTRE[1]:g}", "--no-robot-avoidance"]
    r = RADIUS[row["robots"]]
    if r:
        parts.append(f"--radius {r:g}")
    if "yaw-offsets" in row["extra"]:
        parts.append("--yaw-offsets-deg -20 0 20")
    return " ".join(parts)


def build(csv_path, seed):
    with open(csv_path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    layouts = []
    for row in rows:
        n = int(row["boxes"])
        kind = row["arrangement"].split(" ")[0]
        limit = box_limit(row["robots"])
        if "ostacoli" in row["extra"]:
            limit = min(limit, 0.50)                    # leave room for the obstacles before the robots
        for _ in range(500):
            pts = arrangement(kind, n, rng, limit)
            if pts is None:
                continue
            boxes = pts + np.asarray(CENTRE)
            dmin = 1.3 if "ostacoli" in row["extra"] else 0.9      # robots clear of the obstacles
            robots = (random_robots(boxes, rng, dmin=dmin) if RADIUS[row["robots"]] is None
                      else stations(RADIUS[row["robots"]]))
            if robots is not None:
                break
        else:
            raise SystemExit(f"{row['id']}: no layout found")
        extra = []
        if "ostacoli" in row["extra"] or "ostacoli e" in row["extra"]:
            extra += obstacles(int(row["extra"][0]) if row["extra"][0].isdigit() else 2, pts, rng, robots)
        if "bianc" in row["extra"]:
            k = 2 if row["extra"].startswith("2") or "sparsi" in row["extra"] else 1
            extra += white_objects(k, pts, rng, min(limit, 0.6))
        layouts.append(dict(
            id=row["id"], day=int(row["day"]), block=row["block"], split=row["split"], n_boxes=n,
            arrangement=row["arrangement"], robots=row["robots"], radius_m=RADIUS[row["robots"]],
            note=row["extra"], centre=list(CENTRE),
            boxes=[[round(float(x), 3), round(float(y), 3), round(float(rng.uniform(0, 120)), 0)] for x, y in boxes],
            box_ids=BOX_IDS[:n], robot_targets=robots, objects=extra, command=command(row, n)))
    return layouts


def triangle(x, y, yaw_deg):
    a = math.radians(yaw_deg) + np.array([0, 2 * math.pi / 3, 4 * math.pi / 3])
    return np.stack([x + BOX_R_M * np.cos(a), y + BOX_R_M * np.sin(a)], 1)


def draw_scene(ax, L, zoom):
    """The layout on ax: the whole arena (zoom False) or the box area at a larger scale (zoom True)."""
    from matplotlib.patches import Circle, Polygon
    cx, cy = L["centre"]
    if not zoom:
        ax.add_patch(Polygon(CORNERS, closed=True, fill=False, ec="0.5", lw=1.5))
        ax.add_patch(Polygon([(ARENA[0] + MARGIN_M, ARENA[2] + MARGIN_M), (ARENA[1] - MARGIN_M, ARENA[2] + MARGIN_M),
                              (ARENA[1] - MARGIN_M, ARENA[3] - MARGIN_M), (ARENA[0] + MARGIN_M, ARENA[3] - MARGIN_M)],
                             closed=True, fill=False, ec="0.8", ls="--", lw=0.8))
        for r in (0.5, 1.0, 1.5):
            ax.add_patch(Circle((cx, cy), r, fill=False, ec="0.88", lw=0.8))
        if L["radius_m"]:
            ax.add_patch(Circle((cx, cy), L["radius_m"], fill=False, ec="tab:blue", lw=1, ls=":"))
            for i in range(4):
                for t in np.arange(STEP_DEG, SWEEP_DEG + 1e-6, STEP_DEG):
                    a = math.radians(90 * i + t)
                    ax.plot(cx + L["radius_m"] * math.cos(a), cy + L["radius_m"] * math.sin(a), "o", c="tab:blue",
                            ms=3, alpha=0.35)
        for k, (x, y, h) in enumerate(L["robot_targets"]):
            ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), 0.17, fc="#cfe2f3", ec="tab:blue", lw=1.2))
            ax.annotate("", xy=(x + 0.28 * math.cos(math.radians(h)), y + 0.28 * math.sin(math.radians(h))),
                        xytext=(x, y), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="tab:blue", lw=1.5))
            ax.text(x, y - 0.30, f"R{k + 1}" if L["radius_m"] is None else f"S{k + 1}", ha="center", va="top",
                    fontsize=8, color="tab:blue")
    s = 0.25 if zoom else 0.12
    ax.plot([cx - s, cx + s], [cy, cy], c="k", lw=1)
    ax.plot([cx, cx], [cy - s, cy + s], c="k", lw=1)
    for k, (x, y, yaw) in enumerate(L["boxes"]):
        ax.add_patch(Polygon(triangle(x, y, yaw), closed=True, fc="white", ec="k", lw=1.6 if zoom else 1.2))
        ax.text(x, y, str(k + 1), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=12 if zoom else 7, fontweight="bold")
    for x, y, kind in L["objects"]:
        if kind == "obstacle":
            ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), 0.15, fc="#f4cccc", ec="tab:red", lw=1.2, hatch="//"))
        else:
            ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), 0.10, fc="#fff2cc", ec="tab:orange", lw=1.2))
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    if zoom:
        h = 0.95
        ax.set_xlim(cx - h, cx + h)
        ax.set_ylim(cy - h, cy + h)
        ticks = np.arange(-0.9, 0.91, 0.1)
        ax.set_xticks(cx + ticks, [f"{100 * t:+.0f}" if abs(round(10 * t)) % 3 == 0 else "" for t in ticks],
                      fontsize=7)
        ax.set_yticks(cy + ticks, [f"{100 * t:+.0f}" if abs(round(10 * t)) % 3 == 0 else "" for t in ticks],
                      fontsize=7)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.35)
        ax.set_xlabel("dx from the centre + [cm] (Motive x)")
        ax.set_ylabel("dy [cm] (Motive y)")
        ax.set_title("boxes (10 cm grid)", fontsize=10)
    else:
        pad = 0.15
        ax.set_xlim(ARENA[0] - pad, ARENA[1] + pad)
        ax.set_ylim(ARENA[2] - pad, ARENA[3] + pad)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
        ax.set_xlabel("Motive x [m]")
        ax.set_ylabel("Motive y [m]")
        ax.set_title("arena and robots", fontsize=10)


def draw_page(fig, L):
    fig.clf()
    cx, cy = L["centre"]
    draw_scene(fig.add_axes([0.05, 0.24, 0.33, 0.64]), L, zoom=False)
    draw_scene(fig.add_axes([0.42, 0.24, 0.33, 0.64]), L, zoom=True)
    title = f"{L['id']}   day {L['day']}   {L['block']}   ({L['split']})"
    fig.text(0.05, 0.955, title, fontsize=16, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.05, 0.925, f"{L['n_boxes']} boxes, {L['arrangement']}, robots: {L['robots']}"
             + (f"   |   {L['note']}" if L["note"] else ""), fontsize=10)
    x0, y0 = 0.785, 0.87
    fig.text(x0, y0, "Boxes from the centre +", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(x0, y0 - 0.022, "#   dx [cm]  dy [cm]", fontsize=8, family="monospace")
    for k, (x, y, yaw) in enumerate(L["boxes"]):
        fig.text(x0, y0 - 0.042 - 0.019 * k, f"{k + 1:<2} {100 * (x - cx):+7.0f} {100 * (y - cy):+8.0f}",
                 fontsize=8, family="monospace")
    y1 = y0 - 0.06 - 0.019 * len(L["boxes"]) - 0.02
    if L["radius_m"] is None:
        fig.text(x0, y1, "Robots, round 0", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
