        und = und.reshape(self.H, self.W, 2)
        self.map_x = (und[..., 0] + m).astype(np.float32)
        self.map_y = (und[..., 1] + m).astype(np.float32)
        uu, vv = np.meshgrid(np.arange(self.Wi, dtype=np.float32), np.arange(self.Hi, dtype=np.float32))
        self.rays = np.stack([(uu - self.Ki[0, 2]) / self.Ki[0, 0], (vv - self.Ki[1, 2]) / self.Ki[1, 1],
                              np.ones_like(uu)], -1)
        yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:self.H, 0:self.W].astype(np.float32)
        r2 = ((xx - self.W / 2) / (self.W / 2)) ** 2 + ((yy - self.H / 2) / (self.H / 2)) ** 2
        self.radius2 = r2 / r2.max()


def camera_rotation(yaw, pitch, roll):
    """World -> camera rotation (rows: camera x right, y down, z forward, in world coordinates)."""
    f = np.array([math.cos(yaw) * math.cos(pitch), math.sin(yaw) * math.cos(pitch), -math.sin(pitch)])
    r = np.array([math.sin(yaw), -math.cos(yaw), 0.0])
    d = np.cross(f, r)
    r2 = math.cos(roll) * r + math.sin(roll) * d
    d2 = -math.sin(roll) * r + math.cos(roll) * d
    return np.stack([r2, d2, f])


# ====================================================================
# Textures
# ====================================================================

def separate_instances(labels, rng=None, merge_prob=0.0):
    """Binary box mask (uint8 0/255) from a label image (0 = background, k > 0 = box k), with a 1-pixel
    black line wherever two different boxes touch, so that boxes side by side in the image remain separate
    shapes. merge_prob: share of the touching pairs left without the line (drawn with rng), as when a
    segmentation takes two touching boxes for one. Used on the rendered masks (imgsim) and on the
    segmentation of the real frames (bevnet/real.py), at the resolution the network sees."""
    lab = np.asarray(labels)
    mask = lab > 0
    border = np.zeros_like(mask)
    pairs = []
    for a, b, where in ((lab[:, :-1], lab[:, 1:], (slice(None), slice(None, -1))),
                        (lab[:-1, :], lab[1:, :], (slice(None, -1), slice(None)))):
        touch = (a > 0) & (b > 0) & (a != b)
        if touch.any():
            pairs.append((a[touch], b[touch], where, touch))
    if not pairs:
        return (mask * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    merged = set()
    if merge_prob > 0 and rng is not None:
        found = {tuple(sorted(p)) for a, b, _, _ in pairs for p in zip(a.tolist(), b.tolist())}
        merged = {p for p in sorted(found) if rng.random() < merge_prob}
    for a, b, where, touch in pairs:
        keep = np.array([tuple(sorted(p)) not in merged for p in zip(a.tolist(), b.tolist())], bool)
        sub = border[where]
        idx = np.nonzero(touch)
        sub[idx[0][keep], idx[1][keep]] = True
        border[where] = sub
    return ((mask & ~border) * 255).astype(np.uint8)


def face_textures(app, rng, n=6):
    """Front views of a box face (texture px per metre), a few variants of tape and paper placement."""
    s = app.texture_px_per_m
    W, H = int(round(app.box_side_m * s)), int(round(app.box_height_m * s))
    dictionary = cv2.aruco.getPredefinedDictionary(cv2.aruco.DICT_4X4_50)
    mk = int(round(app.marker_size_m * s))
    marker = cv2.aruco.generateImageMarker(dictionary, 0, mk)
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        tex = np.empty((H, W, 3), np.float32)
        tex[:] = np.array(app.box_bgr) * rng.uniform(0.96, 1.0)
        tex += rng.normal(0, 2.0, (H, W, 1)).astype(np.float32)
        for lo, hi in app.tape_bands_m:          # heights from the floor; image rows from the top
            tilt = rng.uniform(-0.006, 0.006)
            for x in range(0, W, 8):
                dz = tilt * (x / W - 0.5)
                r0 = int((app.box_height_m - (hi + dz)) * s)
                r1 = int((app.box_height_m - (lo + dz)) * s)
                tex[max(r0, 0):max(r1, 0), x:x + 8] = np.array(app.tape_bgr) * rng.uniform(0.93, 1.03)
        ps = int(round(app.paper_size_m * s))
        cx = W / 2 + rng.uniform(-0.01, 0.01) * s
        cy = (app.box_height_m - app.marker_centre_height_m) * s + rng.uniform(-0.01, 0.01) * s
        paper = np.full((ps, ps, 3), 246.0, np.float32)
        y0, x0 = (ps - mk) // 2, (ps - mk) // 2
        paper[y0:y0 + mk, x0:x0 + mk] = np.where(marker[..., None] > 127, 240.0, 22.0)
        ang = rng.uniform(-3, 3)
        M = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((ps / 2, ps / 2), ang, 1.0)
        M[0, 2] += cx - ps / 2
        M[1, 2] += cy - ps / 2
        mask = cv2.warpAffine(np.ones((ps, ps), np.float32), M, (W, H))
        warped = cv2.warpAffine(paper, M, (W, H))
        if app.draw_markers:
            tex = tex * (1 - mask[..., None]) + warped * mask[..., None]
        out.append(np.clip(tex, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8))
    return out


def tileable_noise(rng, size=512, scale=24):
    """Smooth random texture in [-1, 1] that wraps around (floor and walls)."""
    small = rng.normal(0, 1, (size // scale, size // scale)).astype(np.float32)
    big = cv2.resize(np.tile(small, (3, 3)), (3 * size, 3 * size), interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)[size:2 * size,
                                                                                                    size:2 * size]
    fine = rng.normal(0, 0.35, (size, size)).astype(np.float32)
    t = big + cv2.GaussianBlur(fine, (3, 3), 0)
    return t / (np.abs(t).max() + 1e-6)


def obstacle_look(app, seed, centre, radius):
    """Random look of one obstacle on the footprint circle (centre, radius) of the scene: a convex footprint of
    one of app.obstacle_shapes inscribed in it, a height, a colour and a surface pattern. Never white with blue
    bands (the look of a box)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    shape = str(rng.choice(app.obstacle_shapes))
    rot = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
    if shape == "cylinder":
        ang = np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 20, endpoint=False)
        rad = np.full(20, radius)
    elif shape == "box":
        phi = rng.uniform(0.35, 1.22)
        ang = np.array([phi, math.pi - phi, math.pi + phi, 2 * math.pi - phi])
        rad = np.full(4, radius)
    elif shape == "prism":
        ang, rad = np.array([0.0, 2.0944, 4.1888]), np.full(3, radius)
    elif shape == "hexagon":
        ang, rad = np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 6, endpoint=False), np.full(6, radius)
    else:                                                  # blob: an irregular convex polygon
        n = int(rng.integers(6, 11))
        ang = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi, n))
        rad = radius * rng.uniform(0.6, 1.0, n)
    pts = np.stack([centre[0] + rad * np.cos(ang + rot), centre[1] + rad * np.sin(ang + rot)], 1)
    hull = cv2.convexHull(np.float32(pts)).reshape(-1, 2).astype(float)
    area = np.sum(hull[:, 0] * np.roll(hull[:, 1], -1) - np.roll(hull[:, 0], -1) * hull[:, 1])
    if area < 0:                                           # counter-clockwise
        hull = hull[::-1]
    height = _u(rng, app.obstacle_height_m)

    def colour(light):
        if light:
            v = rng.uniform(195, 245)
            return np.array([v, v, v]) * (1 + rng.uniform(-0.04, 0.04, 3))
        hsv = np.uint8([[[rng.integers(0, 180), rng.integers(0, 205), rng.integers(35, 225)]]])
        return cv2.cvtColor(hsv, cv2.COLOR_HSV2BGR)[0, 0].astype(float)

    light = rng.random() < app.light_obstacle_share
    base = colour(light)
    second = colour(False)
    if light and second[0] > 1.3 * max(second[1], second[2]):      # no blue on white
        second = second[[2, 1, 0]]
    th = max(16, int(round(64 * height / 0.5)))
    tex = np.empty((th, 128, 3), np.float32)
    tex[:] = base
    pattern = str(rng.choice(["plain", "noise", "stripes", "bands", "checker"]))
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:th, 0:128]
    if pattern == "noise":
        tex *= (1 + 0.12 * rng.normal(0, 1, (th, 128, 1))).astype(np.float32)
    elif pattern == "stripes":
        period = int(rng.integers(8, 32))
        tex[(xx // period) % 2 == 1] = second
    elif pattern == "bands":
        period = int(rng.integers(8, 40))
        tex[(yy // period) % 2 == 1] = second
    elif pattern == "checker":
        period = int(rng.integers(8, 24))
        tex[((xx // period) + (yy // period)) % 2 == 1] = second
    tex += rng.normal(0, 2.0, tex.shape).astype(np.float32)
    top = base * 1.05
    return dict(footprint=hull, height=height, tex=np.clip(tex, 0, 255), top=top)


def part_look(footprint, z0, height, bgr, rng, pattern="noise", second=None):
    """A solid for draw_solid: convex footprint (counter-clockwise), from z0 to z0 + height, colour and pattern."""
    F = np.asarray(footprint, float)
    area = np.sum(F[:, 0] * np.roll(F[:, 1], -1) - np.roll(F[:, 0], -1) * F[:, 1])
    if area < 0:
        F = F[::-1]
    th = max(8, int(round(64 * height / 0.5)))
    tex = np.empty((th, 64, 3), np.float32)
    tex[:] = bgr
    if pattern == "noise":
        tex *= (1 + 0.10 * rng.normal(0, 1, (th, 64, 1))).astype(np.float32)
    elif pattern == "stripes" and second is not None:
        tex[:, (np.arange(64) // 4) % 2 == 1] = second
    elif pattern == "band" and second is not None:
        tex[th // 3: th // 3 + max(1, th // 6)] = second
    return dict(footprint=F, z0=float(z0), height=float(height), tex=np.clip(tex, 0, 255), top=np.asarray(bgr) * 1.08)


def rect(cx, cy, yaw, x0, x1, y0, y1):
    """Rectangle [x0, x1] x [y0, y1] in a frame at (cx, cy, yaw) -> world corners (4, 2), counter-clockwise."""
    c, s = math.cos(yaw), math.sin(yaw)
    pts = np.array([[x0, y0], [x1, y0], [x1, y1], [x0, y1]])
    return np.stack([cx + c * pts[:, 0] - s * pts[:, 1], cy + s * pts[:, 0] + c * pts[:, 1]], 1)


def robot_parts(bc, yaw, rng):
    """A RoboMaster-like robot at body centre bc, heading yaw: chassis, four wheels with rollers, upper body,
    arm and gripper, in dark greys (drawn per robot)."""
    k = rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1)
    dark = lambda lo, hi: np.full(3, rng.uniform(lo, hi)) * (1 + rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05, 3))
    x, y = bc
    parts = [part_look(rect(x, y, yaw, -0.16 * k, 0.16 * k, -0.095 * k, 0.095 * k), 0.035, 0.085, dark(35, 70), rng)]
    for sx in (-1, 1):
        for sy in (-1, 1):
            wx, wy = sx * 0.105 * k, sy * 0.12 * k
            parts.append(part_look(rect(x, y, yaw, wx - 0.05, wx + 0.05, wy - 0.022, wy + 0.022), 0.0, 0.10,
                                   dark(20, 40), rng, "stripes", dark(60, 90)))
    body = dark(30, 65)
    led = np.array([255.0, 150.0, 40.0]) if rng.random() < 0.6 else dark(70, 110)
    parts.append(part_look(rect(x, y, yaw, -0.15 * k, 0.05 * k, -0.08 * k, 0.08 * k), 0.12, rng.uniform(0.06, 0.10),
                           body, rng, "band", led))
    arm = dark(25, 60)
    up = rng.uniform(0.08, 0.13)
    parts.append(part_look(rect(x, y, yaw, 0.0, 0.035, -0.018, 0.018), 0.19, up, arm, rng))
    parts.append(part_look(rect(x, y, yaw, 0.03, 0.15 * k, -0.018, 0.018), 0.17 + up, 0.035, arm, rng))
    parts.append(part_look(rect(x, y, yaw, 0.13 * k, 0.20 * k, -0.04, 0.04), 0.14 + up * 0.6, rng.uniform(0.06, 0.1),
                           dark(20, 50), rng))
    return parts


# ====================================================================
# Renderer
# ====================================================================

class Renderer:
    """scale < 1 renders a smaller image of the same camera (intrinsics scaled), e.g. 0.2 -> 256 x 144 for an
    image-based network; blur and motion-blur sizes are scaled with it."""

    def __init__(self, calib_path, app=None, seed=0, scale=1.0):
        self.cam = Camera(calib_path, scale=scale)
        self.app = app or Appearance()
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.textures = face_textures(self.app, rng)
        self.noise = tileable_noise(rng)
        self.noise_wall = tileable_noise(rng, scale=48)
        mask = cv2.imread(os.path.join(ASSETS, "gripper_mask.png"), cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE)
        grip = cv2.imread(os.path.join(ASSETS, "gripper.png"))
        if mask is not None and grip is not None:
            self.grip_mask = cv2.resize(mask, (self.cam.W, self.cam.H)).astype(np.float32)[..., None] / 255.0
            self.grip = cv2.resize(grip, (self.cam.W, self.cam.H)).astype(np.float32)
        else:
            self.grip_mask = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ room
    def scene_style(self, rng):
        """Appearance drawn once per scene: room, light, cabinets."""
        a = self.app
        L = _u(rng, a.room_half_m)
        cabinets = []
        for wall in range(4):
            for _ in range(int(rng.integers(0, 4))):
                c, w = rng.uniform(-L, L), rng.uniform(0.6, 2.0)
                cabinets.append((wall, c - w / 2, c + w / 2, rng.uniform(0.9, 1.25), rng.uniform(110, 150)))
        light = rng.normal(0, 1, 3)
        light[2] = abs(light[2]) + 0.5
        style = dict(room=L, floor=_u(rng, a.floor_grey), wall=_u(rng, a.wall_grey), cabinets=cabinets,
                     light=light / np.linalg.norm(light), ambient=_u(rng, a.light_ambient))
        if a.obstacle_style == "random":                   # drawn last: "plain" scenes keep their random stream
            style["obstacle_seed"] = int(rng.integers(0, 2 ** 31 - 1))
            style["obstacle_looks"] = {}
        if a.visual_style == "random":
            style["floor"] = rng.uniform(50, 115)
            style["wall"] = rng.uniform(185, 252)
            style["windows"] = []
            for wall in range(4):
                for _ in range(int(rng.integers(0, 4))):
                    c, w = rng.uniform(-L, L), rng.uniform(0.8, 2.5)
                    style["windows"].append((wall, c - w / 2, c + w / 2, rng.uniform(0.7, 1.3), rng.uniform(1.9, 2.6),
                                             rng.uniform(235, 255), rng.uniform(0.4, 1.0)))
            style["spots"] = [(rng.uniform(-L, L), rng.uniform(-L, L), rng.uniform(0.2, 0.9), rng.uniform(0.15, 0.5),
                               rng.uniform(0, math.pi), rng.uniform(60, 190)) for _ in range(int(rng.integers(0, 4)))]
            clutter = []
            for _ in range(int(rng.integers(0, 7))):
                wall = int(rng.integers(0, 4))
                along, depth = rng.uniform(-L + 0.6, L - 0.6), L - rng.uniform(0.35, 0.9)
                cx, cy = [(depth, along), (-depth, along), (along, depth), (along, -depth)][wall]
                yaw = 0.0 if wall < 2 else math.pi / 2
                dw, dd = rng.uniform(0.5, 1.4), rng.uniform(0.3, 0.45)
                top = np.full(3, rng.uniform(90, 230))
                clutter.append(part_look(rect(cx, cy, yaw, -dd, dd, -dw, dw), 0.0, rng.uniform(0.68, 0.8), top * 0.8,
                                         rng))
                if rng.random() < 0.7:
                    clutter.append(part_look(rect(cx, cy, yaw, -0.03, 0.03, -0.25, 0.25), 0.78, rng.uniform(0.3, 0.42),
                                             np.full(3, rng.uniform(15, 40)), rng))
            style["clutter"] = clutter
            style["robot_seed"] = int(rng.integers(0, 2 ** 31 - 1))
            style["robot_looks"] = {}
        return style

    def background(self, C, R, style):
        """Floor, walls and ceiling by ray casting on the canvas."""
        a = self.app
        d = self.cam.rays @ R                              # (Hi, Wi, 3) world directions
        L, h = style["room"], C[2]
        big = 1e9
        tw = np.full(d.shape[:2], big, np.float32)
        wall_id = np.zeros(d.shape[:2], np.int8)
        coord = np.zeros(d.shape[:2], np.float32)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            for k, (axis, sign) in enumerate([(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 1), (1, -1)]):
                t = (sign * L - C[axis]) / d[..., axis]
                ok = (t > 0) & (t < tw)
                tw = np.where(ok, t, tw)
                wall_id = np.where(ok, k, wall_id)
            tf = np.where(d[..., 2] < -1e-6, -h / d[..., 2], big)
        floor = tf < tw
        img = np.empty(d.shape, np.float32)
        # floor
        X = C[0] + tf * d[..., 0]
        Y = C[1] + tf * d[..., 1]
        n = self.noise
        iu = (np.nan_to_num(X) * 100).astype(np.int64) % n.shape[1]
        iv = (np.nan_to_num(Y) * 100).astype(np.int64) % n.shape[0]
        g = style["floor"] * (1 + 0.10 * n[iv, iu])
        joint = (np.abs(((X / 1.0) % 1.0) - 0.5) > 0.497) | (np.abs(((Y / 1.0) % 1.0) - 0.5) > 0.497)
        g = np.where(joint, g * 0.85, g)
        g *= 1 + 0.35 * np.clip((tf - 1.0) / 5.0, 0, 1)          # glancing reflection: far floor looks lighter
        for sx, sy, ra, rb, ang, amp in style.get("spots", []):     # sun or lamp light on the floor
            dx, dy = X - sx, Y - sy
            u = dx * math.cos(ang) + dy * math.sin(ang)
            v = -dx * math.sin(ang) + dy * math.cos(ang)
            g = g + amp * np.exp(-0.5 * ((np.nan_to_num(u) / ra) ** 2 + (np.nan_to_num(v) / rb) ** 2))
        # walls
        Zw = h + tw * d[..., 2]
        along = np.where(wall_id < 2, C[1] + tw * d[..., 1], C[0] + tw * d[..., 0])
        nw = self.noise_wall
        wg = style["wall"] * (1 + 0.04 * nw[(np.nan_to_num(Zw) * 60).astype(np.int64) % nw.shape[0],
                                           (np.nan_to_num(along) * 60).astype(np.int64) % nw.shape[1]])
        for wall, lo, hi, top, grey in style["cabinets"]:
            m = (wall_id == wall) & (along > lo) & (along < hi) & (Zw < top)
            wg = np.where(m, grey, wg)
            wg = np.where(m & (Zw > top - 0.03), grey * 0.7, wg)
        for wall, lo, hi, bottom, top, bright, mull in style.get("windows", []):
            m = (wall_id == wall) & (along > lo) & (along < hi) & (Zw > bottom) & (Zw < top)
            frame = (np.abs(((along - lo) / mull) % 1.0 - 0.5) > 0.47) | (Zw < bottom + 0.04) | (Zw > top - 0.04)
            wg = np.where(m, np.where(frame, 70.0, bright), wg)
        wg = np.where(Zw < 0.08, 150.0, wg)
        wg = np.where(Zw > a.wall_height_m, 228.0, wg)
        val = np.where(floor, g, wg)
        img[..., 0] = val * np.where(floor, 1.0, 0.99)
        img[..., 1] = val
        img[..., 2] = val * np.where(floor, 0.98, 1.0)
        return img

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ objects
    def project(self, P, C, R):
        """World points (N, 3) -> canvas pixels (N, 2) and depth (N,)."""
        pc = (np.asarray(P, float) - C) @ R.T
        z = pc[:, 2]
        uv = (pc[:, :2] / np.maximum(z[:, None], 1e-6)) * [self.cam.Ki[0, 0], self.cam.Ki[1, 1]] + \
            [self.cam.Ki[0, 2], self.cam.Ki[1, 2]]
        return uv, z, pc

    def draw_textured_quad(self, img, tex, quad_uv, shade):
        x0, y0 = np.floor(quad_uv.min(0)).astype(int)
        x1, y1 = np.ceil(quad_uv.max(0)).astype(int)
        x0, y0 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0)
        x1, y1 = min(x1, self.cam.Wi - 1), min(y1, self.cam.Hi - 1)
        if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0:
            return
        h, w = tex.shape[:2]
        src = np.float32([[0, 0], [w, 0], [w, h], [0, h]])
        dst = np.float32(quad_uv - [x0, y0])
        Hm = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(src, dst)
        size = (x1 - x0 + 1, y1 - y0 + 1)
        warped = cv2.warpPerspective(tex, Hm, size, flags=cv2.INTER_LINEAR,
                                     borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE).astype(np.float32)
        mask = np.zeros((size[1], size[0]), np.float32)
        cv2.fillConvexPoly(mask, np.round(dst * 16).astype(np.int32), 1.0, lineType=cv2.LINE_AA, shift=4)
        roi = img[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1]
        roi[:] = roi * (1 - mask[..., None]) + warped * shade * mask[..., None]

    def draw_polygon(self, img, uv, bgr):
        hull = cv2.convexHull(np.float32(uv)).reshape(-1, 2)
        cv2.fillConvexPoly(img, np.round(hull * 16).astype(np.int32), [float(c) for c in bgr],
                           lineType=cv2.LINE_AA, shift=4)

    def draw_solid(self, img, look, C, R, style):
        """A vertical prism on a convex footprint: the side faces that face the camera (far ones first),
        textured and lit, then the top if the camera is above it."""
        F, tex = look["footprint"], look["tex"]
        z0 = look.get("z0", 0.0)
        h = z0 + look["height"]
        n = len(F)
        edges = np.linalg.norm(np.roll(F, -1, 0) - F, axis=1)
        cum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(edges)]) / max(edges.sum(), 1e-9)
        W = tex.shape[1]
        faces = []
        for i in range(n):
            p, q = F[i], F[(i + 1) % n]
            d = q - p
            nv = np.array([d[1], -d[0]]) / max(np.hypot(*d), 1e-9)          # outward for counter-clockwise
            mid = (p + q) / 2
            if np.dot(nv, C[:2] - mid) <= 0:
                continue
            faces.append((float(np.hypot(*(mid - C[:2]))), i, p, q, nv))
        faces.sort(key=lambda f: -f[0])
        for _, i, p, q, nv in faces:
            quad = np.array([[*p, h], [*q, h], [*q, z0], [*p, z0]])
            uv, z, _ = self.project(quad, C, R)
            if (z < 0.05).any():
                continue
            c0 = int(cum[i] * W)
            c1 = max(c0 + 2, int(cum[i + 1] * W))
            n3 = np.array([nv[0], nv[1], 0.0])
            shade = style["ambient"] + (1 - style["ambient"]) * max(0.0, float(n3 @ style["light"]))
            self.draw_textured_quad(img, np.ascontiguousarray(tex[:, c0:min(c1, W)]), uv, shade)
        if C[2] > h:
            top = np.column_stack([F, np.full(n, h)])
            uv, z, _ = self.project(top, C, R)
            if (z > 0.05).all():
                shade = style["ambient"] + (1 - style["ambient"]) * max(0.0, float(style["light"][2]))
                self.draw_polygon(img, uv, look["top"] * shade)

    def marker_map(self, markers, ids, rng):
        """The markers a robot detects in this image, as filled rectangles (255) on black: the second channel of
        the masks with marker_channel, as bevnet/real.py draws the ArUco detections of the real frames. A
        marker is detected only if its centre is not hidden by something in front, with a probability that
        falls with the viewing angle (0.93 up to 55 degrees, 0 at 75) and beyond 1.8 m (0 at 2.6 m): in the
        real campaigns no marker was detected farther than about 2.5 m."""
        a = self.app
        out = np.zeros((self.cam.H, self.cam.W), np.float32)
        c55, c75 = math.cos(math.radians(55)), math.cos(math.radians(75))
        for mk in markers:
            u, v = int(round(mk["u"])), int(round(mk["v"]))
            if not (0 <= u < self.cam.W and 0 <= v < self.cam.H):
                continue
            if ids is not None and int(round(float(ids[v, u]))) != mk["box"] + 1:
                continue                                    # the marker centre is hidden
            p = 0.93 * min(max((mk["cos"] - c75) / (c55 - c75), 0.0), 1.0) * min(max((2.6 - mk["depth"]) / 0.8, 0.0), 1.0)
            if rng.random() >= p:
                continue
            side = self.cam.K[0, 0] * a.marker_size_m / mk["depth"]
            hw, hh = max(0.5 * side * mk["cos"], 0.5), max(0.5 * side, 0.5)
            cv2.rectangle(out, (int(round(u - hw)), int(round(v - hh))), (int(round(u + hw)), int(round(v + hh))),
                          255.0, -1)
        return out

    def render(self, scene, k, rng, style=None):
        """Image of capture k of scene (sim.scene.Scene), the markers drawn in it and the camera settings.
        Returns (BGR uint8 image, [dict(box, face, u, v, depth)], dict(pitch_deg, roll_deg, height_m)); with
        mask_only the dict also has box_pixels: per box, how many pixels of it are visible in the image."""
        clean, markers, info = self.render_clean(scene, k, rng, style)
        return self.camera_effects(clean, rng), markers, info

    def render_clean(self, scene, k, rng, style=None):
        """As render, but the image before the camera effects (float BGR): several readings of one stop are
        camera_effects() of the same clean image, as a robot standing still takes them."""
        a = self.app
        style = style or self.scene_style(rng)
        x, y, yaw = scene.captures[k].pose
        pitch, roll = math.radians(_u(rng, a.pitch_deg)), math.radians(_u(rng, a.roll_deg))
        C = np.array([x, y, a.camera_height_m])
        R = camera_rotation(yaw, pitch, roll)
        m = a.mask_only
        img = np.zeros((self.cam.Hi, self.cam.Wi, 3), np.float32) if m else self.background(C, R, style)
        objects = []                       # (depth, kind, data)
        half = a.box_side_m / 2
        apothem = a.box_side_m / (2 * math.sqrt(3))       # centre to face of the triangle of side box_side_m
        for j, (c, th) in enumerate(zip(scene.boxes, scene.thetas)):
            for f in range(3):
                nrm = face_normal(th, f)
                nv = np.array([math.cos(nrm), math.sin(nrm)])
                fc = np.asarray(c, float) + apothem * nv
                if np.dot(nv, np.array([x, y]) - fc) <= 0:          # back face
                    continue
                t = np.array([-nv[1], nv[0]])
                left, right = fc - t * half, fc + t * half
                quad = np.array([[*left, a.box_height_m], [*right, a.box_height_m], [*right, 0.0], [*left, 0.0]])
                depth = float(np.hypot(*(np.asarray(c) - [x, y])))
                objects.append((depth + 0.01 * f, "face", (j, f, quad, nv, fc)))
        white = style.setdefault("white_obstacles", {})  # mask_only: obstacles a segmentation takes for boxes
        for q, poly in enumerate(scene.obstacles):
            poly = np.asarray(poly, float)
            oc, r = poly.mean(0), float(np.max(np.hypot(*(poly - poly.mean(0)).T)))
            if q not in white:                              # decided once per scene, the same for every robot
                white[q] = bool(a.white_obstacle_share > 0 and rng.random() < a.white_obstacle_share)
            if "obstacle_seed" in style:                   # the same look from every robot of the scene
                looks = style["obstacle_looks"]
                if q not in looks:
                    looks[q] = obstacle_look(a, style["obstacle_seed"] + 7_919 * q, oc, r)
                objects.append((float(np.hypot(*(oc - [x, y]))), "solid", dict(looks[q], white=white[q])))
            else:
                objects.append((float(np.hypot(*(oc - [x, y]))), "cylinder", (oc, r, white[q])))
        for part in style.get("clutter", []):
            objects.append((float(np.hypot(*(part["footprint"].mean(0) - [x, y]))), "solid", part))
        if a.draw_robots and "robot_seed" in style:
            looks = style["robot_looks"]
            for q, cap in enumerate(scene.captures):
                if q == k:
                    continue
                if q not in looks:
                    qx, qy, qyaw = cap.pose
                    bc = np.array([qx, qy]) - a.robot_body_behind_m * np.array([math.cos(qyaw), math.sin(qyaw)])
                    looks[q] = robot_parts(bc, qyaw, np.random.default_rng(style["robot_seed"] + 104_729 * q))
                for part in looks[q]:
                    objects.append((float(np.hypot(*(part["footprint"].mean(0) - [x, y]))), "solid", part))
        elif a.draw_robots:
            L_, W_, H_ = a.robot_size_m
            for q, cap in enumerate(scene.captures):
                if q == k:
                    continue
                qx, qy, qyaw = cap.pose
                bc = np.array([qx, qy]) - a.robot_body_behind_m * np.array([math.cos(qyaw), math.sin(qyaw)])
                objects.append((float(np.hypot(*(bc - [x, y]))), "robot", (bc, qyaw, L_, W_, H_)))
        objects.sort(key=lambda o: -o[0])
        markers = []
        for depth, kind, data in objects:
            if kind == "face":
                j, f, quad, nv, fc = data
                uv, z, _ = self.project(quad, C, R)
                if (z < 0.05).any():
                    continue
                n3 = np.array([nv[0], nv[1], 0.0])
                shade = style["ambient"] + (1 - style["ambient"]) * max(0.0, float(n3 @ style["light"]))
                if m:                                      # white, with the box number in the second channel
                    self.draw_polygon(img, uv, [255.0, float(j + 1), 0.0])
                else:
                    tex = self.textures[(j * 3 + f) % len(self.textures)]
                    self.draw_textured_quad(img, tex, uv, shade)
                mc = np.array([[fc[0], fc[1], a.marker_centre_height_m]])
                _, mz, mpc = self.project(mc, C, R)
                to_cam = np.array([x, y]) - fc
                markers.append(dict(box=j, face=f, pc=mpc[0], depth=float(mz[0]),
                                    cos=float(nv @ to_cam / max(np.linalg.norm(to_cam), 1e-9))))
            elif kind == "cylinder":
                oc, r, is_white = data
                ang = np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 32, endpoint=False)
                ring = np.stack([oc[0] + r * np.cos(ang), oc[1] + r * np.sin(ang)], 1)
                pts = np.vstack([np.column_stack([ring, np.zeros(32)]),
                                 np.column_stack([ring, np.full(32, a.plain_obstacle_height_m)])])
                uv, z, _ = self.project(pts, C, R)
                if (z < 0.05).any():
                    continue
                self.draw_polygon(img, uv, ([255.0, 0.0, 0.0] if is_white else np.zeros(3)) if m
                                  else np.array([150.0, 155.0, 160.0]) * style["ambient"] * 1.1)
            elif kind == "solid":
                if m and data.get("white"):                # its whole outline white, no box number
                    F = np.asarray(data["footprint"], float)
                    z0 = data.get("z0", 0.0)
                    pts = np.vstack([np.column_stack([F, np.full(len(F), z0)]),
                                     np.column_stack([F, np.full(len(F), z0 + data["height"])])])
                    uv, z, _ = self.project(pts, C, R)
                    if (z > 0.05).all():
                        self.draw_polygon(img, uv, [255.0, 0.0, 0.0])
                    continue
                if m:
                    data = dict(data, tex=np.zeros_like(data["tex"]), top=np.zeros(3))
                self.draw_solid(img, data, C, R, style)
            else:
                bc, qyaw, L_, W_, H_ = data
                fwd = np.array([math.cos(qyaw), math.sin(qyaw)])
                side = np.array([-fwd[1], fwd[0]])
                corners = [bc + sx * fwd * L_ / 2 + sy * side * W_ / 2 for sx in (-1, 1) for sy in (-1, 1)]
                pts = np.array([[*p, zz] for p in corners for zz in (0.02, H_)])
                uv, z, _ = self.project(pts, C, R)
                if (z < 0.05).any():
                    continue
                self.draw_polygon(img, uv, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] if m else [42.0, 40.0, 40.0])
                top = np.array([[*p, H_] for p in corners])
                tuv, _, _ = self.project(top, C, R)
                self.draw_polygon(img, tuv, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] if m else [70.0, 68.0, 66.0])
                for sy in ([] if m else (-1, 1)):
                    led = np.array([[*(bc + fwd * L_ / 2 + sy * side * W_ / 4), H_ * 0.6]])
                    luv, lz, _ = self.project(led, C, R)
                    if lz[0] > 0.05 and np.dot(fwd, np.array([x, y]) - bc) > 0:
                        cv2.circle(img, tuple(int(v) for v in luv[0]), max(1, int(6 / max(lz[0], 0.3))),
                                   (255.0, 170.0, 60.0), -1, lineType=cv2.LINE_AA)
        # through the lens
        out = cv2.remap(img, self.cam.map_x, self.cam.map_y, cv2.INTER_LINEAR, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
        box_pixels = None
        ids = None
        if m:
            white = out[..., 0] > 127.0
            ids = cv2.remap(img[..., 1], self.cam.map_x, self.cam.map_y, cv2.INTER_NEAREST,
                            borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
            box_pixels = np.bincount(np.round(ids[white]).astype(int).clip(0, len(scene.boxes)),
                                     minlength=len(scene.boxes) + 1)[1:].tolist()
            if a.instance_borders:                         # boxes that touch in the image stay apart
                labels = np.where(white, np.round(ids).astype(np.int32).clip(0, len(scene.boxes)), 0)
                white = (separate_instances(labels, rng, a.border_merge_prob) > 0) | (white & (labels == 0))
            out = np.repeat(np.where(white, 255.0, 0.0).astype(np.float32)[..., None], 3, axis=2)
        elif a.draw_gripper and self.grip_mask is not None:
            out = out * (1 - self.grip_mask) + self.grip * self.grip_mask
        # where the markers fell in the image
        if markers:
            pc = np.array([m["pc"] for m in markers], np.float64)
            uv, _ = cv2.projectPoints(pc.reshape(-1, 1, 3), np.zeros(3), np.zeros(3), self.cam.K, self.cam.D)
            for m, p in zip(markers, uv.reshape(-1, 2)):
                m["u"], m["v"] = float(p[0]), float(p[1])
                m.pop("pc")
        markers = [m for m in markers if m["depth"] > 0 and 0 <= m["u"] < self.cam.W and 0 <= m["v"] < self.cam.H]
        if a.mask_only and a.marker_channel:
            out[..., 1] = self.marker_map(markers, ids, rng)
        info = dict(pitch_deg=round(math.degrees(pitch), 2), roll_deg=round(math.degrees(roll), 2),
                    height_m=a.camera_height_m)
        if box_pixels is not None:
            info["box_pixels"] = box_pixels
        return out, markers, info

    def camera_effects(self, img, rng):
        a = self.app
        if a.mask_only:                                    # masks: no camera effects
            return np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
        img = img * _u(rng, a.exposure) * (1 + rng.uniform(-a.white_balance, a.white_balance, 3))
        img = img * (1 - a.vignetting * self.cam.radius2[..., None])
        s = _u(rng, a.defocus_sigma_px) * self.cam.scale
        if s > 0.05:
            img = cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (0, 0), s)
        n = int(round(int(rng.integers(a.motion_blur_px[0], a.motion_blur_px[1] + 1)) * self.cam.scale))
        if rng.random() < a.motion_blur_share and n >= 2:
            kern = np.zeros((n, n), np.float32)
            kern[n // 2, :] = 1.0 / n
            M = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((n / 2 - 0.5, n / 2 - 0.5), rng.uniform(-20, 20), 1.0)
            kern = cv2.warpAffine(kern, M, (n, n))
            img = cv2.filter2D(img, -1, kern / max(kern.sum(), 1e-6))
        img = img + rng.normal(0, _u(rng, a.noise_sd), img.shape).astype(np.float32)
        img = np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
        q = int(rng.integers(a.jpeg_quality[0], a.jpeg_quality[1] + 1))
        ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, q])
        return cv2.imdecode(buf, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)

==> ./imgsim/generate.py <==
"""Image-level sets: the scenes of sim/plan.py rendered (imgsim/render.py) and passed through the real ArUco
detector (vf/perception/aruco_detector.py, marker 77 mm, the robot's calibration), written in the format of
the real runs.

Every scene is drawn by sim.plan.plan_scene with the same seed as in the measurement-level set of the same
name, so scene i of data/imgsim/<set>/ has the same boxes, obstacles and robot poses as scene i of
data/plan/<set>/. What changes is where the reports come from: here a marker is reported when the detector
finds it in the rendered image, and its distance, bearing and viewing angle come from solvePnP, exactly as on
the robots; there they are drawn from the fitted sensor model. As on the robots, every stop takes 5 frames
and keeps one detection per group of detections closer than 0.2 m (acquisition/static_trial.capture_trial);
so the two faces of one box, about 15 cm apart, mostly become one report, as in the real runs. The reports are RAW values, as in the real
runs: imgsim/compare.py fits their range and bearing calibration on the set (as pipeline/calibrate.py does for
the real runs) and writes it as <set>/sensor_calib.json, to be passed as --sensor-calib to every reader.

Each detection is labelled with the marker it comes from (sim_box, sim_face) when its centre lies close to
the projected centre of a drawn marker, otherwise -1 (a false detection). The renderer has no source of false
detections beyond what the detector produces on its own.

Output per set (--out/<set>/): part*/ with P<k>.jsonl, ground_truth.json, runs.csv, geometry.jsonl (as
sim/plan.py), captures.jsonl (per capture: pitch, roll, markers drawn and detected), appearance.json, and
images/<run>_P<k>.jpg for the first --save-images scenes (--save-images -1: every scene, e.g. for training an
image model).

    python -m imgsim.generate --sets G0_nominal_circle --runs 200 --save-images 20
    python -m imgsim.generate --sets G0,E1,E3,S1 --runs 1000 --jobs 30
"""

import argparse
import copy
import csv
import json
import logging
import math
import multiprocessing
import os
import shutil
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict

import cv2
import numpy as np

from imgsim.render import Appearance, Renderer
from sim.model import SensorModel
from sim.plan import PlanSpec, plan_scene, run_model, select, set_table
from sim.writer import write_run

PART = 250
CALIB = dict(P0="config/checkerboard_calib_P0.json", P1="config/checkerboard_calib_P1.json")


def detect(detector, img):
    """[(distance, bearing, viewing angle, u, v, size)] of the markers the real detector finds."""
    out = []
    for _cls, _conf, bbox, (dist, bearing, view) in detector.detect_with_pose(img):
        x, y, w, h = bbox
        out.append((float(dist), float(bearing), float(view), x + w / 2, y + h / 2, max(w, h)))
    return out


def one_stop(renderer, detector, scene, k, rng, style, readings, threshold):
    """What a robot standing at capture k reports, as acquisition/static_trial.capture_trial does on the robot:
    `readings` frames (the same view, new sensor noise, blur and compression), the detections of all of
    them grouped by position (vf.perception.object_position.cluster_by_position, --instance-threshold-m of the
    real runs), and one detection per group, the one whose distance is closest to the group median.
    Returns (reports, first frame, markers drawn, camera settings)."""
    from vf.perception.object_position import cluster_by_position
    clean, markers, info = renderer.render_clean(scene, k, rng, style)
    x, y, yaw = scene.captures[k].pose
    found, first = [], None
    for r in range(readings):
        img = renderer.camera_effects(clean, rng)
        first = img if first is None else first
        found += label(detect(detector, img), markers)
    if not found:
        return [], first, markers, info
    pos = [(x + d["distance"] * math.cos(yaw - d["bearing"]), y + d["distance"] * math.sin(yaw - d["bearing"]))
           for d in found]
    groups = {}
    for d, g in zip(found, cluster_by_position(pos, threshold_m=threshold)):
        groups.setdefault(g, []).append(d)
    reports = []
    for g in groups.values():
        med = float(np.median([d["distance"] for d in g]))
        reports.append(min(g, key=lambda d: abs(d["distance"] - med)))
    return reports, first, markers, info


def label(dets, markers):
    """Box and face of every detection: the nearest drawn marker centre within its size (else -1)."""
    out = []
    for dist, bearing, view, u, v, size in dets:
        best, bd = None, max(12.0, 0.6 * size)
        for m in markers:
            d = math.hypot(m["u"] - u, m["v"] - v)
            if d < bd:
                best, bd = m, d
        out.append(dict(distance=dist, bearing=bearing, view=view,
                        box=best["box"] if best else -1, face=best["face"] if best else -1))
    return out


def generate_part(task):
    (name, spec_dict, runs, start, seed, part_dir, model_path, app_dict, calib, save_images, set_dir, readings,
     threshold) = task
    logging.disable(logging.WARNING)
    from vf.perception.aruco_detector import ArucoDetector, load_calibration
    spec = PlanSpec(**spec_dict)
    model = SensorModel.load(model_path)
    m = run_model(model, spec)
    app = Appearance(**app_dict)
    renderer = Renderer(calib, app, seed=seed)
    K, D = load_calibration(calib)
    detector = ArucoDetector(app.marker_size_m, K, D)
    writer_model = copy.deepcopy(model)
    writer_model.camera_offset_m = 0.0
    os.makedirs(part_dir, exist_ok=True)
    img_dir = os.path.join(set_dir, "images")
    truth, rows, geometry, caps = {}, [], [], []
    for i in range(start, start + runs):
        scene_seed = seed * 1_000_003 + i                   # the seed of sim/plan.py for this scene
        rng = np.random.default_rng(scene_seed)
        family = spec.families[i % len(spec.families)]
        scene, meta = plan_scene(spec, family, rng, name, f"{name}_{i:05d}", m)
        rrng = np.random.default_rng(scene_seed + 7_919)    # rendering draws, independent of the layout
        style = renderer.scene_style(rrng)
        detections = {}
        for k in range(len(scene.captures)):
            dets, img, markers, info = one_stop(renderer, detector, scene, k, rrng, style, readings, threshold)
            detections[k] = dets
            caps.append(dict(run=scene.run_id, robot=scene.captures[k].robot, **info,
                             markers_drawn=len(markers), detections=len(dets),
                             false=sum(d["box"] < 0 for d in dets)))
            if save_images < 0 or i < save_images:
                os.makedirs(img_dir, exist_ok=True)
                cv2.imwrite(os.path.join(img_dir, f"{scene.run_id}_{scene.captures[k].robot}.jpg"), img,
                            [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 92])
        truth.update(write_run(part_dir, scene, detections, writer_model, folder=f"{name}_{i // 500:04d}"))
        rows.append(dict(run=scene.run_id, seed=scene_seed, **meta))
        geometry.append(dict(run=scene.run_id, boxes=scene.boxes.round(4).tolist(),
                             yaws=[round(float(t), 5) for t in scene.thetas],
                             obstacles=[o.round(4).tolist() for o in scene.obstacles],
                             poses=[[round(float(v), 5) for v in c.pose] for c in scene.captures]))
    for fname, data in (("ground_truth.json", truth),):
        with open(os.path.join(part_dir, fname), "w") as f:
            json.dump(data, f)
    for fname, items in (("geometry.jsonl", geometry), ("captures.jsonl", caps)):
        with open(os.path.join(part_dir, fname), "w") as f:
            for g in items:
                f.write(json.dumps(g) + "\n")
    with open(os.path.join(part_dir, "runs.csv"), "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    return name, part_dir


def merge(set_dir, part_dirs):
    truth, rows = {}, []
    with open(os.path.join(set_dir, "geometry.jsonl"), "w") as g, \
            open(os.path.join(set_dir, "captures.jsonl"), "w") as c:
        for d in sorted(part_dirs):
            with open(os.path.join(d, "ground_truth.json")) as f:
                truth.update(json.load(f))
            with open(os.path.join(d, "runs.csv")) as f:
                rows += list(csv.DictReader(f))
            for name, out in (("geometry.jsonl", g), ("captures.jsonl", c)):
                with open(os.path.join(d, name)) as f:
                    out.write(f.read())
            for name in ("ground_truth.json", "runs.csv", "geometry.jsonl", "captures.jsonl"):
                os.remove(os.path.join(d, name))
    with open(os.path.join(set_dir, "ground_truth.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(truth, f)
    with open(os.path.join(set_dir, "runs.csv"), "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["run"]))
    return len(rows)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--sets", required=True, help="as sim.plan --sets: scenario IDs, set names, tests, train, ...")
    ap.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=None, help="scenes per set (default: as in sim/plan.py)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="config/sensor_model.json", help="only for the scene layout (field of view)")
    ap.add_argument("--camera", choices=sorted(CALIB), default="P0", help="calibration of the rendered camera")
    ap.add_argument("--appearance", default=None, help="JSON with Appearance fields to change (imgsim/render.py)")
    ap.add_argument("--save-images", type=int, default=20, help="save the images of the first N scenes (-1: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--readings", type=int, default=5, help="frames per stop (survey.py --n-readings)")
    ap.add_argument("--instance-threshold", type=float, default=0.2,
                    help="detections of one stop closer than this are one report (--instance-threshold-m of the "
                         "real runs) [m]")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/imgsim/")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1, help="as sim.plan --seed (same seeds = same scenes)")
    ap.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 1))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        a.jobs = min(a.jobs, 60)
    big = 10 ** 9
    table = set_table(argparse.Namespace(train_runs=big, gate_runs=big, val_runs=big, test_runs=big, seed=a.seed))
    plan_runs = dict(train=50000, gate=10000, val=2000)
    chosen = select(table, a.sets)
    if not chosen:
        raise SystemExit(f"no set matches {a.sets} (see python -m sim.plan --list)")
    app = Appearance.load(a.appearance)
    tasks, parts = [], {}
    for name, spec, _, seed, sid, level, family in chosen:
        runs = a.runs or plan_runs.get(name, 1000)
        set_dir = os.path.join(a.out, name)
        if os.path.isdir(set_dir):
            shutil.rmtree(set_dir)
        os.makedirs(set_dir)
        app.save(os.path.join(set_dir, "appearance.json"))
        with open(os.path.join(set_dir, "spec.json"), "w") as f:
            json.dump(dict(asdict(spec), scenario=sid, level=level, seed=a.seed * 1000 + seed, camera=a.camera), f,
                      indent=2)
        for k, start in enumerate(range(0, runs, PART)):
            part_dir = os.path.join(set_dir, f"part{k:03d}")
            tasks.append((name, asdict(spec), min(PART, runs - start), start, a.seed * 1000 + seed, part_dir, a.model,
                          asdict(app), CALIB[a.camera], a.save_images, set_dir, a.readings, a.instance_threshold))
            parts.setdefault(name, []).append(part_dir)
    print(f"{len(chosen)} set(s), {sum(t[2] for t in tasks)} scenes: {len(tasks)} parts on "
          f"{min(a.jobs, len(tasks))} process(es)", flush=True)
    with multiprocessing.Pool(min(a.jobs, len(tasks))) as pool:
        for name, done in pool.imap_unordered(generate_part, tasks):
            print(f"  {done}", flush=True)
    for name in parts:
        n = merge(os.path.join(a.out, name), parts[name])
        print(f"  {name}: {n} scenes", flush=True)
    print("next: python -m imgsim.compare --set-dir <set> (fits the range / bearing calibration of the set)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./imgsim/__init__.py <==
"""Image-level simulator: renders the camera image of every robot in a scene of sim/plan.py, runs the real
ArUco detector on it and writes the reports in the format of the real runs (imgsim/render.py,
imgsim/generate.py, imgsim/compare.py)."""

==> ./imgsim/compare.py <==
"""Compares the image-level reports (imgsim/generate.py) with the sensor file fitted on the real runs, i.e. checks
the measurement-level simulator against the images.

On one set of imgsim/generate.py:
  1. range and bearing calibration of the set, as pipeline/calibrate.py does for the real runs
     (d_meas = A d_true + B, b_meas = k b_true + b0 on the reports of a true box; residual spread; P_D of the
     boxes in range and field of view), written as <set>/sensor_calib.json and compared with the real one
     (config/sensor_calib.json)
  2. with that calibration, the checks of module M1 (sim/plan_check.py) with the image reports in place of the
     simulated ones: position error along and across the line of sight per distance, detection probability per
     viewing angle and per distance, two-face rate, false detections per capture, each against the sensor file
     (config/sensor_model.json, fitted on 607 real reports)
  3. real frames (data/survey_rounds/*/frames) next to rendered ones
Outputs in --out: fig_IMG-1_position_error.png, fig_IMG-2_detection.png, fig_IMG-3_frames.png, table_IMG.csv.

    python -m imgsim.compare --set-dir data/imgsim/G0_nominal_circle/ --out results/imgsim/G0_nominal_circle/
"""

import argparse
import csv
import glob
import json
import math
import os

import numpy as np

from gnn.dataset import build_scenes, read_records
from sim.model import SensorModel
from sim.plan_check import binned, detection_pairs, mean_se, plot_detection, plot_position, position_errors


def fit_calibration(set_dir, hfov_deg=88.0, r_max=3.0):
    """Range and bearing fit of the raw reports of a true box, as pipeline/calibrate.py (camera offset 0)."""
    with open(os.path.join(set_dir, "ground_truth.json")) as f:
        truth = json.load(f)
    d_t, d_m, b_t, b_m = [], [], [], []
    for r in read_records(set_dir):
        j = r.get("sim_box")
        if j is None or j < 0:
            continue
        x, y, yaw = r["robot_pose"]
        bx = truth[r["run_id"]][j]
        dx, dy = bx["x"] - x, bx["y"] - y
        d_t.append(math.hypot(dx, dy))
        b_t.append((yaw - math.atan2(dy, dx) + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi)
        d_m.append(float(r["distance"]))
        b_m.append(float(r["bearing_rad"]))
    d_t, d_m, b_t, b_m = map(np.array, (d_t, d_m, b_t, b_m))
    A, B = np.polyfit(d_t, d_m, 1)
    k, b0 = np.polyfit(b_t, b_m, 1)
    sd = float(np.std(d_m - (A * d_t + B)))
    sl = float(np.std((b_m - (k * b_t + b0)) * d_t))
    return dict(range_fit=[round(float(A), 4), round(float(B), 4)], bearing_fit=[round(float(k), 4), round(float(b0), 5)],
                sigma_pos=round(math.sqrt((sd ** 2 + sl ** 2) / 2), 4), camera_offset=0.0,
                residual_distance_m=round(sd, 4), residual_lateral_m=round(sl, 4), detections=int(len(d_t)),
                source=os.path.abspath(set_dir))


def frames_figure(set_dir, out, plt, rng):
    import cv2
    real = sorted(glob.glob("data/survey_rounds/L*/frames/*/*.jpg"))
    synth = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(set_dir, "images", "*.jpg")))
    if not real or not synth:
        return False
    picks = [real[i] for i in rng.choice(len(real), 3, replace=False)] + \
            [synth[i] for i in rng.choice(len(synth), 3, replace=False)]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 5.6))
    for a, p, title in zip(ax.flat, picks, ["real"] * 3 + ["rendered"] * 3):
        a.imshow(cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(p), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))
        a.set_title(f"{title}: {os.path.basename(p)}", fontsize=8)
        a.axis("off")
    fig.suptitle("Fig. IMG-3: real robot frames (top) and rendered frames (bottom)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(out, "fig_IMG-3_frames.png"), dpi=100)
    plt.close(fig)
    return True


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--set-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="config/sensor_model.json", help="sensor file fitted on the real runs")
    ap.add_argument("--real-calib", default="config/sensor_calib.json")
    ap.add_argument("--detection-scenes", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="default results/imgsim/<set>/")
    ap.add_argument("--save-calib", default=None,
                    help="also write the calibration here (e.g. config/sensor_calib_imgsim.json, for every image set "
                         "rendered with the same camera)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(a.set_dir))
    out = a.out or os.path.join("results", "imgsim", name)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    model = SensorModel.load(a.model)

    calib = fit_calibration(a.set_dir, model.hfov_deg, model.r_max_m)
    calib_path = os.path.join(a.set_dir, "sensor_calib.json")
    for path in [calib_path] + ([a.save_calib] if a.save_calib else []):
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(calib, f, indent=2)
    with open(a.real_calib) as f:
        real = json.load(f)
    rows = [dict(quantity="range fit A (d_meas = A d_true + B)", real=real["range_fit"][0], images=calib["range_fit"][0]),
            dict(quantity="range fit B [m]", real=real["range_fit"][1], images=calib["range_fit"][1]),
            dict(quantity="bearing fit k", real=real["bearing_fit"][0], images=calib["bearing_fit"][0]),
            dict(quantity="bearing fit b0 [rad]", real=real["bearing_fit"][1], images=calib["bearing_fit"][1]),
            dict(quantity="residual distance sd [m]", real=real.get("residual_distance_m"),
                 images=calib["residual_distance_m"]),
            dict(quantity="residual lateral sd [m]", real=real.get("residual_lateral_m"),
                 images=calib["residual_lateral_m"])]

    with open(os.path.join(a.set_dir, "geometry.jsonl")) as f:
        geometry = {g["run"]: g for g in map(json.loads, f)}
    scenes = build_scenes(a.set_dir, os.path.join(a.set_dir, "ground_truth.json"), calib_path)
    err = position_errors(scenes)
    plot_position(err, model, os.path.join(out, "fig_IMG-1_position_error.png"), plt, points="images",
                  title="Fig. IMG-1: position error of the reports detected in the rendered images, against the "
                        "sensor file fitted on the real runs")
    pairs = detection_pairs(scenes[:a.detection_scenes], geometry, model)
    plot_detection(pairs, os.path.join(out, "fig_IMG-2_detection.png"), plt, points="images",
                   title="Fig. IMG-2: detection probability in the rendered images, against the sensor file fitted "
                         "on the real runs")
    captures = sum(len(geometry[s["run"]]["poses"]) for s in scenes)
    false = sum(int((s["label"] < 0).sum()) for s in scenes)
    rows += [dict(quantity="P_D, (robot, box) pairs in view", real=round(float(pairs[:, 2].mean()), 4),
                  images=round(float(pairs[:, 4].mean()), 4)),
             dict(quantity="two-face rate, per pair in view", real=round(float(pairs[:, 3].mean()), 4),
                  images=round(float(pairs[:, 5].mean()), 4)),
             dict(quantity="false detections per capture", real=model.false_rate, images=round(false / captures, 4)),
             dict(quantity="reports per scene", real="", images=round(float(np.mean([len(s["pos"]) for s in scenes])), 2))]
    with open(os.path.join(out, "table_IMG.csv"), "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["quantity", "real", "images"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    frames_figure(a.set_dir, out, plt, np.random.default_rng(0))
    print(f"{len(scenes)} scenes, {sum(len(s['pos']) for s in scenes)} reports; calibration written to {calib_path}")
    print(f"  {'quantity':<42}{'real / sensor file':>20}{'images':>12}")
    for r in rows:
        print(f"  {r['quantity']:<42}{str(r['real']):>20}{str(r['images']):>12}")
    print(f"written to {out}")

    main()

==> ./acquisition/survey.py <==
"""Autonomous survey of a static scene: ONE robot drives by itself through a
list of stops around the boxes, and at every stop it captures what its
camera sees, exactly like static_trial.py.

To start all the robots with one command: launch_all.py (it runs this
script once per robot, at the same time).

Why the robots do not need to be synchronised
---------------------------------------------
The boxes do not move, so what robot i sees from stop k is valid at any
time. Every stop is an independent OBSERVATION POINT (observations +
camera pose). The scans that the localization methods are tested on are
composed afterwards, offline, by pipeline/build_scans.py, choosing which
observation points to put together (also more "virtual robots" than the
real ones).

Stops
-----
Rings around the centre of the box layout (--radii), one stop every
--step-deg degrees, the robot facing the centre (plus --yaw-offsets-deg:
extra captures at the same stop with the camera turned left/right, so the
boxes also fall near the edge of the field of view). Each robot starts
the rings at its own angle (--start-deg, e.g. 0 / 120 / 240 for three
robots) and all go round in the same direction, so they stay apart.
Stops closer than --margin to the arena border are skipped. The centre
of the rings comes from the ground truth of the layout
(tools/record_ground_truth.py). Paths: straight to the next stop when the
line stays at least --keep-out-m from every box, otherwise round the
layout on an arc, in the direction whose waypoints all stay inside the
arena (minus --margin); a stop with no such path is skipped.

Safety
------
Speed limit, per-stop timeout, stop when the OptiTrack pose is lost (the
robot watchdog stops it without commands), geofence (the robot is stopped
as soon as it gets closer than --margin / 2 to the arena border, and the
survey ends), wait while another robot is closer than --stop-distance and
in the way (its rigid body id in --others; moving away from it is always
allowed), Ctrl+C stops the robot. A stop that cannot be reached is logged
and skipped.

Output
------
<out>/<robot-id>.jsonl, one row per detected marker (or one "nothing
seen" row) per capture, same fields as static_trial.py plus layout_id,
stop, radius_m, angle_deg, yaw_offset_deg. trial_id =
"<layout>/<robot>/<stop>/<yaw offset>". The file is only appended to:
if the survey is interrupted, running the same command again skips the
captures already in the file.

Raw data (real robot only), for re-processing and for training a learned
model: every reading of every capture (--n-readings frames) is kept.
  <out>/frames/<robot-id>/<capture>_k<reading>.jpg   every camera frame
  <out>/raw/<robot-id>.jsonl   one row per frame: trial id, round, reading
      index, time, frame age, image file, camera and body pose at that
      frame, and ALL the markers detected in it (class, bbox, distance,
      bearing, viewing angle, position), before any grouping
  <out>/raw/meta_<layout>_<robot-id>.json   camera calibration, marker
      size and dictionary, camera offsets, capture settings and the true
      box positions of the layout
--no-frames skips the images (the raw rows are still written).

    # dry run: print the plan, no robot
    python -m acquisition.survey --robot-id P0 --layout-id L1 --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json --plan-only

    # simulation: fake robot and synthetic observations from the ground truth
    # (field of view, range, occlusions between boxes, Gaussian noise on d and beta)
    python -m acquisition.survey --robot-id P0 --layout-id L1 --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json --sim --out survey/

    # real robot
    python -m acquisition.survey --robot-id P0 --layout-id L1 --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json \\
        --out survey/ --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --optitrack-rb-id 8 --others 7 9 \\
        --start-deg 0 --aruco-marker-size 0.08 --camera-calib config/checkerboard_calib_P0.json
"""

import argparse

import json

import os

import random

from vf.control.goto import FakeRobot, go_to, stop, wrap_pi

ARENA_DEFAULT = (-2.690, 2.135, -2.672, 1.519)

# Set when the survey must stop (launch_all.py creates the file "abort" in
# the sync folder on Ctrl+C): every loop checks it, the robot is stopped and
# the connection closed before the process exits.
STOP = threading.Event()


def watch_abort_file(path):
    """Round mode: sets STOP as soon as `path` exists (checked every 0.2 s)."""
    def run():
        while not STOP.is_set():
            if os.path.exists(path):
                STOP.set()
                break
            time.sleep(0.2)
    threading.Thread(target=run, daemon=True).start()



class PhaseWatch:
    """What this robot is doing now, for the team and for debugging.

    phase(text) records the current step (driving, capturing, saving, ...)
    and writes it to <sync dir>/status_<robot>.json, so a robot waiting for
    the team can say what the missing robot is doing. If a working step
    (not a wait for the team) lasts longer than stuck_s, the stack of every
    thread is written to <sync dir>/stuck_<robot>.txt (launch_all.py prints
    it) and, when possible, printed: it shows exactly where the process is
    stuck. The file is written by faulthandler from C, so it works even when
    Python itself is frozen or the output of this process is blocked."""

    def __init__(self, robot_id, folder, stuck_s):
        self.robot_id, self.folder, self.stuck_s = robot_id, folder, stuck_s
        self.text, self.t, self.idle, self.dumped = "starting", time.time(), True, False
        self.dump = None
        if folder:
            os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        if folder and stuck_s > 0:
            try:
                self.dump = open(os.path.join(folder, f"stuck_{robot_id}.txt"), "a")
            except OSError:
                self.dump = None
        threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True).start()

    def set(self, text, idle=False):
        self.text, self.t, self.idle, self.dumped = text, time.time(), idle, False
        if self.dump is not None:
            try:
                if idle:
                    faulthandler.cancel_dump_traceback_later()
                else:
                    self.dump.write(f"--- {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} {text}\n")
                    self.dump.flush()
                    faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(self.stuck_s, repeat=True, file=self.dump)
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                pass
        if self.folder:
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(self.folder, f"status_{self.robot_id}.json"), "w") as f:
                    json.dump(dict(phase=text, t=self.t, idle=idle), f)
            except OSError:
                pass

    def _run(self):
        while True:
            time.sleep(1.0)
            if self.idle or self.dumped or self.stuck_s <= 0:
                continue
            busy = time.time() - self.t
            if busy > self.stuck_s:
                self.dumped = True
                print(f"STUCK: '{self.text}' for {busy:.0f} s; where every thread of this process is now "
                      f"(send this to debug):", flush=True)
                try:
                    sys.stdout.flush()
                    faulthandler.dump_traceback(file=sys.stdout, all_threads=True)
                    sys.stdout.flush()
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"(stack not available: {e})", flush=True)


WATCH = None


def phase(text, idle=False):
    """Current step of this robot (see PhaseWatch); no-op without a team."""
    if WATCH is not None:
        WATCH.set(text, idle)


def read_phase(folder, robot_id):
    """(phase, seconds in it) of another robot, or None."""
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(folder, f"status_{robot_id}.json")) as f:
            q = json.load(f)
        return q["phase"], time.time() - q["t"]
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
        return None


class FrameWriter:
    """Saves the camera frames in a background thread: a slow disk (e.g. a
    network drive) never holds up the robot and the team."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.q = queue.Queue()
        self.failed = 0
        threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True).start()

    def put(self, path, img, quality):
        import cv2
        ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, quality])
        if not ok:
            return False
        self.q.put((path, buf.tobytes()))
        return True

    def _run(self):
        while True:
            path, data = self.q.get()
            try:
                with open(path, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(data)
            except OSError as e:
                self.failed += 1
                print(f"frame not saved: {path} ({e})", flush=True)
            finally:
                self.q.task_done()

    def pending(self):
        return self.q.unfinished_tasks

    def flush(self, timeout_s=60.0):
        t0 = time.time()
        while self.q.unfinished_tasks and time.time() - t0 < timeout_s:
            time.sleep(0.1)
        if self.q.unfinished_tasks:
            print(f"{self.q.unfinished_tasks} frame(s) still not written after {timeout_s:.0f} s", flush=True)


FRAMES = None


def _ctrl_break(signum, frame):
    raise KeyboardInterrupt


if hasattr(signal, "SIGBREAK") and threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():
    # Windows: Ctrl+Break from the launcher -> same cleanup as Ctrl+C (a handler can be set only from the main
    # thread: when this module is imported elsewhere, e.g. by acquisition/live_drive.py, it is skipped there)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGBREAK, _ctrl_break)


def _with_timeout(fn, seconds, what):
    """Runs fn() but gives up waiting after `seconds` (a stuck SDK call
    must not prevent the other cleanup steps)."""
    err = []
    th = threading.Thread(target=lambda: _call(fn, err), daemon=True)
    th.start()
    th.join(seconds)
    if th.is_alive():
        print(f"{what}: no answer after {seconds:.0f} s, going on", flush=True)
    elif err:
        print(f"{what}: {err[0]}", flush=True)


def _call(fn, err):
    try:
        fn()
    except Exception as e:
        err.append(e)
CONNECTED_MSG = "robot connected"


# ====================================================================
# Plan

BOX_SIDE_M = 0.235                      # face width of the triangular boxes


def box_outline(b):
    """Corners [(x, y)] * 3 of a box seen from above: an equilateral triangle
    of side BOX_SIDE_M around its centre, turned by the yaw recorded for the
    box (launch_all.py; 0 if there is none). The zero of that yaw is where
    the rigid body was defined in Motive: the drawing turns with the box,
    up to one fixed angle per box. b: dict with x, y (or xy) and yaw."""
    x, y = (b["xy"][0], b["xy"][1]) if "xy" in b else (b["x"], b["y"])
    yaw = b.get("yaw") or 0.0
    r = BOX_SIDE_M / math.sqrt(3)
    return [(x + r * math.cos(yaw + math.pi / 3 + k * 2 * math.pi / 3),
             y + r * math.sin(yaw + math.pi / 3 + k * 2 * math.pi / 3)) for k in range(3)]


def layout_from_ground_truth(path, layout_id):
    with open(path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    if layout_id not in data:
        sys.exit(f"layout {layout_id!r} not in {path} (record it with tools/record_ground_truth.py)")
    boxes = data[layout_id]
    if not boxes:
        sys.exit(f"layout {layout_id!r} has no boxes")
    cx = sum(b["x"] for b in boxes) / len(boxes)
    cy = sum(b["y"] for b in boxes) / len(boxes)
    reach = max(math.hypot(b["x"] - cx, b["y"] - cy) for b in boxes)
    return boxes, (cx, cy), reach


def plan_stops(center, radii, step_deg, start_deg, arena, margin, yaw_offsets_deg):
    """List of captures: dict(stop, radius_m, angle_deg, x, y, yaw, yaw_offset_deg).
    Rings in the given order, alternating direction, so that consecutive
    stops are close; at every stop one capture per yaw offset."""
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = arena
    n = max(1, int(round(360.0 / step_deg)))
    plan, k = [], 0
    for ring, r in enumerate(radii):
        angles = [start_deg + i * 360.0 / n for i in range(n)]
        if ring % 2:
            angles = angles[::-1]
        for a in angles:
            x = center[0] + r * math.cos(math.radians(a))
            y = center[1] + r * math.sin(math.radians(a))
            if not (x0 + margin <= x <= x1 - margin and y0 + margin <= y <= y1 - margin):
                continue
            face = math.atan2(center[1] - y, center[0] - x)
            for off in yaw_offsets_deg:
                plan.append(dict(stop=k, radius_m=r, angle_deg=round(a % 360.0, 1), x=x, y=y,
                                 yaw=wrap_pi(face + math.radians(off)), yaw_offset_deg=off))
            k += 1
    return plan


def split_groups(plan, n_groups, center):
    """Splits the stops of `plan` among n_groups robots: every robot gets a
    contiguous SECTOR of angles around the layout, so the robots work far
    from each other. The sectors start after the widest empty angle (e.g.
    the side cut by the arena border), so no sector has to go round it.
    Inside a sector: ring by ring, alternating direction. Returns one list
    of captures per robot (all the yaw offsets of a stop together)."""
    by_stop = {}
    for c in plan:
        by_stop.setdefault(c["stop"], []).append(c)
    stops = sorted(by_stop, key=lambda k: by_stop[k][0]["angle_deg"])
    angles = sorted({by_stop[k][0]["angle_deg"] for k in stops})
    if len(angles) > 1:
        gaps = [((angles[(i + 1) % len(angles)] - angles[i]) % 360.0, i) for i in range(len(angles))]
        start = angles[(max(gaps)[1] + 1) % len(angles)]
    else:
        start = angles[0]
    rel = {k: (by_stop[k][0]["angle_deg"] - start) % 360.0 for k in stops}
    ordered_angles = sorted({rel[k] for k in stops})
    # cut the angles so that every sector gets about the same number of stops
    count = {ang: sum(1 for k in stops if rel[k] == ang) for ang in ordered_angles}
    owner, cum, total = {}, 0, len(stops)
    for ang in ordered_angles:
        owner[ang] = min(n_groups - 1, int((cum + count[ang] / 2.0) * n_groups / total))
        cum += count[ang]
    groups = []
    for g in range(n_groups):
        ks = [k for k in stops if owner[rel[k]] == g]
        radii = sorted({by_stop[k][0]["radius_m"] for k in ks})
        seq = []
        for i, r in enumerate(radii):
            ring = sorted((k for k in ks if by_stop[k][0]["radius_m"] == r), key=lambda k: rel[k],
                          reverse=bool(i % 2))
            for k in ring:
                seq += by_stop[k]
        groups.append(seq)
    return groups


def border_distance(p, arena):
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = arena
    return min(p[0] - x0, x1 - p[0], p[1] - y0, y1 - p[1])


def inside(p, arena, margin):
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = arena
    return x0 + margin <= p[0] <= x1 - margin and y0 + margin <= p[1] <= y1 - margin


def segment_clear(a, b, boxes, clearance_m):
    """True if the segment a-b stays at least clearance_m from every box."""
    ax, ay = a
    dx, dy = b[0] - ax, b[1] - ay
    L2 = dx * dx + dy * dy
    for box in boxes:
        px, py = box["x"] - ax, box["y"] - ay
        t = 0.0 if L2 == 0 else max(0.0, min(1.0, (px * dx + py * dy) / L2))
        if math.hypot(px - t * dx, py - t * dy) < clearance_m:
            return False
    return True


def robots_clear(a, b, robots, clearance_m):
    """True if the segment a-b does not bring the robot closer than
    clearance_m to any of the (parked) robots in `robots` [(x, y), ...].
    Moving away from a robot that is already close is allowed: the leg is
    rejected only if it gets closer than clearance_m AND closer than it
    already is at its start."""
    ax, ay = a
    dx, dy = b[0] - ax, b[1] - ay
    L2 = dx * dx + dy * dy
    for rx, ry in robots:
        px, py = rx - ax, ry - ay
        t = 0.0 if L2 == 0 else max(0.0, min(1.0, (px * dx + py * dy) / L2))
        d = math.hypot(px - t * dx, py - t * dy)
        if d < clearance_m and d < math.hypot(px, py) - 1e-6:
            return False
    return True


def route(cur_xy, goal_xy, center, boxes, clearance_m, arena, margin, step_deg=15.0,
          robots=(), robot_clearance_m=0.7):
    """Waypoints from cur to goal that never pass closer than clearance_m to
    a box and never leave the arena (minus margin).

    Straight line when it is clear of the boxes (the arena is a rectangle:
    a segment between two points inside it stays inside). Otherwise round
    the layout on an arc about its centre, trying both directions and
    taking the shorter one whose waypoints are all inside the arena and
    whose legs are all clear of the boxes. A robot that starts too close
    to a box first moves straight away from the layout centre. `robots`
    are the positions of the other (standing) robots: no leg may pass
    closer than robot_clearance_m to them; the arc is also tried further
    out to go round them. None if no path works."""
    def clear(a, b):
        return segment_clear(a, b, boxes, clearance_m) and robots_clear(a, b, robots, robot_clearance_m)

    if clear(cur_xy, goal_xy):
        return [tuple(goal_xy)]
    cx, cy = center
    reach = max(math.hypot(b["x"] - cx, b["y"] - cy) for b in boxes)
    if not segment_clear(cur_xy, cur_xy, boxes, clearance_m):
        # already too close to a box: first move straight away from the
        # layout centre, out of the clearance, then plan from there
        ux, uy = cur_xy[0] - cx, cur_xy[1] - cy
        n = math.hypot(ux, uy) or 1.0
        out = (cx + ux / n * (reach + clearance_m + 0.05), cy + uy / n * (reach + clearance_m + 0.05))
        if not inside(out, arena, margin) or not segment_clear(out, out, boxes, clearance_m):
            return None
        if not robots_clear(cur_xy, out, robots, robot_clearance_m):
            return None
        rest = route(out, goal_xy, center, boxes, clearance_m, arena, margin, step_deg, robots, robot_clearance_m)
        return None if rest is None else [out] + rest
    ra = math.hypot(cur_xy[0] - cx, cur_xy[1] - cy)
    rb = math.hypot(goal_xy[0] - cx, goal_xy[1] - cy)
    # arc as close to the boxes as the clearance allows (+5 cm of slack),
    # but not inside the smaller of the two ring radii
    r = max(reach + clearance_m + 0.05, min(ra, rb))
    a0 = math.atan2(cur_xy[1] - cy, cur_xy[0] - cx)
    a1 = math.atan2(goal_xy[1] - cy, goal_xy[0] - cx)
    short = wrap_pi(a1 - a0)
    options = []
    arc_radii = [r] + ([r + robot_clearance_m] if robots else [])
    for r_arc in arc_radii:
        for da in (short, short - math.copysign(2 * math.pi, short) if short else 2 * math.pi):
            n = max(1, int(math.ceil(abs(math.degrees(da)) / step_deg)))
            # intermediate points on the arc, the ends at the start and goal
            # radius, never inside reach + clearance
            pts = []
            for i in range(n + 1):
                f = i / n
                rr = max(r_arc if 0 < i < n else (ra if i == 0 else rb), reach + clearance_m)
                pts.append((cx + rr * math.cos(a0 + da * f), cy + rr * math.sin(a0 + da * f)))
            path = [tuple(cur_xy)] + pts + [tuple(goal_xy)]
            if not all(inside(q, arena, margin) for q in pts[1:-1]):  # not the start: the robot is there
                continue
            if not all(clear(path[k], path[k + 1]) for k in range(len(path) - 1)):
                continue
            length = sum(math.hypot(path[k + 1][0] - path[k][0], path[k + 1][1] - path[k][1])
                         for k in range(len(path) - 1))
            options.append((length, pts[1:] + [tuple(goal_xy)]))
    if not options:
        return None
    return min(options)[1]


# ====================================================================
# Simulated sensing (--sim)
# ====================================================================

def occluded(target, boxes, cam_xy, box_side_m):
    """True if another box stands between the camera and `target`: it is
    closer to the camera and its centre is less than one box side from the
    camera-target line (the two boxes overlap in the image)."""
    tx, ty = target["x"] - cam_xy[0], target["y"] - cam_xy[1]
    d = math.hypot(tx, ty)
    for o in boxes:
        if o is target:
            continue
        ox, oy = o["x"] - cam_xy[0], o["y"] - cam_xy[1]
        along = (ox * tx + oy * ty) / d
        if 0 < along < d and abs(ox * ty - oy * tx) / d < box_side_m:
            return True
    return False


def simulated_rows(boxes, pose, hfov_deg=88.0, r_min=0.15, r_max=3.0,
                   sigma_d=0.03, sigma_b=math.radians(1.0), box_side_m=0.20, rng=random):
    """Synthetic observations of the ground-truth boxes from a camera pose:
    every box in the field of view and not hidden behind another box
    (occluded), distance and bearing with Gaussian noise."""
    x, y, psi = pose
    rows = []
    for b in boxes:
        dx, dy = b["x"] - x, b["y"] - y
        d = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        beta = wrap_pi(psi - math.atan2(dy, dx))
        if not (r_min <= d <= r_max and abs(beta) <= math.radians(hfov_deg) / 2):
            continue
        if box_side_m > 0 and occluded(b, boxes, (x, y), box_side_m):
            continue
        rows.append(dict(class_name=b["class_name"], confidence=1.0,
                         distance=d + rng.gauss(0, sigma_d), bearing_rad=beta + rng.gauss(0, sigma_b),
                         viewing_angle_rad=None))
    return rows


# ====================================================================
# Main
# ====================================================================

def draw_plan(path, arena, margin, boxes, center, plan, legs):
    """Top view of the plan: arena, margin, boxes, stops (numbered, with the
    camera direction) and the planned paths between them."""
    # matplotlib Figure without pyplot: the backend of the program that
    # calls this (e.g. the live window of launch_all.py) is not touched
    import matplotlib
    from matplotlib.figure import Figure
    from matplotlib.backends.backend_agg import FigureCanvasAgg
    from matplotlib.patches import Polygon, Rectangle
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = arena
    fig = Figure(figsize=(7, 7 * (y1 - y0) / (x1 - x0)))
    FigureCanvasAgg(fig)
    ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0, y0), x1 - x0, y1 - y0, fill=False, color="k"))
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0 + margin, y0 + margin), x1 - x0 - 2 * margin, y1 - y0 - 2 * margin,
                               fill=False, color="0.6", ls="--"))
    for b in boxes:
        ax.add_patch(Polygon(box_outline(b), closed=True, color="tab:orange"))
    ax.plot(*center, "k+")
    for pts in legs:
        ax.plot([q[0] for q in pts], [q[1] for q in pts], color="tab:blue", lw=0.8)
    seen = set()
    for c in plan:
        ax.annotate("", xy=(c["x"] + 0.3 * math.cos(c["yaw"]), c["y"] + 0.3 * math.sin(c["yaw"])),
                    xytext=(c["x"], c["y"]), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="tab:green"))
        if c["stop"] not in seen:
            seen.add(c["stop"])
            ax.plot(c["x"], c["y"], "o", color="tab:green")
            ax.text(c["x"] + 0.05, c["y"] + 0.05, str(c["stop"]), fontsize=8)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xlim(x0 - 0.1, x1 + 0.1)
    ax.set_ylim(y0 - 0.1, y1 + 0.1)
    ax.set_xlabel("x [m] (OptiTrack planar frame)")
    ax.set_ylabel("y [m]")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=120)


def done_trials(path, rounds_only=False):
    """trial_ids already in the file (to resume). rounds_only: only the
    captures made in round mode (rows with a "round"), so data of an older
    survey in the same file is not mistaken for this one."""
    done = set()
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                if line.strip():
                    r = json.loads(line)
                    if not rounds_only or r.get("round") is not None:
                        done.add(r["trial_id"])
    return done


def _jsonable(v):
    """json.dumps fallback for numpy values."""
    if hasattr(v, "tolist"):
        return v.tolist()
    if hasattr(v, "item"):
        return v.item()
    raise TypeError(f"not JSON serializable: {type(v).__name__}")


class RecordingCamera:
    """Wraps the camera: read() is passed through, and the frame it returns
    is kept together with the camera and body pose at that moment."""
