    returned Detection is always one that was REALLY observed. Without a
    measured distance (YOLO, or fewer than 2 readings with a distance) we
    fall back to comparing confidence, which is a real signal there."""
    with_distance = [r for r in readings if r.distance is not None]
    if len(with_distance) >= 2:
        distances = sorted(r.distance for r in with_distance)
        n = len(distances)
        median = (distances[n // 2] if n % 2 == 1
                  else (distances[n // 2 - 1] + distances[n // 2]) / 2)
        chosen = min(with_distance, key=lambda r: abs(r.distance - median))
        if debug:
            print(f"    [debug] representative chosen by median "
                  f"distance: {[round(d, 3) for d in distances]} -> "
                  f"median={median:.3f} -> chosen distance="
                  f"{chosen.distance:.3f}")
        return chosen
    return max(readings, key=lambda r: r.confidence)


def capture_trial(detector, n_readings=5, pause_s=0.1, instance_threshold_m=0.5,
                  debug=False):
    """n_readings closely spaced readings. If the scene contains MORE than
    one object (e.g. 2 boxes in view at the same time), the n_readings see
    ALL of them repeatedly -- this function groups them by estimated
    POSITION (see object_position.cluster_by_position) so the result
    is ONE reading per distinct PHYSICAL OBJECT, not one per raw reading
    (which would count the same object several times).

    Returns a LIST of Detection: normally 1 element (a single object in
    view, or none), but it can have more if the robot sees several
    physical instances together. If no reading saw anything, the list
    contains ONE "nothing seen" Detection (class_name=None) so the trial is
    still recorded for this robot, not silently missing from the file.

    Honest limitation: a detection WITHOUT an estimable position (robot
    pose unavailable at that moment) cannot be assigned to an instance --
    it is dropped rather than risking merging it with the wrong object.
    This only happens if OptiTrack loses tracking in the middle of the
    n_readings: rare, but worth knowing if a trial with several objects
    comes back with fewer objects than expected.

    debug=True prints EVERY raw reading (how many detections in the frame,
    whether each one has an estimable position or not) instead of only
    the final result -- use it when a trial with several objects in view
    (confirmed with --live) comes back with fewer instances than expected:
    it tells whether the problem is upstream (at that precise moment the
    camera saw fewer markers than --live shows, e.g. because of a slightly
    different angle/position) or downstream (the markers were there but
    with no `pose` available, or the estimated positions ended up closer
    than the --instance-threshold-m threshold despite being two distinct
    real objects)."""
    from vf.perception.object_position import cluster_by_position

    all_readings = []
    last_empty = None
    for i in range(n_readings):
        raw_readings = detector.read()
        if debug:
            print(f"  [debug] reading {i + 1}/{n_readings}: "
                  f"{len(raw_readings)} raw detection(s)")
            for r in raw_readings:
                if r.position is not None:
                    pos_str = (f"position=({r.position[0]:.3f}, "
                               f"{r.position[1]:.3f})")
                else:
                    pos_str = "position=NONE (robot pose not available now)"
                print(f"    - class_name={r.class_name} conf={r.confidence:.2f} "
                      f"distance={r.distance} {pos_str}")
        for r in raw_readings:
            if r.class_name is None:
                last_empty = r
            else:
                all_readings.append(r)
        time.sleep(pause_s)

    if debug:
        with_position = sum(1 for r in all_readings if r.position is not None)
        print(f"  [debug] total over the {n_readings} readings: {len(all_readings)} "
              f"non-empty detection(s), {with_position} with estimable "
              f"position (instance-threshold-m={instance_threshold_m})")

    if not all_readings:
        return [last_empty] if last_empty is not None else []

    positioned = [r for r in all_readings if r.position is not None]
    if len(positioned) < 2:
        # either 0 or 1 positionable reading: nothing to group by
        # instance, fall back to the simple behaviour (the best by
        # confidence among those available).
        if debug and len(all_readings) > len(positioned):
            print("  [debug] fewer than 2 detections with a position: no "
                  "per-instance grouping possible, picking the "
                  "representative among ALL raw detections (including "
                  "those without a position)")
        return [_pick_representative(all_readings, debug=debug)]

    cluster_indices = cluster_by_position(
        [r.position for r in positioned], threshold_m=instance_threshold_m)
    n_clusters = max(cluster_indices) + 1
    if debug:
        print(f"  [debug] grouped into {n_clusters} distinct physical "
              f"instance(s)")
    readings_per_cluster = [[] for _ in range(n_clusters)]
    for r, idx in zip(positioned, cluster_indices):
        readings_per_cluster[idx].append(r)
    if debug:
        for i, group in enumerate(readings_per_cluster, start=1):
            print(f"  [debug] instance {i}: {len(group)} reading(s) in the "
                  f"cluster")
    return [_pick_representative(group, debug=debug)
            for group in readings_per_cluster]


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--robot-id", required=True,
                   help="robot name in config.ROBOTS, and robot_id in the log")
    p.add_argument("--sn", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--ip", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--live", action="store_true",
                   help="live video preview with the detected markers "
                        "drawn on top, instead of capturing a trial -- "
                        "see the module docstring. With --live, "
                        "--trial-id/--out/--regions/--localization are "
                        "not needed, UNLESS --state-out is also used")
    p.add_argument("--frame-out", default=None,
                   help="ONLY with --live --state-out: also writes the latest camera frame "
                        "(JPEG) to this path, for the image network of the live demo")
    p.add_argument("--frame-every-s", type=float, default=0.25,
                   help="with --frame-out: seconds between two frames written")
    p.add_argument("--no-window", action="store_true",
                   help="with --live: no video window")
    p.add_argument("--commands", default=None,
                   help="with --live and --state-out: the robot drives to the goals written in this file by the "
                        "live demo page (acquisition/live_drive.py), clear of the boxes and of the other robots "
                        "whose live states are next to --state-out")
    p.add_argument("--state-out", default=None,
                   help="ONLY with --live: continuously writes this "
                        "robot's state (pose + detections with global "
                        "position) to this JSON file, overwritten on "
                        "every frame -- read by demo/live.py for the "
                        "live fusion across robots. Requires --regions "
                        "and (with OptiTrack) --optitrack-rb-id, because "
                        "the global position needs the robot pose")
    p.add_argument("--trial-id", default=None,
                   help="identifies THIS trial (same label for all "
                        "participating robots) -- ties the rows of the "
                        "different robots together in "
                        "the analysis -- required unless "
                        "--live is used")
    p.add_argument("--out", default=None,
                   help="folder shared by the robot processes: one row "
                        "per robot per trial in <out>/<robot-id>.jsonl "
                        "-- required unless --live is used")
    p.add_argument("--regions", default=None,
                   help="see config/optitrack_regions.json -- only needed "
                        "for 'zone' in the log, not the data that matters "
                        "here (the precise position is, see "
                        "--localization) -- required unless --live is used")
    p.add_argument("--localization", choices=["odometry", "optitrack"],
                   default="optitrack",
                   help="OptiTrack by default for static trials: the "
                        "robot is stationary, the pose is needed only "
                        "once, no odometry drift to accumulate")
    p.add_argument("--optitrack-rb-id", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--optitrack-server", default="127.0.0.1")
    p.add_argument("--optitrack-local", default="127.0.0.1")
    p.add_argument("--camera-offset-forward-m", type=float, default=0.0,
                   help="how far FORWARD (in the robot's reference frame) "
                        "the camera is relative to the point tracked by "
                        "OptiTrack/odometry (e.g. the rigid body centre) "
                        "-- measure it with a ruler if the camera is "
                        "mounted on an arm and not at the tracked point: "
                        "see CameraOffsetPose in localization.py. Default "
                        "0.0 = no correction (behaviour unchanged)")
    p.add_argument("--camera-offset-right-m", type=float, default=0.0,
                   help="how far to the RIGHT (negative = to the left) the "
                        "camera is relative to the tracked point -- see "
                        "--camera-offset-forward-m")
    p.add_argument("--frame-correction-file", default=None,
                   help="JSON file produced by tools/calibrate_optitrack.py "
                        "({\"rotation_rad\":.., \"dx_m\":.., \"dy_m\":..}) "
                        "-- corrects the misalignment between THIS robot's "
                        "OptiTrack frame and the true shared frame (see "
                        "FrameCorrectedPose in localization.py). Applied "
                        "BEFORE --camera-offset-*. Omitted = no correction "
                        "(behaviour unchanged)")
    p.add_argument("--detector", choices=["aruco", "yolo"], default="aruco")
    p.add_argument("--aruco-marker-size", type=float, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--aruco-dict", default="4X4_50")
    p.add_argument("--aruco-classes", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--camera-calib", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--aruco-max-distance-m", type=float, default=8.0,
                   help="drops an ArUco detection whose reported distance "
                        "exceeds this threshold -- protects against "
                        "solvePnP's near/far ambiguity on a planar marker "
                        "(see ArucoDetector), which can make the distance "
                        "jump to an absurd value (e.g. ~20m) on an "
                        "isolated frame without the marker having moved. "
                        "Raise the value if your arena really is larger "
                        "than 8m; --aruco-max-distance-m -1 disables the "
                        "check")
    p.add_argument("--aruco-default-params", action="store_true",
                   help="use OpenCV's default DetectorParameters instead "
                        "of the relaxed ones (see "
                        "aruco_detector.relaxed_parameters()) -- only to "
                        "compare 'before/after' if you want to check how "
                        "much they really help against a marker that "
                        "'flickers in and out'")
    p.add_argument("--camera-resolution", choices=["360", "540", "720"],
                   default="720",
                   help="video stream resolution (see camera.py: 720p has "
                        "no measured cost on the link compared to 540p, "
                        "and more pixels on the marker help precisely "
                        "against 'flickering in and out' -- camera.py's "
                        "default of 540 is raised to 720 here)")
    p.add_argument("--yolo-host", default="127.0.0.1")
    p.add_argument("--yolo-port", type=int, default=8765)
    p.add_argument("--n-readings", type=int, default=5,
                   help="closely spaced readings per trial, the best one "
                        "is kept -- see capture_trial()")
    p.add_argument("--instance-threshold-m", type=float, default=0.5,
                   help="within how many metres two readings of THIS robot "
                        "are considered the same physical object instead "
                        "of two distinct instances")
    p.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true",
                   help="print every raw reading during capture (how "
                        "many markers in the frame, whether each has an "
                        "estimable position) -- use it if a trial with "
                        "several objects in view (confirmed with --live) "
                        "comes back with fewer instances than expected, "
                        "see the capture_trial() docstring. With --live it "
                        "additionally prints to the terminal (no longer "
                        "on the video) the pixel offset and the "
                        "bearing-from-pixel for each marker, see "
                        "live_preview()")
    p.add_argument("--faulty", action="store_true",
                   help="designate THIS robot as faulty for this trial "
                        "(simulated systematic fault)")
    p.add_argument("--dropout-prob", type=float, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--mislabel-prob", type=float, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--p-d", type=float, default=1.0,
                   help="ONLY with --live: simulated interference with "
                        "constant detection probability p_D (Section 7.1 "
                        "of the document): every marker in every frame is "
                        "kept with probability p_D, otherwise treated as "
                        "not seen. One value per process = one value per "
                        "robot. Default 1.0 = no interference. Draws are "
                        "reproducible with --seed")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if not 0.0 <= args.p_d <= 1.0:
        p.error("--p-d must be between 0 and 1")
    if args.p_d < 1.0 and not args.live:
        p.error("--p-d only applies with --live (for static trials use "
                "--faulty --dropout-prob)")

    # --state-out is checked BEFORE the "not args.live" block below: if
    # --live is missing, --trial-id is usually missing too (--live and
    # normal trials are alternative modes), so checking
    # trial-id/out/regions first would show the user "--trial-id is
    # required" instead of the much clearer "--state-out only makes sense
    # together with --live" -- misleading for someone who simply forgot
    # --live.
    if args.state_out is not None:
        if not args.live:
            p.error("--state-out only makes sense together with --live")
        if args.regions is None:
            p.error("--state-out requires --regions (needed to compute "
                    "the global position)")
        if args.localization == "optitrack" and args.optitrack_rb_id is None:
            p.error("--state-out requires --optitrack-rb-id with "
                    "--localization optitrack")
    if not args.live:
        if args.trial_id is None:
            p.error("--trial-id is required (unless --live is used)")
        if args.out is None:
            p.error("--out is required (unless --live is used)")
        if args.regions is None:
            p.error("--regions is required (unless --live is used)")

    # In --live mode WITHOUT --state-out we skip regions/OptiTrack: the
    # video preview only serves to check what the camera sees and does
    # not need the robot pose (see live_preview() above). With --state-out,
    # instead, the pose is needed (for the global position), so it must be
    # set up as in the non-live path.
    needs_pose = (not args.live) or (args.state_out is not None)
    regions = None
    pose_provider = None
    if needs_pose:
        regions = load_regions(args.regions)
        if args.localization == "optitrack":
            if args.optitrack_rb_id is None:
                p.error("--optitrack-rb-id is required with "
                        "--localization optitrack")
            from vf.localization.mocap_pose import MocapPose
            from vf.localization.optitrack import OptiTrackPose
            source = MocapPose(args.optitrack_rb_id, args.optitrack_server,
                               args.optitrack_local)
            source.wait_ready()
            pose_provider = OptiTrackPose(
                pose_source=source, regions=regions, close_source=True)

    raw_detector = None
    if args.detector == "aruco":
        if args.aruco_marker_size is None:
            p.error("--aruco-marker-size is required with "
                    "--detector aruco (measure it on the printed marker, "
                    "in metres)")
        from vf.perception.aruco_detector import (
            ArucoDetector, load_aruco_classes, load_calibration,
            dictionary_from_name)
        marker_to_class = (load_aruco_classes(args.aruco_classes)
                           if args.aruco_classes else None)
        if args.camera_calib:
            camera_matrix, dist_coeffs = load_calibration(args.camera_calib)
        else:
            camera_matrix, dist_coeffs = None, None
        max_distance = (None if args.aruco_max_distance_m < 0
                        else args.aruco_max_distance_m)
        raw_detector = ArucoDetector(
            marker_size_m=args.aruco_marker_size,
            camera_matrix=camera_matrix, dist_coeffs=dist_coeffs,
            dictionary=dictionary_from_name(args.aruco_dict),
            marker_to_class=marker_to_class,
            relax_parameters=not args.aruco_default_params,
            max_plausible_distance_m=max_distance)
    else:
        from vf.perception.yolo_client import RemoteYoloDetector
        raw_detector = RemoteYoloDetector(host=args.yolo_host,
                                          port=args.yolo_port)

    from robomaster_sdk import Robot
    from robomaster_sdk.camera import Camera as CameraSDK

    with Robot(args.robot_id, sn=args.sn, ip=args.ip) as robot:
        camera = CameraSDK(robot.camera).start(
            resolution=args.camera_resolution)

        localizer = None
        if needs_pose:
            localizer = (pose_provider if pose_provider is not None
                         else OdometryLocalizer(robot, regions))
            # Corrects the misalignment between THIS robot's OptiTrack
            # frame and the true shared frame -- see FrameCorrectedPose in
            # localization.py and tools/calibrate_optitrack.py. Applied
            # BEFORE the camera offset below: the camera offset uses the
            # yaw to compute forward/right in the robot frame, so it must
            # see the pose already re-calibrated to the true frame.
            # Without --frame-correction-file it is a transparent no-op.
            if args.frame_correction_file:
                with open(args.frame_correction_file) as f:
                    correction = json.load(f)
                localizer = FrameCorrectedPose(
                    localizer,
                    rotation_rad=correction["rotation_rad"],
                    dx_m=correction["dx_m"],
                    dy_m=correction["dy_m"])
            # Corrects the offset between the tracked point (OptiTrack
            # rigid body, or odometry origin) and the TRUE camera position
            # -- see CameraOffsetPose in localization.py. With both
            # offsets at 0.0 (default) it is a transparent no-op: no
            # behaviour change for those who do not pass them.
            localizer = CameraOffsetPose(
                localizer,
                offset_forward_m=args.camera_offset_forward_m,
                offset_right_m=args.camera_offset_right_m)

        if args.live:
            driver = None
            try:
                pose_fn = localizer.pose if localizer is not None else None
                if args.commands and pose_provider is not None and args.state_out:
                    # the controller of the captures steers the rigid body, not the camera ahead of it
                    from acquisition.live_drive import LiveDriver
                    driver = LiveDriver(robot.chassis, pose_provider.pose, args.commands,
                                        os.path.dirname(args.state_out) or ".", args.robot_id)
                    driver.start()
                    print(f"driving on the commands in {args.commands}", flush=True)
                live_preview(camera, raw_detector, args.robot_id,
                             pose_fn=pose_fn, state_out=args.state_out,
                             debug=args.debug, p_d=args.p_d,
                             seed=args.seed, frame_out=args.frame_out,
                             frame_every_s=args.frame_every_s,
                             show_window=not args.no_window,
                             status_fn=(lambda: driver.status) if driver else None)
            finally:
                if driver is not None:
                    driver.close()
                camera.stop()
                if localizer is not None:
                    localizer.close()
            return

        fault_injector = FaultInjector(
            robot_id=args.robot_id,
            faulty_robot_ids=[args.robot_id] if args.faulty else [],
            dropout_prob=args.dropout_prob, mislabel_prob=args.mislabel_prob,
            seed=args.seed)
        detector = ObjectDetector(
            camera=camera, robot_id=args.robot_id,
            current_zone_fn=localizer.current_zone,
            detector=raw_detector, fault_injector=fault_injector,
            pose_fn=localizer.pose)

        # give the camera (non-blocking background reader, see
        # perception.py) time to have a first frame ready.
        time.sleep(0.5)

        try:
            readings = capture_trial(detector, n_readings=args.n_readings,
                                     instance_threshold_m=args.instance_threshold_m,
                                     debug=args.debug)
            # Camera pose at capture time, stored in every row as
            # "robot_pose": the analysis uses it to know each
            # robot's field of view.
            trial_pose = localizer.pose()
        finally:
            camera.stop()
            localizer.close()

    if not readings:
        # should not happen (see capture_trial: even "nothing seen"
        # produces a Detection), but if it does, record it as a "nothing"
        # row instead of silently disappearing from the file.
        readings = [None]

    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(args.out, f"{args.robot_id}.jsonl")
    rows = []
    for r in readings:
        rows.append(dict(
            trial_id=args.trial_id, t=time.time(), robot_id=args.robot_id,
            class_name=r.class_name if r else None,
            confidence=r.confidence if r else 0.0,
            fault_injected=r.fault_injected if r else False,
            dropped=r.dropped if r else False,
            zone=r.zone if r else "unknown",
            position=list(r.position) if (r and r.position) else None,
            distance=r.distance if r else None,
            bearing_rad=r.bearing_rad if r else None,
            viewing_angle_rad=r.viewing_angle_rad if r else None,
            # pose of the frame the marker was seen in (the one its
            # position was computed with); trial pose for "nothing seen"
            robot_pose=(list(r.robot_pose) if (r and r.robot_pose is not None)
                        else list(trial_pose) if trial_pose is not None else None)))

    # Re-running the SAME --trial-id for the SAME robot (e.g. after
    # adjusting the robot's position, or to redo a capture that looked
    # wrong) REPLACES that trial's previous rows in this file instead of
    # piling up under the old ones. Previously it was pure append:
    # running the same trial_id twice left both the old AND the new rows
    # in the same file, and the analysis merged them as if they
    # were different readings of the same trial, giving results that
    # looked like a bug (extra instances or inconsistent positions) but
    # were just stale data never cleaned up. Other trial_ids in the same
    # file are not touched.
    other_rows = []
    n_replaced = 0
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path) as f:
            for existing_row in f:
                existing_row = existing_row.strip()
                if not existing_row:
                    continue
                if json.loads(existing_row).get("trial_id") == args.trial_id:
                    n_replaced += 1
                else:
                    other_rows.append(existing_row)

    with open(path, "w") as f:
        for old_row in other_rows:
            f.write(old_row + "\n")
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")

    description = "; ".join(
        f"class_name={r['class_name']} conf={r['confidence']:.2f} dist={r['distance']}"
        for r in rows)
    note = (f" (replaced {n_replaced} previous row(s) of the same "
            f"trial)" if n_replaced else "")
    print(f"trial {args.trial_id} ({args.robot_id}): {len(rows)} "
          f"object(s) -- {description}  -> {path}{note}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
==> ./acquisition/launch_all.py <==
"""Runs the survey with all the robots from ONE command, ROUND BY ROUND.

Fixed positions (--radius R, the systematic mode): the robots stand on a
circle of radius R around the centre of the boxes (recomputed from the
ground truth for every layout; --circle-center X Y overrides it), evenly
spaced (one position per robot, the first at --first-angle-deg): the same
distance and angles for every layout. Place the robots roughly near the circle:
each one drives to the nearest free position (round 0), then, round after
round, ALL the robots rotate together on the circle by --step-deg, always
facing its centre, for --sweep-deg in total (default 360 / number of
robots: together they cover the whole circle once). A position too close
to a box or to the arena border is not used: that robot stays there in
that round (the path preview shows it).

Without --radius: round 0 is captured where the robots were placed and
the formation rotates around the boxes at the distance where each robot
was placed (default --sweep-deg 180).

The next round starts only when every robot has captured. Each robot
stands still if another robot is in its way (--others is set
automatically).

The boxes are read from OptiTrack at every launch (their rigid bodies:
--box RB:CLASS, or the rb_id saved in --ground-truth by
tools/record_ground_truth.py): the plan, the live figures and the analysis
use where the boxes are NOW. They are written in <run>/ground_truth.json and
added to the --ground-truth file under the run id. --fixed-boxes uses the
file instead.

Every launch is a NEW RUN, saved in its own folder <out>/<layout>_<date-time>/
(captures, raw readings, frames, path preview, live figures): nothing is
skipped because an earlier run was already at the same position.
pipeline/analyze_rounds.py / pipeline/build_scans.py read one run folder or the whole
<out>/ folder (every run is kept separate).

The robots are connected ONE AT A TIME (the DJI SDK looks for the robot
through a UDP port that only one process at a time can use); the first
round starts when all of them are connected. Ctrl+C stops all of them:
each robot stops its motion, closes camera and connection, then exits.

    python -m acquisition.launch_all --robot P0:8 --robot P1:7 --robot P2:9 --robot P3:10 \\
        --layout-id L2 --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json \\
        --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --out survey_rounds/ \\
        --aruco-marker-size 0.077 --radius 1.3 --step-deg 15
"""

import argparse
import json
import locale
import math
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

CONNECTED_MSG = "robot connected"      # printed by survey.py
CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0


def parse_robot(spec):
    parts = spec.split(":")
    if len(parts) < 2:
        raise SystemExit(f"--robot {spec!r}: expected ID:RIGID_BODY[:CAMERA_CALIB]")
    rid, rb = parts[0], int(parts[1])
    calib = parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 and parts[2] else None
    if calib is None:
        default = os.path.join("config", f"checkerboard_calib_{rid}.json")
        calib = default if os.path.exists(default) else None
    return dict(robot_id=rid, rb=rb, calib=calib)


def pump(proc, tag, connected):
    """Prints the output of one robot process. Reads BYTES and never stops
    on a line it cannot decode or print: if this thread died, the pipe of
    that process would fill up and the robot would freeze at its next
    print."""
    for raw in iter(proc.stdout.readline, b""):
        try:
            line = raw.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            line = raw.decode(locale.getpreferredencoding(False) or "latin-1", errors="replace")
        try:
            if line.strip():
                print(f"{tag:>4} | {line.rstrip()}", flush=True)
        except Exception:
            try:
                print(f"{tag:>4} | {line.rstrip().encode('ascii', 'replace').decode()}", flush=True)
            except Exception:
                pass
        if CONNECTED_MSG in line:
            connected.set()
    connected.set()                      # process ended: do not keep the others waiting


class StuckReports:
    """Prints what survey.py writes in <sync dir>/stuck_<robot>.txt when a
    robot stays in one step too long (stack of every thread)."""

    def __init__(self, sync_dir, team):
        self.sync_dir, self.team = sync_dir, team
        self.offset = {r: 0 for r in team}

    def poll(self):
        for r in self.team:
            path = os.path.join(self.sync_dir, f"stuck_{r}.txt")
            try:
                if os.path.getsize(path) <= self.offset[r]:
                    continue
                with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
                    f.seek(self.offset[r])
                    text = f.read()
                    self.offset[r] = f.tell()
            except OSError:
                continue
            last_phase = ""
            out = []
            for line in text.splitlines():
                if line.startswith("--- "):
                    last_phase = line[4:]
                elif line.strip():
                    out.append(line)
            if out:
                print(f"STUCK {r} | no progress in: {last_phase or 'the current step'}; where it is stuck:",
                      flush=True)
                for line in out:
                    print(f"STUCK {r} | {line}", flush=True)


def arg_value(rest, name, default=None):
    return rest[rest.index(name) + 1] if name in rest else default


def set_arg(rest, name, value):
    """rest with `name value` (replaced if already there)."""
    if name in rest:
        i = rest.index(name)
        return rest[:i] + [name, value] + rest[i + 2:]
    return rest + [name, value]


def box_rigid_bodies(box_specs, gt_path, layout_id):
    """[(rigid body id, class)] of the boxes: from --box RB:CLASS, or else
    the rb_id saved by tools/record_ground_truth.py in the ground truth file
    (entry of --layout-id first, otherwise the last entry that has them)."""
    if box_specs:
        out = []
        for v in box_specs:
            rb, _, cls = v.partition(":")
            out.append((int(rb), cls.strip() or "box"))
        return out, "--box"
    data = {}
    if gt_path and os.path.exists(gt_path):
        with open(gt_path) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    keys = ([layout_id] if layout_id in data else []) + [k for k in reversed(list(data)) if k != layout_id]
    for k in keys:
        entries = data.get(k) or []
        if entries and all("rb_id" in e for e in entries):
            return [(int(e["rb_id"]), e.get("class_name", "box")) for e in entries], f"rigid bodies of {k} in {gt_path}"
    return None, None


def record_boxes(objects, server, local, seconds=2.0):
    """Positions of the boxes NOW from OptiTrack (average over `seconds`):
    [dict(class_name, x, y, yaw, rb_id)], or raises SystemExit if a box is
    not tracked. yaw [rad] is the planar yaw of the box rigid body as Motive
    gives it (circular mean): its zero is wherever the rigid body was
    defined, so the face directions follow from it up to one fixed offset
    per box."""
    from tools.record_ground_truth import average_positions
    from vf.localization.mocap_pose import MocapHub
    hub = MocapHub([rb for rb, _ in objects], server, local)
    try:
        try:
            hub.wait_ready()
        except RuntimeError as e:
            raise SystemExit(f"BOXES | {e}")
        samples = {rb: [] for rb, _ in objects}
        t0 = time.time()
        while time.time() - t0 < seconds:
            for rb, _ in objects:
                q = hub.get_pose(rb)
                if q is not None:
                    samples[rb].append((q[0], q[1], q[2]))
            time.sleep(0.02)
    finally:
        hub.close()
    avg = average_positions(samples)
    missing = [rb for rb, _ in objects if rb not in avg]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"BOXES | no OptiTrack reading for the box rigid bodies {missing}: check them in Motive")
    yaw = {rb: math.atan2(sum(math.sin(p[2]) for p in pts), sum(math.cos(p[2]) for p in pts))
           for rb, pts in samples.items() if pts}
    return [dict(class_name=cls, x=round(avg[rb][0], 4), y=round(avg[rb][1], 4), yaw=round(yaw[rb], 4), rb_id=rb)
            for rb, cls in objects]


def boxes_for_this_run(a, rest, layout_id, run_id, gt_out):
    """Reads where the boxes are NOW (OptiTrack) and writes them to gt_out
    as {layout_id: boxes, run_id: boxes}; if run_id is given, they are also
    added to the --ground-truth file under the run id, so the analysis of
    this run always uses the boxes of this run. Returns the new rest (with
    --ground-truth gt_out), or rest unchanged in --sim / --fixed-boxes."""
    gt_path = arg_value(rest, "--ground-truth")
    if "--sim" in rest or a.fixed_boxes:
        print(f"BOXES | positions from {gt_path} ({layout_id})", flush=True)
        return rest
    objects, source = box_rigid_bodies(a.box, gt_path, layout_id)
    if not objects:
        raise SystemExit("BOXES | no rigid body ids of the boxes: give them with --box RB:CLASS (one per box), "
                         "or record the layout once with tools/record_ground_truth.py")
    entries = record_boxes(objects, arg_value(rest, "--optitrack-server", "127.0.0.1"),
                           arg_value(rest, "--optitrack-local", "127.0.0.1"))
    old = {}
    if gt_path and os.path.exists(gt_path):
        with open(gt_path) as f:
            old = {e.get("rb_id"): e for e in (json.load(f).get(layout_id) or [])}
    print(f"BOXES | read now from OptiTrack ({source}):", flush=True)
    for e in entries:
        o = old.get(e["rb_id"])
        moved = "" if o is None else f"  ({math.hypot(e['x'] - o['x'], e['y'] - o['y']):.2f} m from {layout_id} in the file)"
        print(f"BOXES |   rb {e['rb_id']:>3} {e['class_name']:<6} x={e['x']:+.3f} y={e['y']:+.3f} "
              f"yaw={math.degrees(e['yaw']):+6.1f} deg{moved}", flush=True)
    data = {layout_id: entries}
    if run_id:
        data[run_id] = entries
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(gt_out) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    with open(gt_out, "w") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    if run_id and gt_path and os.path.exists(gt_path):
        try:
            with open(gt_path) as f:
                allgt = json.load(f)
            allgt[run_id] = entries
            with open(gt_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(dict(sorted(allgt.items())), f, indent=2)
                f.write("\n")
        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
            print(f"BOXES | could not add {run_id} to {gt_path} ({e}); the positions are in {gt_out}", flush=True)
    return set_arg(rest, "--ground-truth", gt_out)


def show_plan(robots, rest):
    """--plan-only: reads where the robots are NOW (OptiTrack) and shows the
    arc every robot would travel from there; nothing moves."""
    from acquisition import survey

        finally:
            hub.close()

                                                        n_stations=len(team))
    for line in lines + problems:
        print(line)
    if a.plan_png:
        survey.draw_sectors(a.plan_png, arena, a.margin, boxes, groups, team, paths,
                            circle=(survey.circle_center_of(a, arena, boxes), a.radius) if a.radius else None,
                            placed=starts if a.radius else None)
        print(f"\nplan drawn in {a.plan_png}")


def plan_lines(starts, team, boxes, center, arena, a, n_stations):
    """Text and drawing of the team plan (survey.team_plan): (lines,
    problems, groups, paths, track). problems is not empty when a fixed
    position of round 0 cannot be used. n_stations: the robots of the WHOLE
    team (also one that is not running), so the fixed positions never
    depend on which robots are up."""
    from acquisition import survey
    face, r0, arcs = survey.team_plan(starts, team, boxes, center, arena, a, n_stations=n_stations)
    lines, problems = [], []
    if a.radius is not None:
        c = survey.circle_center_of(a, arena, boxes)
        which = "centre of the boxes" if a.circle_center is None else "--circle-center"
        lines.append(f"fixed positions: circle r={a.radius:g} m around ({c[0]:+.2f}, {c[1]:+.2f}) ({which}); "
                     f"every robot {a.sweep_deg:g} deg {a.direction}, one round every {a.step_deg:g} deg")
        lines.append(f"radius that fits: from {survey.min_radius(a, arena, boxes):.2f} m (clear of every box of "
                     f"this layout by --keep-out-m {a.keep_out_m:g}) to {survey.max_radius(a, arena, boxes):.2f} m "
                     f"(--margin {a.margin:g} from the arena border)")
    else:
        lines.append(f"every robot {a.sweep_deg:g} deg {a.direction} around the boxes, one round every "
                     f"{a.step_deg:g} deg:")
    groups, paths, track = [], [], {}
    for rid in team:
        x, y = r0[rid]
        if a.radius is not None:
            why = survey.station_problem((x, y), boxes, arena, a)
            if why:
                problems.append(f"ERROR: the fixed position of {rid} ({x:+.2f}, {y:+.2f}) is {why}: use a "
                                f"smaller --radius, another --circle-center, or move the boxes")
        seq, legs, prev, pts = [dict(stop=0, x=x, y=y)], [], (x, y), [(0, x, y)]
        if a.radius is not None:
            legs.append([tuple(starts[rid][:2]), (x, y)])
        line = f"{rid}: r0 ({x:+.2f}, {y:+.2f})"
        for k, caps in enumerate(arcs[rid], start=1):
            if not caps:
                line += f"  r{k} stays"
                continue
            c = caps[0]
            seq.append(c)
            legs.append([prev, (c["x"], c["y"])])
            prev = (c["x"], c["y"])
            pts.append((k, c["x"], c["y"]))
            line += f"  r{k} ({c['x']:+.2f}, {c['y']:+.2f})"
        lines.append(line)
        groups.append(seq)
        paths.append(legs)
        track[rid] = pts
    return lines, problems, groups, paths, track


def wait_for_enter(live, stop_req):
    """Waits for ENTER on this console without blocking (the live window
    stays responsive, Ctrl+C still works). True = start, False = cancelled."""
    if os.name == "nt":
        import msvcrt
        while not stop_req.is_set():
            while msvcrt.kbhit():
                if msvcrt.getwch() in ("\r", "\n"):
                    return True
            live.wait(0.2)
        return False
    import select
    while not stop_req.is_set():
        ready, _, _ = select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], 0)
        if ready:
            sys.stdin.readline()
            return True
        live.wait(0.2)
    return False


class LiveRounds:
    """Analyses every round as soon as the whole team has finished it."""

    def __init__(self, la, rest, team, sync_dir, show):
        from acquisition import survey
        from vf.fusion.sensor_model import arena_from_regions, sensor_from_arguments, zones_from_arguments
        from vf.fusion.localization_methods import METHODS
        sp = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        survey.add_survey_arguments(sp)
        sa, _unknown = sp.parse_known_args(rest)
        self.sa = sa
        self.track = None                     # planned path of every robot (path preview)
        self.layout, self.out, self.gt = sa.layout_id, sa.out, sa.ground_truth
        self.offsets = sa.yaw_offsets_deg
        self.arena = arena_from_regions(sa.regions) if sa.regions else survey.ARENA_DEFAULT
        self.sensor = sensor_from_arguments(la, self.arena)
        self.zones = zones_from_arguments(la, self.arena)
        self.methods = list(METHODS)
        self.range_fit = la.range_fit
        self.team, self.sync_dir = team, sync_dir
        self.folder = os.path.join(self.out, "rounds_live")
        os.makedirs(self.folder, exist_ok=True)
        self.done_rounds = set()
        self.show = show
        self.fig = None
        if show:
            try:
                import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
                plt.ion()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"live window not available ({e}): figures only saved", flush=True)
                self.show = False

    def _points(self):
        from pipeline.build_scans import load_points, load_truth
        pts = load_points(self.out, self.range_fit)
        pts = {k: v for k, v in pts.items() if v["round"] is not None}    # round-mode captures only
        truth = load_truth(self.gt).get(self.layout, [])
        return {k: v for k, v in pts.items() if v["layout"] == self.layout}, truth

    def preview(self, starts, wait_enter):
        """Draws the path every robot is going to travel (from where it was
        placed), shows it and, with wait_enter, waits for Enter before the
        robots start. Returns False if the start is cancelled."""
        from acquisition import survey
        boxes, center, arena, _plan = survey.load_plan(self.sa, 0.0, quiet=True, need_plan=False)
        team = [r for r in self.team if r in starts]
        lines, problems, groups, paths, track = plan_lines(starts, team, boxes, center, arena, self.sa,
                                                           n_stations=len(self.team))
        for line in lines + problems:
            print(f"PATH | {line}", flush=True)
        self.track = track
        png = os.path.join(self.out, f"path_preview_{self.layout}.png")
        fixed = self.sa.radius is not None
        survey.draw_sectors(png, arena, self.sa.margin, boxes, groups, team, paths,
                            circle=(survey.circle_center_of(self.sa, arena, boxes), self.sa.radius) if fixed else None,
                            placed=starts if fixed else None)
        print(f"PATH | preview saved in {png}", flush=True)
        if self.show:
            try:
                import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
                img = plt.imread(png)
                fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7, 6.5))
                plt.imshow(img)
                plt.axis("off")
                plt.title("path preview: r0 = " + ("fixed position (x = where the robot is now)" if fixed
                                                   else "where each robot is now") + ", r1, r2, ... the rounds")
                self._display(fig)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"PATH | cannot show the preview ({e})", flush=True)
        if problems:
            print("PATH | not started: fix the plan and launch again", flush=True)
            return False
        if not wait_enter:
            return True
        print("PATH | press ENTER here to start the robots, Ctrl+C to cancel", flush=True)
        return wait_for_enter(self, self.stop_req)

    def _scene(self, name, title, members, pts, truth, rnd, off, keep_open):
        from pipeline.analyze_rounds import draw_scene, fuse, scene_rows
        poses, per_class, results = fuse(members, pts, self.sensor, self.zones, self.methods)
        rows = scene_rows(name, self.layout, rnd, off, members, pts, truth, results, self.methods)
        fig = draw_scene(os.path.join(self.folder, name + ".png"), title, members, pts, truth, poses,
                         per_class, results, self.methods, self.sensor, self.arena, rows, keep_open=keep_open,
                         track=self.track, round_now=rnd if isinstance(rnd, int) else None)
        return rows, fig

    def _display(self, fig):
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        if self.fig is not None:
            plt.close(self.fig)
        self.fig = fig
        fig.show()
        plt.pause(0.05)

    def poll(self):
        """Analyse the rounds completed since the last call."""
        k = 0
        while True:
            if k not in self.done_rounds:
                marks = [os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.sync_dir, f"r{k}_{r}")) for r in self.team]
                if not all(marks):
                    break
                self.analyse_round(k)
                self.done_rounds.add(k)
            k += 1

    def analyse_round(self, k):
        from pipeline.analyze_rounds import METHOD_LABELS, round_line
        try:
            pts, truth = self._points()
            if not truth:
                print(f"LIVE | no ground truth for {self.layout}: round {k} not analysed", flush=True)
                return
            header = "".join(f"{METHOD_LABELS[m]:>14}" for m in self.methods)
            for i, off in enumerate(self.offsets):
                members = sorted(key for key, v in pts.items() if v["round"] == k and v["yaw_offset"] == off)
                if not members:
                    continue
                name = f"{self.layout}_r{k:02d}_{off:+.0f}"
                show_it = self.show and i == 0
                rows, fig = self._scene(name, f"LIVE  layout {self.layout}, round {k}, yaw offset {off:+.0f} deg",
                                        members, pts, truth, k, off, keep_open=show_it)
                if i == 0:
                    print(f"LIVE | round {k} (estimated/true, OSPA):{header}", flush=True)
                print(f"LIVE | round {k} offset {off:+4.0f} deg:          {round_line(rows, self.methods)}",
                      flush=True)
                if show_it:
                    self._display(fig)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"LIVE | round {k}: analysis failed ({e})", flush=True)

    def overall(self):
        from pipeline.analyze_rounds import round_line
        try:
            pts, truth = self._points()
            if not pts or not truth:
                return
            rows, fig = self._scene(f"{self.layout}_overall",
                                    f"layout {self.layout}, ALL rounds together ({len(pts)} captures)",
                                    sorted(pts), pts, truth, "all", "all", keep_open=self.show)
            print(f"LIVE | ALL rounds together:                {round_line(rows, self.methods)}", flush=True)
            if self.show:
                self._display(fig)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"LIVE | overall analysis failed ({e})", flush=True)

    def wait(self, seconds):
        if self.show:
            import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
            plt.pause(seconds)
        else:
            time.sleep(seconds)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--robot", action="append", required=True, help="ID:RIGID_BODY[:CAMERA_CALIB], one per robot")
    p.add_argument("--no-live", action="store_true", help="no live window (the round figures are still saved)")
    p.add_argument("--no-confirm", action="store_true",
                   help="do not wait for ENTER after the path preview: the robots start at once")
    p.add_argument("--range-fit", type=float, nargs=2, default=None, metavar=("A", "B"),
                   help="live analysis: distance correction measured = A * true + B")
    p.add_argument("--box", action="append", default=[], metavar="RB:CLASS",
                   help="OptiTrack rigid body of one box (repeat for every box); default: the rigid bodies "
                        "saved in --ground-truth for --layout-id")
    p.add_argument("--fixed-boxes", action="store_true",
                   help="do NOT read the boxes from OptiTrack: use the positions in --ground-truth")
    from vf.fusion.sensor_model import add_sensor_arguments
    add_sensor_arguments(p)
    a, rest = p.parse_known_args()
    robots = [parse_robot(s) for s in a.robot]
    layout_id = arg_value(rest, "--layout-id", "run")
    if "--plan-only" in rest:
        import tempfile
        rest = boxes_for_this_run(a, rest, layout_id, None,
                                  os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ground_truth_now.json"))
        show_plan(robots, [x for x in rest if x != "--plan-only"])
        return

    # every launch is a new run in its own folder: <out>/<layout>_<date-time>/
    out = "data/survey/"
    if "--out" in rest:
        i = rest.index("--out")
        out = rest[i + 1]
        rest = rest[:i] + rest[i + 2:]
    run_id = f"{layout_id}_{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
    run_dir = os.path.join(out, run_id)
    os.makedirs(run_dir, exist_ok=True)
    rest = rest + ["--out", run_dir, "--run-id", run_id]
    # the boxes of THIS run, read now from OptiTrack: plan, live figures and
    # analysis all use them (written in <run>/ground_truth.json)
    rest = boxes_for_this_run(a, rest, layout_id, run_id, os.path.join(run_dir, "ground_truth.json"))
    sync_dir = os.path.join(run_dir, "sync")
    print(f"run {run_id}: data in {run_dir}", flush=True)
    team = [r["robot_id"] for r in robots]

    # Ctrl+C is handled HERE only: the survey.py processes ignore it and are
    # told to stop through the file "abort" in the sync folder, so each one
    # stops its robot, closes the camera and the connection, and exits by
    # itself. The processes are started exactly as before (same console, no
    # redirected input): the robot connection is not affected.
    stop_req = threading.Event()

    def on_ctrl_c(signum, frame):
        if stop_req.is_set():
            print("Ctrl+C again: still stopping the robots, please wait", flush=True)
        stop_req.set()

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, on_ctrl_c)

    procs = []
    for k, r in enumerate(robots):
        if stop_req.is_set():
            break
        others = [str(o["rb"]) for o in robots if o is not r]
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-u", "-m", "acquisition.survey", "--robot-id", r["robot_id"],
               "--optitrack-rb-id", str(r["rb"]), "--team"] + team + ["--sync-dir", sync_dir,
               "--ignore-ctrl-c", "--wait-go"]
        if others:
            cmd += ["--others"] + others
        if r["calib"]:
            cmd += ["--camera-calib", r["calib"]]
        cmd += rest
        print(f"{r['robot_id']}: rigid body {r['rb']}, calibration {r['calib'] or 'NONE'}", flush=True)
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        proc.robot_id = r["robot_id"]
        connected = threading.Event()
        threading.Thread(target=pump, args=(proc, r["robot_id"], connected), daemon=True).start()
        procs.append(proc)
        t0 = time.time()
        while not connected.is_set() and not stop_req.is_set() and time.time() - t0 < CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S:
            time.sleep(0.1)
        if not connected.is_set() and not stop_req.is_set():
            print(f"{r['robot_id']}: not connected after {CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S:.0f} s, starting the next robot",
                  flush=True)
        time.sleep(1.0)                  # let the SDK release the discovery port

    live = LiveRounds(a, rest, team, sync_dir, show=not a.no_live)
    live.stop_req = stop_req
    # path preview: as soon as every running robot has published where it
    # stands, then the robots wait for "go"
    starts = None
    while not stop_req.is_set() and any(pr.poll() is None for pr in procs):
        alive = [pr.robot_id for pr in procs if pr.poll() is None]
        files = {r: os.path.join(sync_dir, f"start_{r}.json") for r in alive}
        if all(os.path.exists(f) for f in files.values()):
            starts = {}
            for r, f in files.items():
                with open(f) as fh:
                    q = json.load(fh)
                starts[r] = (q["x"], q["y"])
            break
        live.wait(0.2)
    if starts and not stop_req.is_set():
        if live.preview(starts, wait_enter=not a.no_confirm):
            with open(os.path.join(sync_dir, "go"), "w") as f:
                f.write("go\n")
            print("PATH | start confirmed: the robots begin", flush=True)
        else:
            stop_req.set()
    stuck = StuckReports(sync_dir, team)
    while any(pr.poll() is None for pr in procs) and not stop_req.is_set():
        live.poll()
        stuck.poll()
        live.wait(0.3)
    if stop_req.is_set():
        stop_all(procs, sync_dir)
    else:
        live.poll()
        live.overall()
    print(f"all robots finished; data in {run_dir}, round figures in {live.folder}", flush=True)
    if live.show and live.fig is not None and not stop_req.is_set():
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        print("close the figure window to exit", flush=True)
        plt.ioff()
        plt.show()


def stop_all(procs, sync_dir, grace_s=30.0):
    """Asks every survey.py to stop (file "abort" in the sync folder) and
    waits for them to stop their robot and close the connection; only a
    process that does not exit in time is killed (its robot then stops by
    itself within 0.3 s, its watchdog)."""
    print("STOP: stopping all robots and closing the connections...", flush=True)
    try:
        os.makedirs(sync_dir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(sync_dir, "abort"), "w") as f:
            f.write("stop requested\n")
    except OSError as e:
        print(f"cannot write the abort file ({e}): killing the processes", flush=True)
        grace_s = 0.0
    t0 = time.time()
    while any(pr.poll() is None for pr in procs) and time.time() - t0 < grace_s:
        time.sleep(0.2)
    for pr in procs:
        if pr.poll() is None:
            print(f"{pr.robot_id}: not stopped after {grace_s:.0f} s, killed "
                  f"(its robot stops by itself within 0.3 s, its watchdog)", flush=True)
            pr.kill()
    for pr in procs:
        print(f"{pr.robot_id}: exit code {pr.poll()}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
==> ./acquisition/pack_runs.py <==
"""Packs the runs WITHOUT the images: only the text data needed for the analysis (a few hundred KB per run).

Keeps, for every run folder: P*.jsonl, ground_truth.json, obstacles.json (if any), raw/*.jsonl and raw/meta_*.json.
Leaves out frames/ (the big part), sync/ and rounds_live/.

    python -m acquisition.pack_runs survey_rounds/ runs_light.zip
    python -m acquisition.pack_runs survey_rounds/ runs_light.zip --only L4_ L5_ L6_     # only the runs whose folder starts with ...
"""
import argparse
import os
import zipfile

KEEP_ROOT = (".jsonl", ".json")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("survey_dir")
    ap.add_argument("out_zip")
    ap.add_argument("--only", nargs="*", default=None, help="prefixes of the run folders to include")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    runs = sorted(d for d in os.listdir(a.survey_dir)
                  if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(a.survey_dir, d)) and "_" in d
                  and (not a.only or any(d.startswith(p) for p in a.only)))
    n_files = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(a.out_zip, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for run in runs:
            base = os.path.join(a.survey_dir, run)
            for name in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
                p = os.path.join(base, name)
                if os.path.isfile(p) and name.endswith(KEEP_ROOT):
                    z.write(p, os.path.join(run, name)); n_files += 1
            raw = os.path.join(base, "raw")
            if os.path.isdir(raw):
                for name in sorted(os.listdir(raw)):
                    if name.endswith(KEEP_ROOT):
                        z.write(os.path.join(raw, name), os.path.join(run, "raw", name)); n_files += 1
    size = os.path.getsize(a.out_zip) / 1e6
    print(f"{len(runs)} run(s), {n_files} files -> {a.out_zip} ({size:.1f} MB)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./acquisition/record_obstacle.py <==
"""Records where the OCCLUDERS are (OptiTrack rigid bodies on the cartons), once per run.

The occluders are NOT boxes of the layout: launch_all.py only reads the rigid bodies of the boxes
(--box / rb_id in the ground truth), so the occluders never enter the ground truth and are never
counted as targets. This script saves their positions apart, in <run>/obstacles.json, to know exactly
where they stood (to explain the results, and to reproduce them in the simulator).

Run it right after launch_all.py has started the run (or just before it, with the cartons already in
place and not moved afterwards), with the run folder as --out:

    python -m acquisition.record_obstacle --rb 20 21 22 --out data/survey_rounds/L12_20261026-153000/ --size 0.30 0.30 0.30

--size: side of each carton [m], same order as --rb (used by the analysis as the radius of the blocked
region; default 0.30).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import time

from vf.localization.mocap_pose import MocapHub


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--rb", type=int, nargs="+", required=True, help="OptiTrack rigid body ids of the occluders")
    ap.add_argument("--size", type=float, nargs="*", default=None, help="side of each carton [m]")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="run folder (obstacles.json is written inside)")
    ap.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=2.0, help="averaging time")
    ap.add_argument("--optitrack-server", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--optitrack-local", default="127.0.0.1")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    sizes = a.size or [0.30] * len(a.rb)
    if len(sizes) != len(a.rb):
        raise SystemExit("--size needs one value per --rb")

    hub = MocapHub(a.rb, a.optitrack_server, a.optitrack_local)
    samples = {rb: [] for rb in a.rb}
    try:
        try:
            hub.wait_ready()
        except RuntimeError as e:
            raise SystemExit(f"OptiTrack: {e}")
        t0 = time.time()
        while time.time() - t0 < a.seconds:
            for rb in a.rb:
                q = hub.get_pose(rb)
                if q is not None:
                    samples[rb].append((q[0], q[1]))
            time.sleep(0.02)
    finally:
        hub.close()

    obstacles = []
    for rb, size in zip(a.rb, sizes):
        s = samples[rb]
        if not s:
            raise SystemExit(f"no OptiTrack reading for rigid body {rb}: check it in Motive")
        x = sum(p[0] for p in s) / len(s)
        y = sum(p[1] for p in s) / len(s)
        obstacles.append(dict(rb_id=rb, x=round(x, 4), y=round(y, 4), size_m=size))
        print(f"obstacle rb {rb}: x={x:+.3f} y={y:+.3f} (side {size:g} m)")
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(a.out, "obstacles.json")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(obstacles, f, indent=2)
    print(f"written {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
==> ./acquisition/regroup_captures.py <==
"""Rebuilds the captures of a survey from the RAW readings (every frame),
with a different grouping threshold, without running the robots again.

Every capture is --n-readings frames; the detections of all its frames are
grouped by position into physical objects (one row per object, the reading
whose distance is closest to the median of its group), exactly as
static_trial.capture_trial does during the survey. During the survey the
threshold is --instance-threshold-m (default 0.5 m): two boxes closer than
that, seen by the same robot, become ONE object. This script redoes the
grouping with another threshold and writes a new survey folder that
pipeline/analyze_rounds.py / pipeline/build_scans.py / pipeline/evaluate_runs.py read as usual.

    python -m acquisition.regroup_captures --survey-dir data/survey_rounds/ --out survey_rounds_t015/ --threshold 0.15

Input: <run>/raw/<robot>.jsonl (one row per frame, written by survey.py)
and <run>/<robot>.jsonl (for the capture metadata). Output: the same run
folders with new <robot>.jsonl files (ground_truth.json is copied).
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import shutil
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np

from vf.perception.object_position import cluster_by_position

META_KEYS = ("trial_id", "robot_id", "layout_id", "stop", "radius_m", "angle_deg", "yaw_offset_deg",
             "fault_injected", "dropped", "zone", "round", "run_id")


def regroup_capture(frames, threshold_m):
    """frames: raw rows of ONE capture. Returns one dict per physical object
    (detections grouped across the frames by position)."""
    dets = []
    for f in frames:
        for d in f["detections"]:
            if d.get("class_name") and d.get("position") is not None:
                dets.append(dict(d, robot_pose=f.get("camera_pose"), t=f["t"]))
    if not dets:
        return []
    labels = cluster_by_position([tuple(d["position"]) for d in dets], threshold_m=threshold_m)
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for d, k in zip(dets, labels):
        groups[k].append(d)
    out = []
    for g in groups.values():
        with_d = [d for d in g if d.get("distance") is not None]
        if len(with_d) >= 2:
            med = float(np.median([d["distance"] for d in with_d]))
            rep = min(with_d, key=lambda d: abs(d["distance"] - med))
        else:
            rep = g[0]
        out.append(rep)
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--survey-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=0.15,
                    help="detections of one capture closer than this are the same object [m]")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    raw_files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(a.survey_dir, "**", "raw", "*.jsonl"), recursive=True))
    if not raw_files:
        raise SystemExit(f"no raw/*.jsonl under {a.survey_dir}: the runs were recorded before the raw readings "
                         f"were saved")
    for raw in raw_files:
        run_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(raw))
        robot = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(raw))[0]
        rel = os.path.relpath(run_dir, a.survey_dir)
        out_dir = os.path.join(a.out, rel)
        os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
        gt = os.path.join(run_dir, "ground_truth.json")
        if os.path.exists(gt):
            shutil.copy(gt, out_dir)
        meta = {}
        main_file = os.path.join(run_dir, f"{robot}.jsonl")
        if os.path.exists(main_file):
            with open(main_file) as f:
                for line in f:
                    if line.strip():
                        r = json.loads(line)
                        meta.setdefault((r["trial_id"], r.get("round")), {k: r.get(k) for k in META_KEYS})
        caps = defaultdict(list)
        with open(raw) as f:
            for line in f:
                if line.strip():
                    r = json.loads(line)
                    caps[(r["trial_id"], r.get("round"))].append(r)
        n_in = n_out = 0
        with open(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{robot}.jsonl"), "w") as f:
            for key, frames in caps.items():
                m = meta.get(key)
                if m is None:
                    continue
                objs = regroup_capture(frames, a.threshold)
                pose = next((fr["camera_pose"] for fr in frames if fr.get("camera_pose")), None)
                rows = [dict(class_name=o["class_name"], confidence=o.get("confidence", 1.0),
                             position=o["position"], distance=o.get("distance"), bearing_rad=o.get("bearing_rad"),
                             viewing_angle_rad=o.get("viewing_angle_rad"), robot_pose=o.get("robot_pose") or pose,
                             t=o["t"], **m) for o in objs]
                if not rows:
                    rows = [dict(class_name=None, confidence=0.0, distance=None, bearing_rad=None,
                                 viewing_angle_rad=None, robot_pose=pose, t=frames[0]["t"], **m)]
                for r in rows:
                    f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
                n_in += 1
                n_out += sum(1 for r in rows if r["class_name"])
        print(f"{rel}/{robot}: {n_in} capture(s), {n_out} object(s) with threshold {a.threshold:g} m")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
==> ./docs/commands.md <==
# Commands

Run every command from the repository root. Scripts are run as modules (`python -m <package>.<script>`).

## Live demo: every method continuously, in the browser

The robots stand still and stream what they see. Place them, move them by hand, move, add or take away boxes, put
other objects in the way, at any time: the page follows within a second for MHT, MHT with sensor model and the
graph network, within a few seconds for the two image networks.

`demo/live.py` only reads the files the robots write, so it runs in its own terminal and its own Python environment
(the robot SDK needs an old Python; the networks need a recent one with `torch`). One-time setup on the capture PC,
from the repository root:

    py -3.11 -m venv .venv_demo
    .venv_demo\Scripts\activate.bat
    pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
    pip install transformers pillow opencv-python numpy scipy matplotlib

Terminal 1 (the usual capture environment): the robots and OptiTrack. It starts one camera process per robot, one
after the other, and writes the boxes OptiTrack tracks inside the arena (every box must be a rigid body in Motive,
11-17). Ctrl+C here stops every robot; `--windows` also shows the camera window of each robot.

    python -m demo.live_robots --robot P0:8 --robot P1:7 --robot P3:10:config/checkerboard_calib_P1.json --robot P5:6:config/checkerboard_calib_P1.json

Terminal 2 (demo environment): the methods and the page, http://localhost:8000. The first start downloads the
segmentation models (Grounding DINO, SAM) once.

    .venv_demo\Scripts\activate.bat
    python -m demo.live

Moving the robots from the page: click a robot (or its button in the "Move" bar), then a point of any map: the
robot drives there on a path clear of the boxes and of the other robots and arrives facing the centre of the
boxes (acquisition/live_drive.py, the controller of the captures). "turn left/right" turns it by 22.5 degrees,
"face the boxes" turns it towards them, "stop" halts it, "stop all robots" halts every robot. Goals too close to a
box or to the arena border are refused, and the reason shows next to the buttons. `--no-drive` on
`demo.live_robots` turns this off (robots moved only by hand).

Each panel shows the boxes its method finds now against the true boxes, the verdict (correct, too few, too many,
misplaced), how old its input is and how often it was correct in the last 30 seconds; above the panels, the
difficulty level of the scene as it is now; below, the frames of the robots with the box masks and the markers.

Camera angles for the image networks: by default the pitch and yaw offset of each camera are fitted continuously on
the markers the robots see. To fix them before the demo, leave the robots looking at some boxes for a minute while
saving them, then start the demo with the file:

    python -m demo.live --write-camera-calib config/demo_cameras.json
    python -m demo.live --camera-calib config/demo_cameras.json

Rehearsal without robots: a recorded run played as if it were live, one round every 4 seconds:

    python -m demo.live --replay data/survey_v2/R01_20261109-153345F --replay-every 4

Other options: `--window-s` (seconds of detections pooled per object, default 1), `--no-images` (only the methods
on the detections, for a PC without GPU), `--gnn`, `--image`, `--image-markers` (variant folders in `results/`),
`--port`. A method whose packages or model files are missing is shown as "not available" and the others keep
working.

## GNN trained on the simulator

Needs PyTorch (`pip install torch`). Build every set (training 50,000 scenes, validation 2,000, T0-T7 1,000 each) and run the classical methods on T0-T7:

    python -m sim.make_sets --model config/sensor_model.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json

Main model (robot nodes, all inputs, ring neighbours, 2 hops, 5 seeds), tested on T0-T7 and on the 56 real scenes:

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --standard-tests --graph robot --features full --edges ring --hops 2 --out results/gnn_sim/

The other variants change only the last flags:

    --graph robot --features positions --edges ring --hops 2         (positions only)
    --graph detection --features full --edges ring --hops 2          (detection nodes)
    --graph detection --features positions --edges ring --hops 2
    --graph robot --features full --edges range --comm-range 1.5 --hops 1   (also --hops 2, --hops 3)
    --graph robot --features full --edges full --hops 1               (upper bound: every robot hears every robot)
    --graph robot --features full --edges opposite --hops 2           (each robot linked to the robot in front and the two diagonals)
    --graph robot --features full --edges full --hops 2               (every robot linked to every robot, 2 rounds)

Each variant writes `results/gnn_sim/<variant>/summary.csv` (GNN mean and sd over the seeds, classical methods on the same scenes) and `mcnemar.csv`. `--eval-only` re-evaluates saved models; `--max-train 2000 --epochs 3 --seeds 1` is a quick check that everything runs.

Real scenes with more viewpoints: the rounds of each real run are combined (4, 8, ... 28 viewpoints) and the classical methods are run on them; then every trained variant is evaluated on them (no training, writes `summary_combined.csv` next to `summary.csv`):

    python -m pipeline.combine_rounds --regions config/optitrack_regions.json
    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --combined-tests --eval-only --graph robot --features full --edges ring --hops 2 --out results/gnn_sim/

(same `--eval-only` command with the flags of every other variant)

## Two-circle scenario (targets in an inner circle, robots on an outer circle, communication range)

Sets: training (3-10 robots), validation, the nominal test C0 (6 robots at 1.5 m, inner circle 0.7 m) and its variants with 3-16 robots (Cn*), with the classical methods:

    python -m sim.make_sets --model config/sensor_model.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --sets circle

GNN whose robots exchange messages only within a communication range, drawn between 0.5 and 5 m for every training scene, with the three skip-connection variants:

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_Ctrain/ --val-dir data/sim_Cval/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --circle-tests --edges range --comm-range-train 0.5 5 --comm-range 2.0 --skip residual --out results/gnn_circle/
    (same with --skip none and --skip jk)

The same models at other communication ranges (no training; 1 m: no neighbour, 2 m: the nearest ones, 3.2 m: everyone with 6 robots at 1.5 m):

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_Ctrain/ --val-dir data/sim_Cval/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --circle-tests --edges range --comm-range-train 0.5 5 --comm-range 1.0 --skip residual --eval-only --results-name comm1.0 --out results/gnn_circle/

Distributed GNN (--association local): two detections are associated only if their robots are at most --hops links apart in the communication graph, so the communication range and the number of hops limit what each robot can merge (folder suffix _local). Same commands with --association local, e.g. hops 1-3 and the three skip variants:

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_Ctrain/ --val-dir data/sim_Cval/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --circle-tests --edges range --comm-range-train 0.5 5 --comm-range 2.0 --association local --hops 2 --skip residual --out results/gnn_circle/
    python -m gnn.train_sim ... --association local --hops 2 --comm-range 1.0 --eval-only --results-name comm1.0 --out results/gnn_circle/


## Re-evaluating everything after a change of the metrics (no retraining)

A box is found only by an estimate within `MATCH_CUTOFF_M` (pipeline/evaluate_runs.py, 0.15 m: half the side of a box) of its centre; P_D, RMSE* (a missed box counts as that distance), false estimates and correct scenes all follow from it. After changing it, every stored result is recomputed from the sets and the trained models:

    python -m sim.make_sets --model config/sensor_model.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --baselines-only
    python -m pipeline.evaluate_runs --survey-dir data/survey_rounds/ --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --out results/evaluation_calib/
    python -m pipeline.combine_rounds --regions config/optitrack_regions.json
    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --standard-tests --eval-only --out results/gnn_sim/
    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --combined-tests --eval-only --out results/gnn_sim/

Two-circle sets: the same with `--sets circle --baselines-only`, then `--eval-only` for each trained variant (same flags as its training).


## MHT with sensor model (the same per-detection inputs as the GNN)

`mht_sensor` (vf/fusion/sensor_aware_mht.py) is the MHT that also reads distance, line of sight and viewing angle of every report and the fitted sensor model (config/sensor_model.json). It is one of the classical methods of pipeline/evaluate_runs.py, so new evaluations include it. To add it to results already computed without running the other methods again (their rows in scenes.csv are kept):

    python -m sim.make_sets --model config/sensor_model.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --baselines-only --methods mht_sensor
    python -m sim.make_sets --model config/sensor_model.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --sets circle --baselines-only --methods mht_sensor
    python -m pipeline.evaluate_runs --survey-dir data/survey_rounds/ --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --methods mht_sensor --keep-other-methods --out results/evaluation_calib/
    python -m pipeline.combine_rounds --regions config/optitrack_regions.json --methods mht_sensor

The GNN results then compare with it after `--eval-only` (same commands as above).

GNN trained on random layouts (sim/specs/R_train.json: the R0 placement with the randomised sensor of the general training set), tested on T0-T7, the real scenes and R0:
