    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_Rtrain/ --val-dir data/sim_Rval/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --standard-tests --test R0 data/sim_R0/ data/sim_R0/ground_truth.json results/baselines_sim/R0/scenes.csv --graph detection --features full --edges ring --hops 2 --seeds 3 --out results/gnn_random/

GNN trained on both placements (ring layouts of the general training set and random layouts, 50,000 scenes each, pooled; validation on both), tested on the same sets:

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ data/sim_Rtrain/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ data/sim_Rval/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --standard-tests --test R0 data/sim_R0/ data/sim_R0/ground_truth.json results/baselines_sim/R0/scenes.csv --graph detection --features full --edges ring --hops 2 --seeds 3 --out results/gnn_mixed/


## Research plan: MHT with a learned normality gate (modules M0-M1)

M0, simulator and datasets (sim/plan.py): two scene families (circle, random) in the world frame, the nominal sensor file, the error knobs k_f, k_2, h, and every set of the plan with fixed seeds (train 50,000, gate 10,000, val 2,000, 52 test sets of 1,000 scenes: G0-G2, E1-E3, S1, V1-V2 in both families). Seeds in results/plan/seeds.csv. About 3 GB in data/plan/.

    python -m sim.plan --list
    python -m sim.plan --model config/sensor_model.json
    python -m sim.plan_check --examples --out results/plan/M0/

M1, generator and gate-input check (sim/plan_check.py) on the gate-training set: position error and detection probability against the sensor file, two-face and false-detection rates, histograms of the 8 gate-input features by family, N and B, region sizes and purity (Fig. M1-1 to M1-4, table_M1.csv):

    python -m sim.plan_check --set-dir data/plan/gate/ --out results/plan/M1/

Region link distance: 0.20 m instead of the plan's 0.35 m (pipeline/plan_regions.py LINK_M). With 0.35 m the largest region has 101 reports (M_max 64) and 27% of the regions hold two or more boxes, also in G0; with 0.20 m 54 reports, 7% (3% in G0), 0.4% of the boxes split over two regions.

M2, MHT setup (pipeline/plan_mht.py): MHT with sensor model in simulation without the two real-data terms, H in {100, 300, 1000}, three random robot orders, on the validation set; writes table_M2.csv, fig_M2-1 and prints the chosen H (smallest within 0.5 points of H = 1000). Then MHT with the chosen H on the gate-training set, and M1-3 again on the regions MHT gets right only:

    python -m pipeline.plan_mht --sets data/plan/val/ --hypotheses 100 300 1000 --orders 3 --choose-h --out results/plan/M2/
    python -m pipeline.plan_mht --sets data/plan/gate/ --hypotheses H --orders 1 --out results/plan/M2/
    python -m sim.plan_check --set-dir data/plan/gate/ --out results/plan/M1/ --mht-estimates results/plan/M2/gate/estimates_HH_o0.jsonl
(replace H with the chosen value)

M2 result: H = 100 (70.47% correct on validation; 300 and 1000 give 70.52%), the three orders within 1 point, so one order from here on.

M3, MHT failure map (pipeline/plan_failure_map.py): MHT with H = 100 on every test set, S1 also with H = 300 and 1000; table_M3.csv, one figure per scenario, kept_cases.csv (special cases where MHT loses at least 5 points from G0):

    python -m pipeline.plan_mht --sets "data/plan/G*" "data/plan/E*" "data/plan/V*" --hypotheses 100 --out results/plan/M3/
    python -m pipeline.plan_mht --sets "data/plan/S1_*" --hypotheses 100 300 1000 --out results/plan/M3/
    python -m pipeline.plan_failure_map --results results/plan/M3/ --out results/plan/M3/ --data data/plan/

(--data adds the share of scenes in which every box was reported by some robot, and MHT's correct share on those.)

Evaluation scenarios kept for the thesis (advisor: at most 3-4): the nominal scene G0 as reference, E1 (false detections x1-8), E3 (robots hidden by obstacles, h 0-2), S1 (dense boxes 20 cm apart, B 4-16); both families. Dropped: E2 (MHT loses at most 6 points), G1, G2, V2 (MHT flat), V1 (nearly no scene has every box reported).

M4, GNN and oracle selector (pipeline/plan_oracle.py): detection-node GNN trained on the plan's training set (nominal sensor, both families, every pair of robots linked, edges within 1 m), 3 seeds, its boxes saved on the kept test sets; then the region-level oracle against MHT (H = 100):

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/plan/train/ --val-dir data/plan/val/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --graph detection --features full --edges full --hops 2 --seeds 3 --plan-tests "G0_*" "E1_*" "E3_*" "S1_*" --save-estimates --out results/plan/M4/gnn/
    python -m pipeline.plan_oracle --sets "G0_*" "E1_*" "E3_*" "S1_*" --mht results/plan/M3/ --gnn results/plan/M4/gnn/detection_full_full_h2/ --out results/plan/M4/


## Image-level simulator (imgsim/)

imgsim/render.py renders the camera image of every robot in a scene of sim/plan.py (same seeds: scene i of data/imgsim/<set>/ is scene i of data/plan/<set>/), with the real camera calibration, the camera height and pitch measured on the real frames, the real boxes (white, blue tape, ArUco 4X4_50 id 0, 77 mm), obstacles, the other robots, the room and the robot's own gripper (imgsim/assets, from the real frames of P5). imgsim/generate.py runs the real detector (vf/perception/aruco_detector.py) on 5 frames per stop and keeps one detection per group closer than 0.2 m, as acquisition/static_trial.capture_trial does on the robots, and writes the reports in the format of the real runs. imgsim/compare.py fits the range / bearing calibration of an image set (as pipeline/calibrate.py) and compares the image reports with the sensor file fitted on the real runs (Fig. IMG-1 to IMG-3, table_IMG.csv). Needs OpenCV with cv2.aruco (opencv-python >= 4.7 or opencv-contrib-python).

E1 and E2 multiply rates of the sensor file, which the renderer does not use: in the images false detections and second faces come from the detector itself, so only G0, E3 and S1 are rendered.

    python -m imgsim.generate --sets G0,E3,S1 --runs 1000 --save-images 20
    python -m imgsim.compare --set-dir data/imgsim/G0_nominal_circle/ --save-calib config/sensor_calib_imgsim.json
    python -m imgsim.compare --set-dir data/imgsim/G0_nominal_random/
    python -m pipeline.plan_mht --sets "data/imgsim/G0_*" "data/imgsim/E3_*" "data/imgsim/S1_*" --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib_imgsim.json --hypotheses 100 --out results/imgsim/M3/

GNN trained on the measurement-level sets (M4), tested on the image sets, then the oracle on the image sets:

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/plan/train/ --val-dir data/plan/val/ --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib_imgsim.json --graph detection --features full --edges full --hops 2 --seeds 3 --eval-only --plan-dir data/imgsim/ --plan-tests "G0_*" "E3_*" "S1_*" --save-estimates --results-name imgsim --out results/plan/M4/gnn/
    python -m pipeline.plan_oracle --sets "G0_*" "E3_*" "S1_*" --data data/imgsim/ --mht results/imgsim/M3/ --gnn results/plan/M4/gnn/detection_full_full_h2/ --estimates-dir estimates_imgsim --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib_imgsim.json --out results/imgsim/M4/

Appearance settings (imgsim/render.py Appearance) can be changed with --appearance <json> on imgsim.generate; --save-images -1 saves every image (for an image-based model).

## Image-based network (bevnet/)

bevnet/ learns the boxes from the camera images and the robot poses only (no ArUco, no solvePnP, no sensor file). Each robot encodes its image with a small CNN; the features are read where every cell of a 4 x 4 m floor grid (5 cm cells), lifted to 0.05, 0.20 and 0.35 m, falls in the image (known pose, pitch and lens) and turned into a message of --message channels per cell it sees; the team fuses the messages (mean, maximum, number of robots per cell) and a U-Net on the floor grid gives the probability of a box centre per cell and its offset. Boxes = local maxima above a threshold chosen on the validation set; same "correct scene" metric as MHT and the GNN (count right, every box within 15 cm). The scenes are those of sim/plan.py (same seeds), rendered by imgsim/render.py at 256 x 144 (--scale 0.2). Needs PyTorch (pip install torch; a CUDA GPU makes training minutes instead of hours).

Render the sets (about 80 kB per scene: 4 GB for the 50,000 training scenes):

    python -m bevnet.data --sets train,val,G0,E3,S1
    python -m bevnet.data --sets train,val,G0,E3,S1 --no-markers --out data/bev_nomarkers/   # same scenes, boxes without paper and marker

Train, choose epoch and threshold on val, test (results/bev/bev_c64_m16/: model.pt, train_log.csv, test_scenes.csv, summary.csv); on a CPU only, start with --max-train 10000 --workers 4:

    python -m bevnet.train --train data/bev/train --val data/bev/val --tests "data/bev/G0_*" "data/bev/E3_*" "data/bev/S1_*"
    python -m bevnet.train --message 4 ...           # smaller message per cell (bandwidth study)
    python -m bevnet.train ... --eval-only           # test the saved model again
    python -m bevnet.train --train data/bev_nomarkers/train --val data/bev_nomarkers/val --tests "data/bev_nomarkers/G0_*" "data/bev_nomarkers/E3_*" "data/bev_nomarkers/S1_*" --out results/bev_nomarkers/

Occluders and other objects in the training scenes. --obstacles 2 puts the E3 cylinders (0, 1 or 2 per box, drawn per scene) in the training and validation scenes; --distractors N adds 0..N free-standing objects to any set; --obstacle-style random gives every obstacle its own shape (--obstacle-shapes from cylinder, box, prism, hexagon, blob), height (15-100 cm), colour (a quarter white or light grey) and pattern (plain, noise, stripes, bands, checker). Training on three shapes and testing on the two others measures how the network copes with objects it has never seen:

    python -m bevnet.data --sets train --runs 20000 --obstacles 2 --distractors 4 --obstacle-style random --obstacle-shapes cylinder,box,prism --out data/bev_rand/
    python -m bevnet.data --sets val --obstacles 2 --distractors 4 --obstacle-style random --obstacle-shapes cylinder,box,prism --out data/bev_rand/
    python -m bevnet.data --sets G0,E3 --distractors 4 --obstacle-style random --obstacle-shapes hexagon,blob --out data/bev_unseen/
    python -m bevnet.train --train data/bev_rand/train --val data/bev_rand/val --tests "data/bev/G0_*" "data/bev/E3_*" "data/bev/S1_*" --out results/bev_rand/
    python -m bevnet.train --eval-only --out results/bev_rand/ --tests "data/bev_unseen/*" --results-name unseen

Real frames (bevnet/real.py): the 56 real scenes (data/survey_rounds, 8 layouts x 7 rounds, 4 robots) in the same format, one set per reading k = 0..4 of each stop: each robot's frame resized to 256 x 144, its OptiTrack camera pose, its own camera matrix and distortion, pitch 11.5 deg (P5 22 deg), true boxes from ground_truth.json, all shifted to the centre of the robots. --check writes fig_REAL-0.png with the true box centres projected into the frames. Then any model trained in simulation is tested on them without retraining (results in summary_real.csv):

    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_rounds/*" --out data/bev_real/ --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --check
    python -m bevnet.train --eval-only --out results/bev/ --tests "data/bev_real/*" --results-name real
    python -m bevnet.train --eval-only --out results/bev_obst/ --tests "data/bev_real/*" --results-name real

Twins of the real scenes (bevnet/twin.py: same poses, pitch and boxes, rendered) and fine-tuning on the real frames, leave-one-layout-out (bevnet/finetune.py):

==> ./README.md <==
# Multi-Robot Cooperative Perception

Master's thesis code. A team of RoboMaster EP robots, localised by OptiTrack, looks at the same arena
through its cameras and has to estimate **how many boxes there are and where they are**.

Every box carries the same ArUco marker on purpose: a robot knows *what* it sees but not *which* box it is,
so deciding which observations of different robots are the same box is the core problem. Three families of
methods are implemented and compared on simulated scenes and on two real campaigns:

| Family | Input | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Classical fusion: zone and class, union, MHT, PHD, CPHD, MHT with sensor model | feature vectors of the ArUco detections | `vf/fusion/`, `pipeline/` |
| Graph neural network (one node per detection) | the same feature vectors | `gnn/` |
| Image network (features lifted to a floor grid, fused cell by cell) | camera frames as box masks, optionally with the detected markers | `bevnet/`, `imgsim/` |

Run every command from the repository root, with the scripts as modules: `python -m <package>.<script> ...`.
All the commands, in the order of the pipeline, are in `docs/commands.md`.

## Folder structure

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `robomaster_sdk/` | Robot SDK used for the data collection: connection (`robot`), camera (`camera`), robot registry (`config`) |
| `vf/` | Shared library: motion (`control/`), ArUco detection and feature vectors (`perception/`), robot pose from OptiTrack (`localization/`), fusion methods (`fusion/`: sensor model, zone and class, union, MHT, PHD/CPHD, MHT with sensor model) |
| `acquisition/` | Everything that runs with the robots: `launch_all` (all robots, round by round), `survey` (one robot driving to its stops and capturing), `static_trial` (one capture of one robot), `record_obstacle`, `regroup_captures`, `pack_runs` |
| `tools/` | Lab tools: camera and OptiTrack calibration, motion check, ground truth recorder; capture plans of the real campaigns (`capture_plan`, `capture_plan_v3`), live placement check (`place_check`), run selection (`select_runs`), difficulty levels of the scenes (`scene_levels`) |
| `pipeline/` | Processing of the recorded runs: `build_scans` (loading, sanity checks), `analyze_rounds` (fusion of one round), `calibrate` (sensor calibration), `evaluate_runs` (classical methods, metrics, figures), `combine_rounds` (real scenes with more viewpoints); on the simulated sets: `plan_mht`, `plan_failure_map`, `plan_regions`, `plan_oracle` |
| `sim/` | Measurement-level simulator: library (`geometry`, `model`, `scene`, `sensor`, `writer`), fit on the real runs (`calibrate`), check against them (`generate` replay, `fidelity`), the sets of the thesis (`plan`, `plan_check`) and the earlier training sets (`make_sets`, `specs/`) |
| `gnn/` | Graph network for the association: `dataset` (scenes from runs), `model`, `train_sim` (training on simulated scenes, evaluation on simulated and real ones) |
| `imgsim/` | Image simulator: `render` (camera images, box masks, marker channel), `generate` and `compare` (validation with the real ArUco detector) |
| `bevnet/` | Image network: `data` (rendered sets), `model`, `geometry` (floor grid and projection), `train`, `segment` (Grounding DINO + SAM masks of real frames), `real` (real scenes in the network's format), `twin`, `finetune`, `compare` |
| `demo/` | Live comparison of the methods in the browser: `live_robots` (every robot streams what it sees, OptiTrack the boxes), `live` (runs every method continuously) and its page `map.html` |
| `config/` | Arena regions, camera calibrations, ArUco ID to class map, ground truth of the layouts, sensor calibration, sensor model, appearance files of the image simulator |
| `data/` | Real runs: `survey_rounds/` (first campaign, L4-L11), `survey_v2/` (second campaign, R01-R104). Simulated and image sets are regenerated (`data/sim_*`, `data/plan`, `data/bev*`, not versioned) |
| `results/` | Outputs of every step; `results/scene_levels.csv` and `results/sim_levels.csv` hold the difficulty level of every real and simulated scene |
| `docs/` | `commands.md` (all the commands), capture plans and guides of the second campaign |

## Requirements

- Robots: the `robomaster` SDK, OpenCV with the ArUco module (`opencv-contrib-python`), numpy, matplotlib; the
  `natnet` package and Motive running, with every robot and box defined as a rigid body.
- Analysis of the classical methods: numpy, scipy, matplotlib.
- Networks: PyTorch (`torch`); for the segmentation of real frames also `transformers` and a GPU.

## Pipeline in short

1. **Calibrate once**: cameras (`tools.calibrate_camera`), OptiTrack frame if needed (`tools.calibrate_optitrack`).
2. **Capture**: place the boxes of a layout (`tools.place_check`), then `acquisition.launch_all` moves all the
   robots round by round and stores frames, detections, poses and the true boxes of the run.
3. **Classical methods on real runs**: `pipeline.calibrate` (sensor calibration), `pipeline.evaluate_runs`.
4. **Simulator**: `sim.calibrate` fits the sensor model on the real runs, `sim.fidelity` checks it,
   `sim.plan` builds the training, validation and test sets with fixed seeds.
5. **Graph network**: `gnn.train_sim` trains on the simulated sets and evaluates on simulated and real scenes;
   `pipeline.plan_mht`, `pipeline.plan_failure_map` and `pipeline.plan_oracle` give MHT and the oracle on the same sets.
6. **Image network**: `bevnet.data` renders the sets (box masks, optional marker channel), `bevnet.train`
   trains and tests, `bevnet.real` converts the real runs (segmentation, camera calibration).
7. **Difficulty levels**: `tools.scene_levels` assigns every real scene a level from its geometry.
8. **Live demo**: `demo.live_robots` and `demo.live` show every method continuously while boxes and robots are
   moved by hand.

Files set aside during clean-ups are in `_to_delete/` (not versioned).

==> ./gnn/__init__.py <==
"""GNN for multi-robot box association: scenes (dataset.py), model (model.py), training on simulated scenes and
evaluation on simulated and real ones (train_sim.py).

Run from the repository root:
    python -m gnn.train_sim ...
"""

==> ./gnn/train_sim.py <==
"""GNN trained on the simulator: training on the general environment, model selection on a validation set
of the same distribution, then one evaluation per test set (failure-prone simulated conditions T0-T7 and
the real runs). No test scene is ever used for training or for choosing anything.

    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ \\
        --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --standard-tests \\
        --graph robot --features full --edges ring --hops 2 --seeds 5 --out results/gnn_sim/

The sets come from sim.make_sets; --standard-tests tests on T0-T7 and on the 56 real scenes. Other test sets
can be added with --test (below). --combined-tests adds the real scenes with combined rounds (4 to 28
viewpoints, pipeline.combine_rounds); with --eval-only and no other test they are written to
summary_combined.csv, mcnemar_combined.csv, test_scenes_combined.csv, next to the main results:
    python -m gnn.train_sim --train-dir data/sim_train/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ \\
        --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json --combined-tests --eval-only --out results/gnn_sim/

--train-dir and --val-dir take one or more sets, pooled (e.g. ring and random layouts:
--train-dir data/sim_train/ data/sim_Rtrain/ --val-dir data/sim_val/ data/sim_Rval/).

Variant (the folder name in --out is built from it, e.g. robot_full_ring_h2):
  --graph     robot (one node per robot) | detection (one node per detection)
  --features  full (with the viewing angle) | positions (positions and robot poses only)
  --edges     ring (ring neighbours) | opposite (the robot in front and the two diagonals) |
              range (robots closer than --comm-range; --comm-range-train LO HI draws one per training
              scene) | full (every pair)
  --hops      rounds of message passing
  --skip      skip connections: residual (each hop adds to the node) | none | jk (jumping knowledge)
  --association  central (every close pair of detections is scored) | local (distributed: only pairs whose
              robots are at most --hops links apart in the communication graph; name suffix _local)

Training: Adam, --epochs at most; after every epoch the model is run on the validation scenes and the epoch
with the highest correct rate is kept (early stop after --patience epochs without improvement). --seeds
models are trained independently; every result is reported as mean and standard deviation over them.

A --test is NAME DIR GROUND_TRUTH BASELINE: BASELINE is the scenes.csv of pipeline/evaluate_runs.py on the
same runs ('-' for none). Metrics (pipeline.evaluate_runs.detection_metrics): detection probability P_D,
RMSE* over all true boxes (a missed box counts as the cut-off, 0.15 m) and false estimates per scene. The GNN and
every classical method are compared scene by scene with exact sign tests (mcnemar.csv), for every seed: on
the boxes found, on the false estimates and on "correct" (count right and every true box matched). Simulated scenes in which
no robot reported anything are counted for every method as an empty estimate.

Outputs (in --out/<variant>/): model_seed<k>.pt, variant.json, train_log.csv, test_scenes.csv (GNN, one row
per test scene and seed), summary.csv (per test set and method), mcnemar.csv. --eval-only skips the
training and evaluates the saved models.
"""

import argparse
import copy
import csv
import json
import math
import os
import time
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import torch

from gnn.dataset import build_scenes
from gnn.model import build_model, collate, decode, encode_scene, loss_fn
from pipeline.evaluate_runs import MATCH_CUTOFF_M, detection_metrics, scene_metrics

METHOD_ORDER = ["zone_class", "union", "phd", "cphd", "mht"]
LABELS = dict(zone_class="Zone+class", union="Union", phd="PHD", cphd="CPHD", mht="MHT", gnn="GNN")


def variant_name(a):
    edges = a.edges
    if a.edges == "range":
        edges = (f"range{a.comm_range_train[0]:g}to{a.comm_range_train[1]:g}" if a.comm_range_train
                 else f"range{a.comm_range:g}")
    name = f"{a.graph}_{a.features}_{edges}_h{a.hops}"
    if a.skip != "residual":
        name += f"_skip{a.skip}"
    return name if a.association == "central" else f"{name}_local"


def encode_all(scenes, a, rng=None):
    """Encoded scenes. With rng and --comm-range-train, every scene gets its own communication range drawn
    in that interval (training and validation), so one model works at any range; otherwise --comm-range."""
    ranges = ([float(rng.uniform(*a.comm_range_train)) for _ in scenes] if rng is not None and a.comm_range_train
              else [a.comm_range] * len(scenes))
    return [encode_scene(s, features=a.features, edges=a.edges, comm_range=r, gate=a.gate,
                         association=a.association, hops=a.hops)
            for s, r in zip(scenes, ranges)]


def class_weights(encoded):
    """pos_weight of the two heads: negatives / positives in the training scenes (capped at 10)."""
    pos_same = sum(float(e["same"].sum()) for e in encoded)
    n_same = sum(len(e["same"]) for e in encoded)
    pos_false = sum(float(e["false"].sum()) for e in encoded)
    n_false = sum(len(e["false"]) for e in encoded)
    return (min(10.0, (n_same - pos_same) / max(pos_same, 1)), min(10.0, (n_false - pos_false) / max(pos_false, 1)))


def predict(model, encoded, batch=64):
    """(p_same, p_false) per scene."""
    out = []
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for start in range(0, len(encoded), batch):
            chunk = encoded[start:start + batch]
            same, false = model(collate(chunk))
            same = torch.sigmoid(same).numpy()
            false = torch.sigmoid(false).numpy()
            ps = np.cumsum([0] + [len(e["pairs"]) for e in chunk])
            pd = np.cumsum([0] + [len(e["det"]) for e in chunk])
            for k in range(len(chunk)):
                out.append((same[ps[k]:ps[k + 1]], false[pd[k]:pd[k + 1]]))
    return out


def evaluate_scenes(model, scenes, encoded, a, estimates=None):
    """One metrics row per scene. With a list `estimates`, the boxes of every scene and, per box, the indices of
    the detections it was built from are appended to it (the format of pipeline.plan_mht)."""
    rows = []
    for s, e, (p_same, p_false) in zip(scenes, encoded, predict(model, encoded)):
        est, assign = decode(s["pos"], e["pairs"], p_same, p_false)
        if estimates is not None:
            members = [[int(i) for i in np.nonzero(assign == k)[0]] for k in range(len(est))]
            estimates.append(dict(run=s["run"], boxes=[[round(float(v), 4) for v in b] for b in est],
                                  members=members))
        r = scene_metrics(est, list(s["truth"]), a.cutoff, a.ospa_p)
        r["correct"] = int(r["dn"] == 0 and r["n_matched"] == r["n_true"])
        r.update(run=s["run"], layout=s["layout"], round=s["round"], n_robots=len(s["robots"]))
        rows.append(r)
    return rows


def train_one(train_enc, val_scenes, val_enc, a, seed, log):
    """One model for one seed: Adam on the training scenes, the correct-scene rate on the validation scenes
    after every epoch, the best epoch kept, early stop after --patience epochs without improvement. Appends
    one row per epoch to log."""
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    model = build_model(a.graph, a.hidden, a.hops, a.features, a.skip)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=a.lr, weight_decay=a.weight_decay)
    w_same, w_false = class_weights(train_enc)
    best, best_state, best_epoch, waited = -1.0, None, 0, 0
    for epoch in range(1, a.epochs + 1):
        t0 = time.time()
        model.train()
        order = rng.permutation(len(train_enc))
        total = 0.0
        for start in range(0, len(order), a.batch):
            b = collate([train_enc[i] for i in order[start:start + a.batch]])
            same, false = model(b)
            loss = loss_fn(same, false, b, w_same, w_false)
            opt.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()
            total += float(loss.item())
        val = evaluate_scenes(model, val_scenes, val_enc, a)
        correct = 100 * float(np.mean([r["correct"] for r in val]))
        exact = 100 * float(np.mean([r["dn"] == 0 for r in val]))
        log.append(dict(seed=seed, epoch=epoch, loss=round(total / max(1, math.ceil(len(order) / a.batch)), 5),
                        val_exact_pct=round(exact, 2), val_correct_pct=round(correct, 2),
                        seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1)))
        print(f"    seed {seed} epoch {epoch:3d}: loss {log[-1]['loss']:.4f}  validation exact {exact:5.1f}%  "
              f"correct {correct:5.1f}%  ({log[-1]['seconds']:.0f} s)", flush=True)
        if correct > best:
            best, best_state, best_epoch, waited = correct, copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict()), epoch, 0
        else:
            waited += 1
            if waited >= a.patience:
                break
    model.load_state_dict(best_state)
    print(f"    seed {seed}: kept epoch {best_epoch} (validation correct {best:.1f}%)", flush=True)
    return model


# ====================================================================
# Test sets and baselines
# ====================================================================

def expected_runs(directory):
    """Run ids of a simulated set (runs.csv of sim.generate random), None for real runs."""
    path = os.path.join(directory, "runs.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path) as f:
        return [r["run"] for r in csv.DictReader(f)]


def empty_rows(runs, seen, truth, a):
    """Scenes in which no robot reported anything: an empty estimate (round 0, one round per sim run)."""
    rows = []
    for run in runs or []:
        if run in seen or run not in truth:
            continue
        r = scene_metrics([], [np.array([b["x"], b["y"]]) for b in truth[run]], a.cutoff, a.ospa_p)
        r["correct"] = int(r["dn"] == 0 and r["n_matched"] == r["n_true"])
        r.update(run=run, layout=run, round=0, n_robots=0)
        rows.append(r)
    return rows


def read_baseline(path):
    """{method: {(run, round): row}} of the all-robot rows of pipeline/evaluate_runs.py scenes.csv."""
    out = defaultdict(dict)
    with open(path) as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            if int(r["k"]) != int(r["n_robots"]):
                continue
            row = dict(n_true=int(r["n_true"]), n_est=int(r["n_est"]), dn=int(r["dn"]), n_matched=int(r["n_matched"]),
                       rmse=float(r["rmse"]) if r["rmse"] not in ("", "nan") else math.nan, ospa=float(r["ospa"]))
            row["correct"] = int(row["dn"] == 0 and row["n_matched"] == row["n_true"])
            out[r["method"]][(r["run"], int(r["round"]))] = row
            out[r["method"]].setdefault(("layout", r["layout"], int(r["round"])), row)
    return out


def baseline_row(table, row):
    return table.get((row["run"], row["round"])) or table.get(("layout", row["layout"], row["round"]))


def mcnemar(b, c):
    """Exact two-sided McNemar p-value (binomial test on the discordant pairs)."""
    n = b + c
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    k = min(b, c)
    logs = [math.lgamma(n + 1) - math.lgamma(i + 1) - math.lgamma(n - i + 1) - n * math.log(2) for i in range(k + 1)]
    return min(1.0, 2 * sum(math.exp(x) for x in logs))


def stats(rows, c=0.5):
    dn = np.array([r["dn"] for r in rows])
    rmse = np.array([r["rmse"] for r in rows], float)
    rmse = rmse[np.isfinite(rmse)]
    return dict(scenes=len(rows), **detection_metrics(rows, c), exact_pct=100 * float(np.mean(dn == 0)),
                correct_pct=100 * float(np.mean([r["correct"] for r in rows])),
                too_few_pct=100 * float(np.mean(dn < 0)), too_many_pct=100 * float(np.mean(dn > 0)),
                rmse_median_cm=100 * float(np.median(rmse)) if len(rmse) else math.nan,
                ospa_mean=float(np.mean([r["ospa"] for r in rows])))


def write_csv(path, rows):
    if not rows:
        return
    keys = list(rows[0])
    for r in rows[1:]:
        keys += [k for k in r if k not in keys]
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=keys)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

            g[k] = round(float(np.nanmean(vals)), 3)
            g[k + "_sd"] = round(float(np.nanstd(vals)), 3)
        summary.append(g)

                f"RMSE* {g['rmse_all_cm']:4.1f}±{g['rmse_all_cm_sd']:.1f} cm, false {g['false_per_scene']:.2f}")

                missing = sum(1 for _, b in paired if b is None)
                rows = [b for _, b in paired if b is not None]
                # scenes without any detection are absent from scenes.csv: empty estimate for this method too
                rows += [r for r, b in paired if b is None and r.get("n_robots", 1) == 0]
                st = stats(rows, a.cutoff)
                summary.append(dict(test=name, method=method, **{k: round(v, 3) for k, v in st.items()}))
                for seed, rows_g in enumerate(per_seed):
                    # paired sign tests, scene by scene: boxes found, false estimates, scene correct
                    cnt = {k: [0, 0] for k in ("found", "false", "correct")}
                    for r in rows_g:
                        rb = baseline_row(base[method], r)
                        if rb is None:
                            if r.get("n_robots", 1) != 0:
                                continue
                            rb = dict(r, n_est=0, n_matched=0, correct=r["correct"])
                        diffs = dict(found=int(r["n_matched"]) - int(rb["n_matched"]),
                                     false=(int(rb["n_est"]) - int(rb["n_matched"])) - (int(r["n_est"]) - int(r["n_matched"])),
                                     correct=int(r["correct"]) - int(rb["correct"]))
                        for k, d in diffs.items():          # positive = the GNN is better on this scene
                            cnt[k][0] += int(d > 0)
                            cnt[k][1] += int(d < 0)
                    for k, (gb, bb) in cnt.items():
                        mc.append(dict(test=name, baseline=method, seed=seed, metric=k, gnn_better=gb,
                                       baseline_better=bb, p_value=mcnemar(gb, bb)))
                if missing - sum(1 for r, bb in paired if bb is None and r.get("n_robots", 1) == 0):
                    print(f"    warning: {method}: some {name} scenes have no row in {baseline_path}")
                if method == "mht":
                    line += (f" | MHT P_D {st['pd_pct']:5.1f}%, RMSE* {st['rmse_all_cm']:4.1f} cm, "
                             f"false {st['false_per_scene']:.2f}")
        print(line, flush=True)

    sfx = f"_{a.results_name}" if a.results_name else ""
    write_csv(os.path.join(out, f"test_scenes{sfx}.csv"), tests_rows)
    write_csv(os.path.join(out, f"summary{sfx}.csv"), summary)
    write_csv(os.path.join(out, f"mcnemar{sfx}.csv"), mc)
    print(f"\nwritten in {out}: summary{sfx}.csv, mcnemar{sfx}.csv, test_scenes{sfx}.csv"
          + ("" if a.eval_only else ", models"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./gnn/model.py <==
"""GNN for multi-robot box association (feature vectors only, no images).

Two graph designs, same inputs and same read-out:

  RobotGNN       one NODE per robot, carrying the robot pose and the set of its detections; EDGES join
                 robots that can exchange messages and carry their relative pose.
  DetectionGNN   one NODE per detection, carrying the feature vector and the pose of its robot; EDGES join
                 detections that may be the same box (closer than the pair gate) and whose robots can
                 exchange messages, or that come from the same robot (two faces of one box); they carry
                 the offset between the two detections.

Which robots exchange messages (edges=):
  ring     neighbours on the ring around the robots' centre (every pair with 3 robots or fewer)
  opposite the robots facing each robot across the team: the one in front and its two neighbours
           (the diagonals); with an odd number of robots, the two that face it
  range    robots closer than comm_range metres (limited communication)
  full     every pair of robots (upper bound: one central model sees everything)
`hops` rounds of message passing; with a local graph a robot hears robots up to `hops` links away.

Association (association=):
  central  every pair of detections closer than the pair gate is scored, whichever robots made them: one
           central read-out sees all detections (the communication graph only carries context)
  local    distributed: two detections are scored only if their robots are at most `hops` links apart in
           the communication graph (or are the same robot), so a robot can only associate what reaches it
           through the network; detections of robots that cannot reach each other are never merged

Inputs (features=):
  full       detection position, line of sight, distance, bearing, viewing angle of the marker, robot pose
  positions  the same without the viewing angle: only what follows from the positions and the robot poses

Skip connections (skip=):
  residual  each hop adds its update to the node, so a node keeps what its robot saw (default)
  none      each hop replaces the node
  jk        jumping knowledge: residual hops, and the read-out sees the node after every hop

Read-out:
  same-box head   for every pair of detections closer than the pair gate (also two detections of the same
                  robot): probability that they are the same box
  false head      for every detection: probability that it is a false detection
Decoding (decode()): false detections are dropped, the rest are grouped by average-linkage clustering on
the same-box probabilities (pairs beyond the gate count as 0); the number of groups is the box count and
the mean position of each group is the box position.

Everything runs on the host PC. Only nn.Linear, ReLU, indexing, cat, index_add and BCE-with-logits are used.
"""

import math

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RING_SCALE_M = 1.3          # ring radius, used to scale positions
PAIR_SCALE_M = 0.1          # pair offsets are given in units of 10 cm
PAIR_CLIP_M = 1.0           # pair offsets beyond 1 m carry no extra information

DET_FEATURES = {"full": 10, "positions": 8}
ROBOT_FEATURES = 5
EDGE_FEATURES = 5
PAIR_FEATURES = 6


# ====================================================================
# Features
# ====================================================================

def ring_edges(robot_xy, center):
    """Directed edges between ring neighbours (every pair when there are 3 robots or fewer)."""
    n = len(robot_xy)
    if n <= 1:
        return []
    if n <= 3:
        return [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j]
    ang = np.arctan2(robot_xy[:, 1] - center[1], robot_xy[:, 0] - center[0])
    order = list(np.argsort(ang))
    edges = set()
    for k, i in enumerate(order):
        for j in (order[(k - 1) % n], order[(k + 1) % n]):
            edges.add((int(i), int(j)))
            edges.add((int(j), int(i)))
    return sorted(edges)


def opposite_edges(robot_xy, center):
    """Directed edges from every robot to the robots facing it across the team: the robots are ordered by
    their angle around the centre, and robot i is linked to the robots whose position in that order is
    within one step of the opposite point (i + n/2): with an even n the robot in front and the two next
    to it (the diagonals), with an odd n the two robots that face it. Every pair with 3 robots or fewer."""
    n = len(robot_xy)
    if n <= 1:
        return []
    if n <= 3:
        return [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j]
    ang = np.arctan2(robot_xy[:, 1] - center[1], robot_xy[:, 0] - center[0])
    order = list(np.argsort(ang))
    offsets = [o for o in range(1, n) if abs(o - n / 2) <= 1]
    edges = set()
    for k, i in enumerate(order):
        for o in offsets:
            j = order[(k + o) % n]
            edges.add((int(i), int(j)))
            edges.add((int(j), int(i)))
    return sorted(edges)


def robot_edges(robot_xy, mode="ring", comm_range=None):
    """Directed robot-robot edges for the chosen communication graph."""
    n = len(robot_xy)
    if mode == "ring":
        return ring_edges(robot_xy, np.zeros(2))
    if mode == "opposite":
        return opposite_edges(robot_xy, np.zeros(2))
    if mode == "full":
        return [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j]
    if mode == "range":
        if comm_range is None:
            raise ValueError("edges='range' needs comm_range")
        d = np.linalg.norm(robot_xy[:, None, :] - robot_xy[None, :, :], axis=2)
        return [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j and d[i, j] <= comm_range]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown edge mode {mode}")


def pair_features(pos, u, r_of, i, j):
    """Offset of detection j seen from detection i (arrays of indices): along and across i's line of sight,
    distance, same robot, angle between the two lines of sight, |across|."""
    d = pos[j] - pos[i]
    dist = np.minimum(np.hypot(d[:, 0], d[:, 1]), PAIR_CLIP_M)
    ui = u[i]
    along = np.clip((d * ui).sum(axis=1), -PAIR_CLIP_M, PAIR_CLIP_M)
    across = np.clip(ui[:, 0] * d[:, 1] - ui[:, 1] * d[:, 0], -PAIR_CLIP_M, PAIR_CLIP_M)
    cos_rays = (ui * u[j]).sum(axis=1)
    return np.column_stack([along / PAIR_SCALE_M, across / PAIR_SCALE_M, dist / PAIR_SCALE_M,
                            (r_of[i] == r_of[j]).astype(float), cos_rays, np.abs(across) / PAIR_SCALE_M])


def reachable(n, edge_arr, hops):
    """n x n bool: robot j can be reached from robot i in at most `hops` links (every robot reaches itself)."""
    adj = np.eye(n, dtype=bool)
    if len(edge_arr):
        adj[edge_arr[:, 0], edge_arr[:, 1]] = True
        adj[edge_arr[:, 1], edge_arr[:, 0]] = True
    reach = np.eye(n, dtype=bool)
    for _ in range(hops):
        reach = (reach.astype(int) @ adj.astype(int)) > 0
    return reach


def encode_scene(scene, rotation=0.0, features="full", edges="ring", comm_range=None, gate=None,
                 association="central", hops=2):
    """numpy features of one scene, in a frame centred on the robots and rotated by `rotation`.
    gate: only pairs of detections closer than this [m] are scored (None = every pair).
    association='local': only pairs whose robots are at most `hops` links apart are scored."""
    poses = scene["poses"]
    center = poses[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    c, s = math.cos(rotation), math.sin(rotation)
    R = np.array([[c, -s], [s, c]])

    robot_xy = (poses[:, :2] - center) @ R.T
    robot_yaw = poses[:, 2] + rotation
    pos = (np.asarray(scene["pos"], float).reshape(-1, 2) - center) @ R.T
    r_of = np.asarray(scene["det_robot"], int)
    ray = robot_yaw[r_of] - scene["bearing"]                  # world direction of each detection
    u = np.stack([np.cos(ray), np.sin(ray)], axis=1).reshape(-1, 2)   # unit vector along the line of sight
    n_det = np.bincount(r_of, minlength=len(poses))

    robot = np.column_stack([robot_xy / RING_SCALE_M, np.cos(robot_yaw), np.sin(robot_yaw), n_det / 4.0])
    cols = [pos / RING_SCALE_M, u, scene["distance"], scene["bearing"]]
    if features == "full":
        cols += [np.cos(scene["view"]), np.sin(scene["view"])]
    elif features != "positions":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown feature set {features}")
    cols.append(robot_xy[r_of] / RING_SCALE_M)
    det = np.column_stack(cols).reshape(len(pos), DET_FEATURES[features])

    edge_list = robot_edges(robot_xy, edges, comm_range)
    edge_arr = np.array(edge_list, int).reshape(-1, 2)
    if len(edge_arr):
        i, j = edge_arr[:, 0], edge_arr[:, 1]                 # message i -> j, seen from robot j
        d = robot_xy[i] - robot_xy[j]
        cj, sj = np.cos(-robot_yaw[j]), np.sin(-robot_yaw[j])
        local = np.column_stack([cj * d[:, 0] - sj * d[:, 1], sj * d[:, 0] + cj * d[:, 1]])
        dyaw = robot_yaw[i] - robot_yaw[j]
        edge_feat = np.column_stack([local / RING_SCALE_M, np.cos(dyaw), np.sin(dyaw),
                                     np.hypot(d[:, 0], d[:, 1]) / RING_SCALE_M])
    else:
        edge_feat = np.zeros((0, EDGE_FEATURES))

    ii, jj = np.triu_indices(len(pos), k=1)
    if gate is not None and len(ii):
        near = np.hypot(*(pos[jj] - pos[ii]).T) <= gate
        ii, jj = ii[near], jj[near]
    if association == "local":
        reach = reachable(len(poses), edge_arr, hops)
        ok = reach[r_of[ii], r_of[jj]]
        ii, jj = ii[ok], jj[ok]
    elif association != "central":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown association {association}")
    pairs = np.column_stack([ii, jj]).astype(int).reshape(-1, 2)
    pair_ij = pair_features(pos, u, r_of, ii, jj).reshape(-1, PAIR_FEATURES)
    pair_ji = pair_features(pos, u, r_of, jj, ii).reshape(-1, PAIR_FEATURES)
    linked = np.zeros((len(poses), len(poses)), bool)
    np.fill_diagonal(linked, True)
    if len(edge_arr):
        linked[edge_arr[:, 0], edge_arr[:, 1]] = True
    pair_link = linked[r_of[ii], r_of[jj]] | linked[r_of[jj], r_of[ii]]

    label = scene.get("label")
    if label is not None:
        label = np.asarray(label, int)
        same = ((label[ii] >= 0) & (label[ii] == label[jj])).astype(float)
        false = (label < 0).astype(float)
    else:
        same, false = np.zeros(len(ii)), np.zeros(len(pos))
    return dict(robot=robot, det=det, det_robot=r_of, edges=edge_arr, edge_feat=edge_feat,
                pairs=pairs, pair_ij=pair_ij, pair_ji=pair_ji, pair_link=pair_link, same=same, false=false)


def collate(encoded):
    """Several encoded scenes -> one batch of tensors (block-diagonal graph)."""
    r_off = np.cumsum([0] + [len(e["robot"]) for e in encoded])
    d_off = np.cumsum([0] + [len(e["det"]) for e in encoded])

    def cat(key, width=None, offset=None):
        parts = [e[key] + (offset[k] if offset is not None else 0) for k, e in enumerate(encoded)]
        if width is not None:
            parts = [np.asarray(p, float).reshape(-1, width) for p in parts]
        return np.concatenate(parts) if parts else np.zeros((0,) if width is None else (0, width))

    det_width = encoded[0]["det"].shape[1]
    edges = cat("edges", offset=r_off).reshape(-1, 2) if encoded else np.zeros((0, 2), int)
    pairs = cat("pairs", offset=d_off).reshape(-1, 2) if encoded else np.zeros((0, 2), int)

    def f32(x):
        return torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(x, np.float32))

    def i64(x):
        return torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(x, np.int64))

    return dict(robot=f32(cat("robot", ROBOT_FEATURES)), det=f32(cat("det", det_width)),
                det_robot=i64(cat("det_robot", offset=r_off)), n_robots=int(r_off[-1]), n_det=int(d_off[-1]),
                edge_src=i64(edges[:, 0]), edge_dst=i64(edges[:, 1]), edge_feat=f32(cat("edge_feat", EDGE_FEATURES)),
                pair_a=i64(pairs[:, 0]), pair_b=i64(pairs[:, 1]),
                pair_ij=f32(cat("pair_ij", PAIR_FEATURES)), pair_ji=f32(cat("pair_ji", PAIR_FEATURES)),
                pair_link=torch.as_tensor(np.concatenate([e["pair_link"] for e in encoded]).astype(bool)),
                same=f32(np.concatenate([e["same"] for e in encoded])),
                false=f32(np.concatenate([e["false"] for e in encoded])))


# ====================================================================
# Models
# ====================================================================

def mlp(*sizes):
    layers = []
    for a, b in zip(sizes[:-1], sizes[1:]):
        layers += [nn.Linear(a, b), nn.ReLU()]
    return nn.Sequential(*layers[:-1])                       # no activation after the last layer


def segment_mean(values, index, n):
    """Mean of the rows of `values` grouped by `index` (empty groups give 0)."""
    total = torch.zeros(n, values.shape[1]).index_add(0, index, values)
    count = torch.zeros(n, 1).index_add(0, index, torch.ones(values.shape[0], 1))
    return total / count.clamp(min=1.0)


class PairReadout(nn.Module):
    """Same-box logit per scored pair (symmetric) and false-detection logit per detection."""

    def __init__(self, h):
        super().__init__()
        self.pair_head = mlp(2 * h + PAIR_FEATURES, h, h // 2, 1)
        self.false_head = mlp(h, h // 2, 1)

    def forward(self, g, b):
        ga, gb = g[b["pair_a"]], g[b["pair_b"]]
        same = 0.5 * (self.pair_head(torch.cat([ga, gb, b["pair_ij"]], dim=1)) +
                      self.pair_head(torch.cat([gb, ga, b["pair_ji"]], dim=1)))
        return same.view(-1), self.false_head(g).view(-1)


class RobotGNN(nn.Module):
    """skip: how the hops are chained (see SKIP_MODES)."""

    def __init__(self, hidden=64, hops=2, det_features=DET_FEATURES["full"], skip="residual"):
        super().__init__()
        h = hidden
        self.skip = skip
        self.det_enc = nn.Sequential(mlp(det_features, h, h), nn.ReLU())
        self.robot_enc = nn.Sequential(mlp(ROBOT_FEATURES + h, h, h), nn.ReLU())
        self.message = nn.ModuleList([nn.Sequential(mlp(h + EDGE_FEATURES, h, h), nn.ReLU())
                                      for _ in range(hops)])
        self.update = nn.ModuleList([mlp(2 * h, h, h) for _ in range(hops)])
        n_node = (hops + 1) if skip == "jk" else 1
        self.det_ctx = nn.Sequential(mlp(h + n_node * h, h, h), nn.ReLU())
        self.readout = PairReadout(h)

    def forward(self, b):
        h_det = self.det_enc(b["det"])                                       # detections
        pooled = segment_mean(h_det, b["det_robot"], b["n_robots"])          # set of detections per robot
        node = self.robot_enc(torch.cat([b["robot"], pooled], dim=1))        # robot nodes
        states = [node]
        for message, update in zip(self.message, self.update):               # message passing between robots
            m = message(torch.cat([node[b["edge_src"]], b["edge_feat"]], dim=1))
            agg = segment_mean(m, b["edge_dst"], b["n_robots"])
            new = update(torch.cat([node, agg], dim=1))
            node = new if self.skip == "none" else node + new
            states.append(node)
        robot_view = torch.cat(states, dim=1) if self.skip == "jk" else node
        g = self.det_ctx(torch.cat([h_det, robot_view[b["det_robot"]]], dim=1))   # detection in its context
        return self.readout(g, b)


class DetectionGNN(nn.Module):
    """The adopted design: one node per detection. Every node starts from the features of its detection and of
    its robot; in each hop it averages the messages of the detections that could be the same box (the pairs
    inside the gate, see encode_scene) and updates its state; the read-out scores every pair (same box?) and
    every detection (false?). skip: how the hops are chained (see SKIP_MODES)."""

    def __init__(self, hidden=64, hops=2, det_features=DET_FEATURES["full"], skip="residual"):
        super().__init__()
        h = hidden
        self.skip = skip
        self.enc = nn.Sequential(mlp(det_features + ROBOT_FEATURES, h, h), nn.ReLU())
        self.message = nn.ModuleList([nn.Sequential(mlp(h + PAIR_FEATURES, h, h), nn.ReLU())
                                      for _ in range(hops)])
        self.update = nn.ModuleList([mlp(2 * h, h, h) for _ in range(hops)])
        self.jk = nn.Sequential(mlp((hops + 1) * h, h, h), nn.ReLU()) if skip == "jk" else None
        self.readout = PairReadout(h)

    def forward(self, b):
        g = self.enc(torch.cat([b["det"], b["robot"][b["det_robot"]]], dim=1))
        link = b["pair_link"]
        a, c = b["pair_a"][link], b["pair_b"][link]
        src = torch.cat([a, c])
        dst = torch.cat([c, a])
        feat = torch.cat([b["pair_ji"][link], b["pair_ij"][link]])      # offset of src seen from dst
        states = [g]
        for message, update in zip(self.message, self.update):
            m = message(torch.cat([g[src], feat], dim=1))
            agg = segment_mean(m, dst, b["n_det"])
            new = update(torch.cat([g, agg], dim=1))
            g = new if self.skip == "none" else g + new
            states.append(g)
        if self.jk is not None:
            g = self.jk(torch.cat(states, dim=1))
        return self.readout(g, b)


SKIP_MODES = {
    "residual": "each hop adds its update to the node (node = node + update); the read-out uses the "
                "detection's own encoding and the node after the last hop",
    "none": "each hop replaces the node (node = update); no shortcut across the hops",
    "jk": "residual hops, and the read-out uses the node after EVERY hop (0, 1, ... hops): "
          "jumping knowledge, the first layer connected to the last",
}


def build_model(graph="robot", hidden=64, hops=2, features="full", skip="residual"):
    cls = {"robot": RobotGNN, "detection": DetectionGNN}[graph]
    return cls(hidden=hidden, hops=hops, det_features=DET_FEATURES[features], skip=skip)


def loss_fn(same_logit, false_logit, b, pos_weight_same, pos_weight_false):
    loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
        false_logit, b["false"], pos_weight=torch.tensor(float(pos_weight_false), dtype=torch.float32))
    if len(same_logit):
        loss = loss + F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
            same_logit, b["same"], pos_weight=torch.tensor(float(pos_weight_same), dtype=torch.float32))
    return loss


# ====================================================================
# Decoding
# ====================================================================

def decode(pos, pairs, p_same, p_false, threshold=0.5):
    """Boxes of one scene: drop false detections, then average-linkage clustering on p_same (pairs not
    scored count as 0). Returns (list of box positions, cluster index per detection, -1 for dropped ones)."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, float).reshape(-1, 2)
    n = len(pos)
    P = np.eye(n)
    for (i, j), p in zip(pairs, p_same):
        P[i, j] = P[j, i] = p
    keep = [i for i in range(n) if p_false[i] < threshold]
    clusters = [[i] for i in keep]
    if clusters:
        S = P[np.ix_(keep, keep)].copy()          # current sum of probabilities between clusters
        sizes = np.ones(len(keep))
        alive = np.ones(len(keep), bool)
        members = [[i] for i in keep]
        np.fill_diagonal(S, -np.inf)
        while alive.sum() > 1:
            link = S / np.outer(sizes, sizes)
            link[~alive, :] = -np.inf
            link[:, ~alive] = -np.inf
            a, c = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(link), link.shape)
            if link[a, c] <= threshold:
                break
            a, c = min(a, c), max(a, c)
            S[a, :] += S[c, :]
            S[:, a] += S[:, c]
            S[a, a] = -np.inf
            sizes[a] += sizes[c]
            alive[c] = False
            members[a] += members[c]
        clusters = [members[k] for k in range(len(keep)) if alive[k]]
    assign = np.full(n, -1)
    for k, cl in enumerate(clusters):
        assign[cl] = k
    return [pos[cl].mean(axis=0) for cl in clusters], assign

==> ./gnn/dataset.py <==
"""Scenes for the GNN, built from the same round-mode runs used by pipeline/evaluate_runs.py.

A SCENE is one round of one run: the feature vectors of all the robots standing at their positions of
that round (same definition as pipeline/evaluate_runs.py). For every scene this module returns

  robots     robot ids, in a fixed order
  poses      camera pose (x, y, yaw) of every robot                                  (R, 3)
  det_robot  index of the robot that produced each detection                          (N,)
  distance   measured distance, corrected with the range fit                          (N,)
  bearing    measured bearing, corrected with the bearing fit                         (N,)
  view       viewing angle of the marker                                              (N,)
  pos        world position of the detection, from pose, distance and bearing         (N, 2)
  label      index of the true box the detection belongs to, -1 for a false detection (N,)
  truth      true box positions (OptiTrack)                                           (M, 2)

The distance / bearing correction and the camera offset come from the calibration file written by
pipeline/calibrate.py (--sensor-calib), exactly as pipeline/evaluate_runs.py applies them, so the GNN and the classical
methods see the same detections at the same positions.

A detection is labelled with the nearest true box when it lies within LABEL_RADIUS_M of it, otherwise it
is a false detection (-1). Simulated runs carry the true label of every detection (sim_box), which is used
instead, so two boxes closer than the measurement error are still told apart. The labels are used for
training only; the evaluation compares the estimated
boxes with the true boxes as pipeline/evaluate_runs.py does.

    python -m gnn.dataset --survey-dir data/survey_rounds/ --ground-truth config/ground_truth_positions.json \\
        --sensor-calib config/sensor_calib.json
prints a summary of the scenes (detections, false detections, boxes seen twice by one robot).
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import math
import os
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np

LABEL_RADIUS_M = 0.4


def load_calibration(path):
    """Range fit, bearing fit and camera offset from pipeline/calibrate.py --out (identity without a file)."""
    if not path:
        return dict(range_fit=None, bearing_fit=None, camera_offset=0.0)
    with open(path) as f:
        calib = json.load(f)
    return dict(range_fit=calib.get("range_fit"), bearing_fit=calib.get("bearing_fit"),
                camera_offset=float(calib.get("camera_offset") or 0.0))


def load_truth(path):
    """{run or layout id: (M, 2) array of true box centres}."""
    with open(path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return {k: np.array([[b["x"], b["y"]] for b in v], float) for k, v in data.items()}


def read_records(survey_dir):
    """All feature vectors of the round-mode runs (same files as build_scans.load_points)."""
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(survey_dir, "**", "*.jsonl"), recursive=True))
    paths = [q for q in paths
             if not {"raw", "sync"} & set(os.path.normpath(os.path.relpath(q, survey_dir)).split(os.sep)[:-1])]
    for path in paths:
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                try:
                    r = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue
                if "layout_id" not in r or r.get("round") is None or r.get("yaw_offset_deg", 0) != 0:
                    continue
                if not r.get("class_name") or r.get("distance") is None or r.get("bearing_rad") is None:
                    continue
                if r.get("robot_pose") is None:
                    continue
                yield r


def build_scenes(survey_dir, truth_path, calib_path=None):
    calib = load_calibration(calib_path)
    truth = load_truth(truth_path)
    A, B = calib["range_fit"] or (1.0, 0.0)
    K, B0 = calib["bearing_fit"] or (1.0, 0.0)
    off = calib["camera_offset"]

    grouped = defaultdict(list)
    for r in read_records(survey_dir):
        run = r.get("run_id") or r["layout_id"]
        grouped[(run, r["layout_id"], int(r["round"]))].append(r)

    scenes = []
    for (run, layout, rnd), recs in sorted(grouped.items()):
        true_xy = truth.get(run, truth.get(layout))
        if true_xy is None:
            continue
        robots = sorted({r["robot_id"] for r in recs})
        poses = {}
        det_robot, distance, bearing, view, pos, sim_box = [], [], [], [], [], []
        for r in sorted(recs, key=lambda q: (q["robot_id"], q.get("t", 0.0))):
            x, y, yaw = r["robot_pose"]
            cam = (x + off * math.cos(yaw), y + off * math.sin(yaw), yaw)
            poses.setdefault(r["robot_id"], cam)
            d = (float(r["distance"]) - B) / A
            b = (float(r["bearing_rad"]) - B0) / K
            det_robot.append(robots.index(r["robot_id"]))
            distance.append(d)
            bearing.append(b)
            view.append(float(r.get("viewing_angle_rad") or 0.0))
            sim_box.append(r.get("sim_box"))
            # bearing positive to the right: world direction = yaw - bearing
            pos.append((cam[0] + d * math.cos(cam[2] - b), cam[1] + d * math.sin(cam[2] - b)))
        pos = np.array(pos, float)
        gaps = np.linalg.norm(pos[:, None, :] - true_xy[None, :, :], axis=2)
        nearest = gaps.argmin(axis=1)
        label = np.where(gaps[np.arange(len(pos)), nearest] <= LABEL_RADIUS_M, nearest, -1)
        if all(b is not None for b in sim_box):          # simulated run: true labels
            label = np.array(sim_box, int)
        scenes.append(dict(
            run=run, layout=layout, round=rnd, robots=robots,
            poses=np.array([poses[q] for q in robots], float),
            det_robot=np.array(det_robot, int), distance=np.array(distance), bearing=np.array(bearing),
            view=np.array(view), pos=pos, label=label.astype(int), truth=true_xy))
    return scenes


def subset_robots(scene, keep):
    """The same scene seen by the robots `keep` only (indices into scene['robots'])."""
    keep = sorted(keep)
    mask = np.isin(scene["det_robot"], keep)
    remap = {old: new for new, old in enumerate(keep)}
    out = dict(scene)
    out["robots"] = [scene["robots"][i] for i in keep]
    out["poses"] = scene["poses"][keep]
    out["det_robot"] = np.array([remap[i] for i in scene["det_robot"][mask]], int)
    for key in ("distance", "bearing", "view", "label"):
        out[key] = scene[key][mask]
    out["pos"] = scene["pos"][mask]
    return out


def describe(scenes):
    n_det = sum(len(s["pos"]) for s in scenes)
    n_false = sum(int((s["label"] < 0).sum()) for s in scenes)
    twice = 0
    for s in scenes:
        seen = defaultdict(int)
        for r, lab in zip(s["det_robot"], s["label"]):
            if lab >= 0:
                seen[(r, lab)] += 1
        twice += sum(1 for v in seen.values() if v > 1)
    print(f"{len(scenes)} scenes, {n_det} detections, {n_false} false detections "
          f"(farther than {LABEL_RADIUS_M} m from every box), {twice} boxes reported twice by one robot")
    per_layout = defaultdict(int)
    for s in scenes:
        per_layout[s["layout"]] += 1
    def order(name):
        digits = "".join(ch for ch in name if ch.isdigit())
        return (int(digits) if digits else 0, name)

    print("scenes per layout: " + ", ".join(f"{k} {per_layout[k]}" for k in sorted(per_layout, key=order)))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--survey-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--ground-truth", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--sensor-calib", default=None)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    describe(build_scenes(a.survey_dir, a.ground_truth, a.sensor_calib))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./robomaster_sdk/camera.py <==
"""RoboMaster camera, with a background reader.

Why a separate thread
--------------------------
`read_cv2_image` blocks until it has a frame. Calling it inside the
recording loop would tie the sample rate to the video rate: a late frame
becomes a late sample, and the 10 Hz rate, which works well now, would
degrade.

Here instead a thread reads continuously and keeps the LATEST frame in a
cache together with its acquisition time. The loop takes whatever is
there, never waiting, and also records how old it is. That age ends up in
the dataset and is a quality measure: if an episode has images half a
second old, the model would see a scene that no longer matches the
recorded action.

Channel measurements
-----------------
With the stream on, angle readings go from 16.4 to 15.9 per second, i.e.
a 3% drop, with no failures, and the same at 360, 540 and 720p. Video and
the synchronous channel do not interfere: images and angles can be
recorded in the same frame.
"""

import logging
import threading
import time

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

try:
    from robomaster import camera as camera_mod
except ImportError:      # pragma: no cover - useful for tests without the SDK
    camera_mod = None

RESOLUTIONS = {}
if camera_mod is not None:
    RESOLUTIONS = {
        "360": getattr(camera_mod, "STREAM_360P", None),
        "540": getattr(camera_mod, "STREAM_540P", None),
        "720": getattr(camera_mod, "STREAM_720P", None),
    }

# Default resolution. 540p is the compromise: the channel also handles
# 720, but VLAs resize to a 224-512 side anyway, and at 540 the dataset
# takes about a third of the space.
DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = "540"

# Beyond this age a frame no longer describes the scene at the time of
# the action.
MAX_FRAME_AGE = 0.5


class CameraError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Camera:
    """Video stream with a cache of the latest frame."""

    def __init__(self, ep_camera):
        self._cam = ep_camera
        self._frame = None
        self._frame_t = None
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self._thread = None
        self._streaming = False
        self._errors = 0
        self._read_count = 0
        self.resolution = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def start(self, resolution=DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, wait=3.0):
        """Start the stream and the background reader."""
        if self._streaming:
            return self

        res = RESOLUTIONS.get(resolution)
        try:
            if res is not None:
                self._cam.start_video_stream(display=False, resolution=res)
            else:
                self._cam.start_video_stream(display=False)
        except Exception as e:
            raise CameraError(f"starting the stream failed: {e}")

        self._streaming = True
        self.resolution = resolution
        self._stop.clear()
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()

        deadline = time.time() + wait
        while self._frame is None and time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.05)
        if self._frame is None:
            self.stop()
            raise CameraError(
                f"no frame within {wait:.0f}s of starting"
            )
        h, w = self._frame.shape[:2]
        log.info("camera started: %dx%d (%sp)", w, h, resolution)
        return self

    def _loop(self):
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                img = self._cam.read_cv2_image(strategy="newest", timeout=1)
            except Exception as e:
                self._errors += 1
                if self._errors in (5, 50):
                    log.warning("video read failed %d times",
                                self._errors)
                time.sleep(0.05)
                continue
            if img is None:
                continue
            with self._lock:
                self._frame = img
                self._frame_t = time.time()
                self._read_count += 1

    def stop(self):
        self._stop.set()
        if self._thread:
            self._thread.join(timeout=2.0)
            self._thread = None
        if self._streaming:
            try:
                self._cam.stop_video_stream()
            except Exception as e:
                log.warning("stopping the stream failed: %s", e)
            self._streaming = False

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def read(self):
        """Latest frame and its age in seconds.

        Never blocks. Returns (None, None) if there is nothing yet.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if self._frame is None:
                return None, None
            return self._frame, time.time() - self._frame_t

    @property
    def is_streaming(self):
        return self._streaming

    @property
    def frame_count(self):
        return self._read_count

    @property
    def error_count(self):
        return self._errors

    def stats(self):
        with self._lock:
            age = (time.time() - self._frame_t) if self._frame_t else None
            shape = self._frame.shape[:2] if self._frame is not None else None
        return {
            "streaming": self._streaming,
            "resolution": self.resolution,
            "frames": self._read_count,
            "errors": self._errors,
            "age": age,
            "shape": shape,
        }

    def __enter__(self):
        return self.start()

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.stop()
        return False

==> ./robomaster_sdk/robot.py <==
"""SDK entry point: the Robot class.

Minimal usage:

    from robomaster_sdk import Robot

    with Robot("P0") as r:
        r.chassis.drive_speed(x=0.1, y=0, z=0)
"""

import logging

import robomaster
from robomaster import robot as dji_robot

from . import config

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Robot:
    """A single RoboMaster EP.

    Hides serial number, connection type and subsystem initialization.
    Exposes: .chassis, .camera, .servo.
    """

    def __init__(self, name, sn=None, conn_type=None, ip=None):
        if sn is None:
            if name not in config.ROBOTS:
                raise KeyError(
                    f"Robot '{name}' not in the registry. "
                    f"Known names: {sorted(config.ROBOTS)}. "
                    "Pass sn= explicitly for an unregistered robot."
                )
            sn = config.ROBOTS[name]

        self.name = name
        self.sn = sn
        self.conn_type = conn_type or config.CONN_TYPE
        self.ip = ip
        self._ep = None
        self.chassis = None
        self.camera = None
        self.servo = None

        self._connected = False

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Lifecycle
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def connect(self):
        """Open the connection and set up the subsystems."""
        if self._connected:
            log.warning("%s: connect() on an already connected robot", self.name)
            return self

        log.info("Connecting to %s (sn=%s, %s)", self.name, self.sn,
                 self.conn_type)

        self._ep = dji_robot.Robot()

        # --- BEGIN IP TRICK (monkey patching) ---
        if self.ip:
            log.info("Bypassing UDP scan: forcing IP %s", self.ip)
            import robomaster.conn
            # Save the original function
            _original_scan = robomaster.conn.scan_robot_ip
            # Replace the DJI scan function with a fake one that immediately returns your IP
            robomaster.conn.scan_robot_ip = lambda *args, **kwargs: self.ip
            
            try:
                # Now initialize() will "find" the robot right away without timing out
                self._ep.initialize(conn_type=self.conn_type, sn=self.sn)
            finally:
                # Restore the original function to clean up
                robomaster.conn.scan_robot_ip = _original_scan
        else:
            self._ep.initialize(conn_type=self.conn_type, sn=self.sn)
        # --- END IP TRICK ---

        version = self._ep.get_version()
        actual_sn = self._ep.get_sn()
        log.info("%s: firmware %s, reported sn %s", self.name, version,
                 actual_sn)

        if actual_sn and actual_sn != self.sn:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"{self.name}: the robot answers with sn={actual_sn} but "
                f"{self.sn} was expected. Connected to the wrong robot."
            )

        self.chassis = self._ep.chassis
        self.camera = self._ep.camera
        self.servo = self._ep.servo

        self._connected = True

        return self

    def disconnect(self):
        """Close the connection (idempotent)."""
        if self._ep is not None:
            try:
                self._ep.close()
            except Exception:
                log.warning("%s: close() failed", self.name, exc_info=True)
        self._connected = False
        log.info("%s: disconnected", self.name)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self.connect()

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
        self.disconnect()
        return False

    @property
    def is_connected(self):
        return self._connected

    def __repr__(self):
        state = "connected" if self._connected else "not connected"
        return f"<Robot {self.name} sn={self.sn} {state}>"

==> ./bevnet/twin.py <==
"""Simulated twins of the real scenes: the scenes of data/bev_real/<set> rendered by imgsim/render.py with the
same robot poses, pitch and boxes (box orientations are not recorded: drawn at random). The twin set has the
format of bevnet/data.py, so a model can be tested on the real frames and on their twins with the same command:
if it finds the boxes in the twins but not in the real frames, what fails is the look of the images, not the
geometry. --figure puts real frames and twin frames side by side (fig_REAL-2.png).

    python -m bevnet.twin --real data/bev_real/real_k0 --out data/bev_real_twin/ --figure
    python -m bevnet.train --eval-only --out results/bev_obst/ --tests data/bev_real_twin/twin_k0 --results-name twin
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import pickle
from dataclasses import asdict

import cv2
import numpy as np

from bevnet.data import CALIB
from imgsim.render import Appearance, Camera, Renderer
from sim.scene import Capture, Scene


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--real", default="data/bev_real/real_k0")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/bev_real_twin/")
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=0.2)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--figure", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    with open(os.path.join(a.real, "shard_0000.pkl"), "rb") as f:
        real = pickle.load(f)
    app = Appearance()
    renderer = Renderer(CALIB["P0"], app, seed=a.seed, scale=a.scale)
    cam = Camera(CALIB["P0"], scale=a.scale)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(a.seed)
    twins = []
    for s in real:
        boxes = np.asarray(s["boxes"], float)
        scene = Scene(layout_id=s["run"].split("_")[0], run_id=s["run"], boxes=boxes,
                      thetas=rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, len(boxes)), obstacles=[],
                      captures=[Capture(round=0, robot=q, pose=tuple(map(float, p)))
                                for q, p in zip(s["robots"], s["poses"])])
        style = renderer.scene_style(rng)
        jpgs = []
        for k, p in enumerate(s["pitch"]):
            app.pitch_deg = [float(np.degrees(p))] * 2
            app.roll_deg = [0.0, 0.0]
            img, _, _ = renderer.render(scene, k, rng, style)
            ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 92])
            jpgs.append(buf.tobytes())
        t = {k: v for k, v in s.items() if k not in ("K", "D", "jpgs")}
        t.update(jpgs=jpgs, family="twin")
        twins.append(t)
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(a.real)).replace("real", "twin")
    out = os.path.join(a.out, name)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "shard_0000.pkl"), "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump(twins, f, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "meta.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(dict(set=name, scenario="twin", level="", scenes=len(twins), camera="P0", K=cam.K.tolist(),
                       D=cam.D.tolist(), size=[cam.W, cam.H], scale=a.scale, appearance=asdict(app)), f, indent=2)
    print(f"  {name}: {len(twins)} scenes -> {out}")
    if a.figure:
        rows = []
        for s, t in list(zip(real, twins))[::7][:6]:
            for src in (s, t):
                rows.append(np.hstack([cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(j, np.uint8), 1) for j in src["jpgs"]]))
        cv2.imwrite(os.path.join(a.out, "fig_REAL-2.png"), np.vstack(rows))
        print(f"  figure: {os.path.join(a.out, 'fig_REAL-2.png')}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

==> ./bevnet/real.py <==
"""The real scenes (data/survey_rounds: 8 layouts x 7 rounds = 56 scenes, 4 robots) in the format of
bevnet/data.py, so the image-based network trained in simulation can be tested on the real camera frames.

For every scene (layout, round) and reading k (each robot took 5 frames per stop): the frame of each robot,
resized to the network's image size (--scale of 1280 x 720, as in bevnet/data.py), its camera pose from
OptiTrack (raw/<robot>.jsonl, camera_pose), its own camera matrix and distortion (raw/meta_<layout>_<robot>.json,
scaled to the image size), the downward pitch measured on the real frames (--pitch), and the true boxes
(ground_truth.json). Poses and boxes are shifted so that the centre of the robots is the origin of the floor
grid. One set per reading: data/bev_real/real_k<k>/ (shard_*.pkl, meta.json); run ids <layout>_r<round>.
--calibrate fits, per robot, the camera pitch and a yaw offset from the ArUco detections stored with the
frames (without --marker-channel the detections are used only for this calibration, never as network input), leave one layout
out: the frames of a layout use the values fitted on the other layouts. A low camera (25 cm) makes the floor
geometry very sensitive to the pitch: at 1.5 m, 1 degree moves the middle of a box by about 60 cm along the ray.
--check draws the true box centres and the grid's sampling points into a few frames (fig_REAL-0.png), to see
that poses, pitch and lens put them on the boxes.

    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_rounds/*" --out data/bev_real/ --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --check
    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_rounds/*" --out data/bev_real_cal/ --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --calibrate
    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_rounds/*" --out data/bev_real_masks/ --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --calibrate --masks
      (--masks: the boxes cut out of every frame by bevnet/segment.py, as the boxes-only simulation; the full-size
       masks are cached in <out>/cache/ and an overlay figure is written to <out>/fig_REAL-masks.png)
    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_rounds/*" --out data/bev_real_cut/ --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --calibrate --cutout \
        --mask-cache data/bev_real_masks/cache
      (--cutout: the frame itself inside the mask, black elsewhere, as bevnet.data --cutout)
    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_v2/*" --best-run-per-layout --out data/bev_real_v2_masks/ \
        --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --calibrate --masks          # second campaign: one run per layout (R01, R02, ...)
    python -m bevnet.real --runs "data/survey_v2_best/*" --out data/bev_real_v2_mko/ --readings 0,1,2,3,4 --calibrate \
        --calibrate-scope same-run --masks --marker-channel --oracle-markers --mask-cache data/bev_real_v2_masks/cache
      (--oracle-markers: the detected markers plus those of the visible boxes the detector missed)
    python -m bevnet.train --eval-only --out results/bev_obst/ --tests "data/bev_real/*" --results-name real
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import math
import os
import pickle
from collections import defaultdict

import cv2
import numpy as np

from bevnet import geometry as geo
from pipeline.build_scans import best_runs

PITCH_DEG = dict(P0=11.5, P1=11.5, P3=11.5, P5=22.0)      # measured on the real frames (imgsim/render.py)
CAMERA_HEIGHT_M = 0.25                  # lens above the floor (measured 24-26 cm)
CAMERA_FORWARD_FIX_M = 0.03             # lens 15 cm ahead of the rigid body; the acquisition moved the pose by 12 cm
MARKER_CENTRE_M = 0.15                  # marker centre above the floor (faces 30 cm high)
BOX_SIDE_M = 0.235                      # face width (measured 23-24 cm)



def camera_pose(rec):
    """(x, y, yaw) of the lens: the recorded camera pose moved forward by CAMERA_FORWARD_FIX_M."""
    x, y, yaw = rec["camera_pose"]
    return (x + CAMERA_FORWARD_FIX_M * math.cos(yaw), y + CAMERA_FORWARD_FIX_M * math.sin(yaw), yaw)


def load_run(run_dir):
    """One run folder of launch_all.py: (layout id, true boxes (B, 2), frames, cameras), with
    frames[(round, reading, yaw offset)][robot] = the raw record of that frame (pose, image path, detections)
    and cameras[robot] = (camera matrix, distortion)."""
    with open(os.path.join(run_dir, "ground_truth.json")) as f:
        gt = json.load(f)
    frames = defaultdict(dict)                     # (round, reading, yaw offset) -> robot -> record
    cams = {}
    layout = None
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(run_dir, "raw", "*.jsonl"))):
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                r = json.loads(line)
                if r.get("round") is None:
                    continue
                layout = r["layout_id"]
                off = int(round(float(r["trial_id"].rsplit("/", 1)[-1])))   # --yaw-offsets-deg captures
                frames[(int(r["round"]), int(r["reading"]), off)][r["robot_id"]] = r
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(run_dir, "raw", "meta_*.json")):
        with open(path) as f:
            m = json.load(f)
        cams[m["robot_id"]] = (np.array(m["camera_matrix"], float), np.array(m["dist_coeffs"], float).ravel())
    key = layout if layout in gt else os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(run_dir))
    boxes = np.array([[b["x"], b["y"]] for b in gt[key]], np.float32)
    return layout, boxes, frames, cams


APOTHEM_M = BOX_SIDE_M / (2 * math.sqrt(3))


def angle_offsets(runs, pitch):
    """Per (layout, robot): median offsets [deg] between where the marker centres are seen (undistorted) and
    where the true box puts them (the face towards the camera, at the marker centre height), vertical and horizontal."""
    out = defaultdict(lambda: ([], []))
    for d, layout, boxes, frames, cams in runs:
        for recs in frames.values():
